en.name: São Marcos Monastery
description:
"The São Marcos (St Mark) Monastery dates back to 1441 when mass was said in a small chapel on the site. In 1452, D. Beatriz da Silva donated the chapel to the Hieronymite Friars, and extensive work was carried out under the Master, Gil de Sousa. The early structure was, however, profoundly altered in the Manueline era, with the church doorway c.1510, in the Late Gothic style, with a strong naturalistic component, being the oldest remaining part.  
Despite further alterations in the mid-16th century, the Gothic chancel and sacristy have both been conserved. This has left intact the ribbed vaulting and highly decorated key stones, both completed in 1521, the year D. Manuel I died.  
The tombs of João da Silves and Aires Gomes da Silva, dating from the same period, were the work of Diogo Pires the Younger, the leading sculptor in Coimbra in the Manueline period. Despite the Late Gothic fondness for foliate naturalism, there are already signs of Renaissance elements here. This was due to Pires’ contact with Nicolas Chanterène, who, at the same time, was carving the lovely high altar retable commissioned by Aires Gomes da Silva, one of the finest classical works in Portugal.  
Other tombs in the church are of considerable interest and artistic value, ranging from the Flamboyant Gothic of that of Fernão Teles de Meneses, to those in the Capela dos Reis Magos, dated 1572 and Mannerist in style, the last great works of the sculptor Jean of Rouen.  
  
**Lower Mondego**  
The lower course of the River Mondego from Portela, almost at the entrance to Coimbra, is characterised by an ever wider alluvial plain. After passing through the narrow lands of the Penacova valley, on reaching Ceira, the waters that rise in the Serra da Estrela are set free from the girdle of hills, and, in the winter, used to overflow the banks and flood the fertile fields of Montemor and Vila Verde.  
In recent years, with the construction of the Aguieira Dam, the flow appears to be under control and the old towns of Ereira and Maiorca are no longer regularly turned into isolated islands. The landscape remains the same, with its largely flat ricegrowing lands, although other valuable crops are also grown here.  
This agricultural land was occupied in prehistoric times, as can be seen by the remains of the hill-fort of Santa Eulália. The main towns of Montemor-o-Velho, Tentúgal and Buarcos were at one time occupied by Muslims, but were definitively taken by the Christians in 1064. This was due to the *Mozarab* D. Sesnando, who built castles, cleared land, and fixed settlements in the Lower Mondego.  
The fertility of the land attracted both institutions and individuals, such as the Monastery of Santa Cruz, the University and the Dukes of Aveiro, who owned considerable property in the area. There are still many important reminders of these periods of prosperity."

en.name: Funduq al-Zawiya
description: According to tradition, this *funduq* was built in the 12th/18th century by the Bey Husayn Ibn ‘Ali at the same time as the Zawiya of Sidi Jomni. Like the classic layout of traditional *funduq*s, this one is square; it is a two-storey building with rooms opening onto galleries that surround the courtyard. The originality of the *funduq*s of Humt Suq lies in their means of access to the upper floor, which is formed by a staircase that is situated in the courtyard, as if the architect wanted to economise on covered space to keep it for more useful requirements. This *funduq* has two staircases which face one another. All the commodity rooms are located on the ground floor: the cistern and the latrines. The ceilings are of local style, constructed as barrel vaults, except for the galleries: those on the ground floor seem to have kept their original ceilings made of palm-tree whilst those on the upper floor are made of wood. They are the result of restorations done at the beginning of the 20th century, and a more recent, badly executed work of restoration which transformed two sides of this gallery by covering it in cement flagstones. Today, the premises on the ground floor are nearly all used as storerooms for merchandise (raw or spun wool) whilst those on the upper floor are occupied by weavers. The intense liveliness and bustle which ruled there in the past, linked to commercial activities and lodging, has given way to the peacefulness of a single complementary but scaled-down activity.

es.name: Funduq el-Zawiya
description: Según la tradición, este *funduq* fue construido en el siglo XII/XVIII por el bey Hussein ibn Alí al mismo tiempo que la *zawiya* de Sidi Yomni. Según el plano clásico de los *funduq*s tradicionales éste es cuadrado; se trata de un edificio con dos plantas con habitaciones que se abren sobre galerías que rodean el patio. La originalidad de los *funduq*s de Humt Suq reside en su acceso al piso superior, a través de una escalera que parte desde el patio, como si se quisiera economizar el espacio cubierto. Este *funduq* tiene en realidad dos escaleras afrontadas. Todas las comodidades se encuentran en el piso bajo: aljibes y letrinas. Las cubiertas son de estilo local, hechas de cañón, excepto en una de las galerías; las del piso bajo parecen haber conservado su cubierta original realizada con troncos de palmera, mientras que la del piso elevado está hecha en madera, resultado de una restauración de principios de siglo. Una mala restauración más reciente ha desnaturalizado dos partes de esta galería, al cubrirla con una capa de cemento. Actualmente los locales de la parte baja sirven de almacenes de mercancías (lanas en bruto o hilada), mientras que los del piso superior están ocupados por los tejedores. La intensa animación que reina siempre alrededor de la actividad comercial y el hospedaje, ha dado paso a la calma de una sola actividad complementaria y más reducida.

fr.name: Fondouk el-Zaouïa
description: Selon la tradition, ce fondouk fut  construit au XIIe/XVIIIe par le bey Hussein  Ben Ali en même temps que la zaouïa de  Sidi Jomni. Selon le plan classique des  fondouk traditionnels, celui-ci est carré;  il s’agit en somme d’une bâtisse à deux  étages avec des pièces ouvrant sur des  galeries qui entourent la cour. L’originalité  des fondouk de Houmt Souk réside  dans l’accès à l’étage qui se fait par un  escalier qui part de la cour comme si l’on  voulait économiser l’espace couvert et le  réserver à un usage plus utile. Ce fondouk  a deux escaliers qui se font face. Toutes  les commodités se trouvent au rez-dechaussée:  citerne et latrines. Les couvertures  sont de style local faites en berceaux,  excepté pour les galeries: celle du  rez-de-chaussée semble avoir conservé sa  couverture d’origine réalisée en troncs de  palmiers tandis que celle de l’étage est en  bois. Elle provient d’une restauration du  début du siècle, une mauvaise restauration  plus récente avait dénaturé deux  côtés de cette galerie, en la couvrant  d’une dalle en béton. Aujourd’hui, les  locaux du rez-de-chaussée servent  presque tous d’entrepôts de marchandises  (laines brutes ou en filés) tandis que ceux de l’étage sont occupés par des tisserands.  L’intense animation qui y régnait autrefois,  liée à l’activité commerciale et à  l’hébergement, a cédé la place au calme  d’une monoactivité complémentaire mais  plus réduite.

en.name: Painted ceiling and Small Chapel
description:
In the first room is a painted wooden ceiling decorated with floral motifs. In the centre, a Portuguese Vessel (Nau) invokes St. Elmo, the patron saint of the Brotherhood.  
The second tempera painted ceiling is in the chapel. The Chapel is completely covered with gold-leaf carving in the “National” style, enhancing the shrines embedded in the walls, and exemplifying space management during the Baroque period. The ceiling depicts scenes from the Life of Saint Elmo.
place: Interior rooms, House of the Holy Body (Museum of Baroque)
partner: Institute for the Administration of Architectural and Archaeological Heritage -  IGESPAR

pt.name: Tectos pintados e Capela
description:
A sala de entrada está ornamentada com um tecto pintado sobre madeira, decorado com motivos florais. Ao centro, uma nau portuguesa invoca Santelmo, o santo padroeiro da Confraria.  
Na segunda sala, o tecto pintado a têmpera mostra imagens de Santelmo, entre motivos florais.  
Na capela, completamente forrada a talha dourada, ao “Estilo Nacional”, sobressaem os bustos-relicários incrustados nas paredes, os painéis de azulejos com cenas da vida de Santelmo e o pavimento de tijoleira com aplicação de azulejos de motivos florais.

en.name: Portal and façade detail
description:
Atop the three round arches of the façade are the figures of St. Engrácia, St  
Condestável and St. Isabel, according to the decree of Infanta D. Maria, whose wish was that only Portuguese saints should be depicted here.  
The portal is flanked by two Solomonic columns surmounted by a crown and coat-of-arms.
partner: Institute for the Administration of Architectural and Archaeological Heritage -  IGESPAR

pt.name: Detalhe do portal e da fachada
description:
Na fachada, sobre os três arcos, encontram-se as estátuas de *Santa Engrácia*, do *Santo Condestável* e de *Santa Isabel*, respeitando a determinação da infanta D. Maria de, na Igreja de Santa Engrácia, apenas se homenagearem santos portugueses.  
Na galilé, o portal barroco é ladeado por duas colunas salomónicas e encimado por uma coroa e pedra de armas.

ar.name: جزء من قاعدة شمعدان.
description:
القطعة عبارة عن الجزء السفلي من قاعدة شمعدان من الحجر الصابوني (Steatite). الحجر الصابوني ناعم يسهل حفره وتنفيذ الزخرفة عليه، وهذا من أهم الأسباب التي جعلته شائع الاستعمال على مر العصور بما فيها الفترة الإسلامية.  
  
قسِّم السطح الذي يتخذ شكلاً كروياً إلى ستة أشرطة أفقية بعضها ضيق وبعضها عريض. ملئت الأشرطة بأشكال هندسية مختلفة كالمعينات والمثلثات والمستطيلات، بالإضافة إلى أشكال قمعية مائلة ومتصلة مع بعضها البعض ودوائر بداخلها أشكال وردية. حُفر في الشريط الأسفل العريض صف من أربعة عقود تتدلى منها بواسطة سلاسل سُرُج تشبه السُرُج الزجاجية التي صارت شائعة في العصور الإسلامية اللاحقة. وتشبه هذه الزخارف تلك الموجودة على مجمرة عُثر عليها في الفدين.  
  
هناك أوانٍ وأدوات أخرى من الحجر الصابوني تم العثور عليها في نفس الموقع أيضاً.

قاعدة من الكوارتز، عُثر عليها في الفدين، ذات أربعة نتوءات بارزة، عائدة إلى سراج كوارتزي ضخم. إنها مُقسَّمة أفقياً إلى ست شرائح، منقوشة بأشكال مختلفة؛ الشريحة السُفلى تُصوِّر رواقاً من طراز ذي أسلوب يُميِّز المباني الإسلامية المبكرة.
place: من المرجَّح أن تكون قد صنعت في إيران أو العراق.
keywords: حجر صابوني؛ زخرفة هندسية؛ سراج؛ نحت؛ وريدة.

en.name: Steatite base.
description:
A steatite (soapstone) base with four protrusions that belonged to a large steatite lamp. The base has been mended. Being that it is soft, steatite lends itself perfectly to carved decoration; this made the stone popular throughout the ages, including the Islamic period.  
  
This hemispherical base is divided horizontally into six wide and narrow bands that are incised with various patterns. The upper band contains two six-petalled rosettes within double concentric circles, while the lower band depicts an arcade with hanging lamps, an architectural style typical of early Islamic buildings and reminiscent of the decoration on the bronze brazier also found at al-Fudayn. The narrow bands are decorated with simple geometrical patterns which include small triangles and intersecting diagonal lines which form indented squares. Other steatite vessels such as bowls and deep dishes with incised geometric patterning were found at the same site.

Steatite (soapstone) base found at al-Fudayn with four protrusions that belonged to a large steatite lamp. It is divided horizontally into six bands that are incised with various patterns; the lower band depicts an arcade in a style typical of early Islamic buildings.
keywords: Carving; geometrical decoration; lamp; rosette; steatite

es.name: Base de esteatita
description:
Base de esteatita restaurada, con cuatro salientes, que perteneció a una gran lámpara del mismo material. La esteatita es un material blando y resulta perfecta para la decoración tallada, de ahí que se haya empleado abundantemente en todas las épocas, incluida la islámica.  
Esta base semiesférica está dividida horizontalmente en seis bandas anchas y estrechas, grabadas con diversos patrones. La banda superior contiene dos rosetas de seis pétalos con círculos dobles concéntricos. La banda inferior presenta una arcada con lámparas colgantes del estilo arquitectónico típico de los inicios del Islam; este elemento también recuerda a la decoración de los braseros de bronce hallados en al-Fudayn. Las bandas estrechas están adornadas con motivos geométricos sencillos, como triángulos pequeños y líneas diagonales cruzadas formando cuadrados dentados. En el mismo lugar se hallaron otros recipientes de esteatita, como cuencos o platos hondos con motivos geométricos grabados.

Base de esteatita (jabón de sastre) con cuatro protuberancias, encontrada en al-Fudayn, que perteneció a una gran lámpara del mismo material. Está dividida horizontalmente por seis bandas grabadas con varios motivos; en la inferior hay una arcada del estilo típico de los edificios de inicios del Islam.
dates: Siglo II de la Hégira / VIII d. C.
keywords: Grabado; decoración geométrica; lámpara; roseta; esteatita.

fr.name: Base en stéatite.
description:
Base en stéatite (pierre de savon) à quatre saillies appartenant à une grande lampe sculptée dans le même matériau. Nombreuses réparations. Pierre tendre, la stéatite se prête à la décoration gravée ou sculptée, ce qui la fit longtemps apprécier, y compris pendant la période islamique.  
Cette base hémisphérique est divisée horizontalement en six bandeaux étroits ou larges, incisés de divers motifs. Le bandeau supérieur contient six rosettes à pétales entourées de deux cercles concentriques. Le bandeau inférieur reproduit une arcade sous laquelle sont suspendues des lampes, dans un style architectural typique des premières constructions islamiques et qui rappelle le décor d'un brasero en bronze également trouvé à al-Foudayn. Les bandeaux étroits sont ornés de motifs géométriques simples faits de petits triangles et de traits sécants en diagonale qui forment des carrés dentelés. D'autres objets en stéatite, dont des coupes et des plats creux à motifs géométriques incisés, ont été découverts sur le même site.

Base en stéatite (pierre de savon) trouvée à al-Foudayn, à quatre saillies, provenant d’une grande lampe du même matériau. Cette base est divisée horizontalement en six bandeaux incisés de divers motifs ; le bandeau inférieur reproduit une arcade dans un style typique des premières constructions islamiques.
dates: IIe siècle de l’Hégire (VIIIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: sculpture ; décoration géométrique ; lampe ; rosette ; stéatite

en.name: Sugar bowl
description:
Pressed glass is produced by placing a batch of hot glass in a metal mould, usually made up of several parts, and pressing the glass into this mould with a plunger. It is an invention dating back to the early 19th century. The technique used in this process makes it possible to produce glass of exactly the same shape in large numbers and to decorate the surfaces in a way that would not be possible with other techniques, or only with a great deal of work. The sharply detailed decoration, evident in this piece, could otherwise only be achieved with glass-cutting and carving techniques.  
  
The 1840 and 1841 catalogues from Launay Hautin & Cie., a company with its headquarters on the renowned Rue de Paradis in Paris, provide an invaluable resource for the identification and dating of early French examples of pressed glass. Launay Hautin distributed products from several glassworks, notably those of Baccarat and Saint-Louis. The glassware items listed in the company’s catalogues are reproduced as meticulously executed lithographs, all of which are to a consistent scale for each piece.
keywords: Red glass; pressed glass; Launay Hautin; sugar bowl

en.name: Substructions of the Temple of Aesculapius
description:
Inside the Hotel Villa Aricia, on via Appia Antica, it is possible to see still preserved substructures in *opus caementicium* leaning against the wall, with coverings in *opus reticulatum, quadratum* and *latericium*. They are thought to be the remains of the Temple of Aesculapius or of a villa of the *Atii* family, who owned the land in Roman times. (E. Lucidi).  
(Bibliography: E. Lucidi, 1796; G. R. Florescu, 1925; R. Lefevre, 1977; M. Lilli, 2002; M. Leoni, 2008)

it.name: Sostruzioni del cd. Tempio di Esculapio
description:
All’interno della proprietà dell’Hotel Villa Aricia, presso la via Appia Antica, si conservano strutture sostruttive in opera cementizia addossate alla parete, con rivestimenti in opera reticolata, opera quadrata, opera laterizia, riferite al Tempio di Esculapio o a una villa degli *Atii* (E. Lucidi).  
(Bibliografia: E. Lucidi, 1796; G. R. Florescu, 1925; R. Lefevre, 1977; M. Lilli, 2002; M. Leoni, 2008)

en.name: Four anklets
short_description: Ankle bracelets - or "anklets" - were common accessories in various regions of the ancient Middle East. They were first worn by ancient Egyptian women, and were made of materials such as brass, gold, silver, iron, glass, or ivory. The Hebrew word for "ankle chain" and "step chains" both come from the root *tsa'adh'*, meaning "to take steps; to march". The Hebrew word *e'khes*, meaning "bangle; anklet" comes from the root *akhas*, meaning "to make a tinkling sound" or "shaking bangles". Indeed, many anklets were adorned with small bells and heavier anklets would have made a loud tinkling or ringing noise as the wearer walked along. These bells were usually fashioned by placing a small pebble in hollowed silver spheres. It is possible that heavier anklets would have been designed to restrict the woman's step, thus forcing her to walk slowly in a style perceived as feminine, or to attract attention as she walked. The anklets pictured here are made of silver and are adorned with small dangling silver bells.
keywords: Decoration; Silver; Jewels; Fashion

de.name: St. Michaels-Altar (Hochaltar)
description: Der Hochaltar besticht nicht nur durch die subtile Ponderation von anspruchsvollem Säulenpomp und architektonischer Eleganz, sondern auch durch seine Skulpturen: Ein szenisches Emmausmahl vor dem Tabernakel als typologisches Exempel zur Eucharistie sowie Standfiguren der Erzengel Gabriel und Raffael, deren ironischer Dialog mit dem jeweils beigesellten Putto zu den Höhepunkten der bayerischen Rokoko-Plastik zählt. Der linke spielt die Verkündigungsmadonna, der rechte den Tobias mit dem Fisch. Im Auszug treibt ein dritter Putto Unfug mit den Waffen Michaels. Das damit in Beziehung stehende ältere Altarblatt, das den Triumph des Erzengels über Satan darstellt, gilt hingegen als Hauptwerk der Münchner Barockmalerei.
artist: Altarblatt: Andreas Wolf (1652-1716); Altar und Skulpturen: Johann Baptist Straub Johann Baptist Straub (1704-1784)

en.name: Altar of St. Michael (High Altar)
description: The high altar is impressive not only through the subtle ponderation of a demanding pomp of columns and architectural elegance, but also through its sculptures: A scenic meal of Emmaus in front of the tabernacle as a typological example of the Eucharist, as well as archangel statues of Gabriel and Raphael, whose ironic dialogue with the accompanying cherub are  counted as the highlights of Bavarian Rococo sculpture : The left one performs the Annunciation Madonna, the right one St. Tobias with the fish. In the upper storey of the altar, a third cherub is engaged in horseplay with St. Michael’s weapons. The correlating older altarpiece, which portrays the triumph of the Archangel over Satan, is considered as a major work of Munich Baroque painting.
artist: Altarpiece: Andreas Wolf (1652-1716); Altar and sculptures: Johann Baptist Straub (1704–84)
partner: University of Munich, Institute of Art History

ar.name: مسجد حسان.
description:
قرر السلطان يعقوب المنصور حال اعتلائه العرش إنشاء عاصمة جديدة، رباط الفتح، واختار موقعاً بالقرب من قصبة وادي سلا )مدينة سلا الحالية(، وأحاطها بسور ضخم، ثم شرع في بناء مسجد شاسع داخلها، كان من المتوقع أن يشكل أكبر جامع في الغرب الإسلامي، وبوسعه استيعاب جيش بكامله.  
جَنَّد المشروع قوى عاملة هائلة من بينها 700 أسير مسيحي. لكن البناء توقف بعد وفاة السلطان، وتعرضت المعلمة الغير مكتملة، خلال مراحل مختلفة، إلى تخريبات جسيمة من أعمال السلب، وإعادة استخدام موادها (الحجارة والرخام لبناء مباني أخرى والخشب لبناء القوارب) وكذلك بسبب الزلازل (ارتدادات زلزال لشبونة الذي حصل في عام 1755 وضرب المئذنة)، بالإضافة للحريق الذي تم اكتشاف آثاره عند القيام ببناء ضريح الملك محمد الخامس.  
كان الجامع يضم قاعة للصلاة تتجاوز مساحتها هكتارين ونصف، سقفها مدعوم بثلاث مائة عمود وبمائة سارية، وكذلك مئذنة يصل ارتفاعها إلى 67 متر (وأكثر من 80 متر مع القبة القنديلية العليا (العزري).  
يتخلل سورَ المعلمة الذي يبلغ طوله 183 متر وعرضه 139 متر، 12 باباً، وقسمت القاعة الواسعة الأرجاء إلى 19 بلاطة تتشكل كل واحدة منها من 21 أسكوبا.  
تشكل هذه الأعمدة استثناءا في الفن الديني الموحدي، فطرازها روماني بيزنطي، ومكونة من أسطوانات متراكبة، تعلوها تيجان تصميمها أولي.  
يصل ارتفاع المئذنة (صومعة حسان)، المطلة على وادي النهر وعلى واجهة البحر، والتي تشكل رمز مدينة الرباط ومعلمتها الأكثر شهرة، إلى 44 متر حالياً، وتبعث في النفس، بقاعدتها المربعة التي يصل ضلعها إلى 16.20 متر وسماكة جدارنها إلى 2.50 متر، انطباعاً بالقوة والعظمة. وقد بُني كل جانب من جوانبها بمداميك كبيرة من الحجر، تَغَيَّر لونها مع الزمن إلى تدرج لوني مختلف يبتدئ من اللون الرمادي المفضض إلى اللون الأحمر الأمغر الغامق. وفُتحَ كل جانب منها بفتحات أنيقة تنير الدرابزين الداخلي، الذي يمكن تسلقه على صهوة حصان. زينت هذه الأخيرة بعدة حقول من العقود الصغيرة، التي تعلوها زخارف من التشبيكات المعمارية الكلاسيكية وزخارف تنبعث من الأقواس المستندة على عواميد صغيرة من الرخام والحجارة، تعلوها تيجان يرجع مصدر البعض منها إلى الأندلس، وترقى لفترة خلافة قرطبة (القرن 4 الهجري / القرن 10 الميلادي).  
وقد تم بناء ضريح الملك محمد الخامس (1927 - 1961) بين عامي 1961 و 1969، داخل سور المسجد الكبير المختفي.

بعد بناء السياج الحائطي لعاصمته المقبلة، بدأ الخليفة يعقوب المنصور في تشييد مسجد ضخم يتكون من قاعة للصلاة تزيد مساحتها عن هكتارين، وسقف يحمله 300 عمود و 100 دعامة ومنارة يصل علوها إلى 80 متر.  
توقفت الأشغال عند وفاة السلطان؛ وتعرضت البناية إلى تخريبات هامة (زلازل وحريق وإعادة استعمال...).  
بقيت من المسجد الساحة، وجزءٌ من السياج الحائطي، والأعمدة وجزءٌ من المنارة. يبلغ ارتفاع هذه الأخيرة 44 متر، ويحملُ كل جانب من جوانبها زخرفة مختلفة، مع فتحات مزينة بعقود وشبكات من التشبيكات وأعمدة صغيرة ذات تيجان.
artist: السلطان الموحدي أبو يوسف يعقوب المنصور (حكم في الفترة 579 - 595 هجري / 1184 -1199 ميلادي).
keywords: عمارة دينية؛ جامع؛ مسجد؛ حجر؛ رخام؛ زخرفة هندسية.
partner: Ministry of Culture,Directorate of Cultural Heritage

en.name: Hasan Mosque.
description:
When Ya'qub al-Mansur acceded to the throne, he decided to create a new capital, Ribat al-Fath. He chose a site near to the *kasbah* of Wadi Sala (modern-day Salé), surrounded it with an enormous rampart and began work on a vast mosque, which was to be the largest in the Muslim West and capable of accommodating an entire army.  
Huge numbers of workers were involved in the project, including 700 Christian captives, but construction was halted with the death of the monarch and the unfinished building suffered serious damage at various different stages: plundering and re-use of materials (stone and marble for the construction of other buildings, wood for the construction of boats, etc.), earthquakes (shockwaves from the 1755 Lisbon earthquake, which knocked the top off the minaret) and fire, traces of which were discovered during the construction of the Muhammad V mausoleum.  
The mosque was to include a prayer room of more than 2.5 ha, with a roof supported by 300 columns and 100 pillars, as well as a minaret 64 m high (more than 80 m with the top lantern).  
The outer wall of the building, 183 m long and 139 m wide, would have had 12 gateways and its immense hall would have been split into 19 naves of 21 bays each.  
The columns, in a Roman Byzantine style, consisting of superimposed shafts crowned with almost shapeless capitals, are exceptional in Almohad religious art.  
Dominating the river valley and the seafront, the minaret ('the Hasan Tower'), a symbol of the town of Rabat and its most famous monument, currently rises to 44 m in height and, with its 6.20 m square base and 2.50 m thick walls, gives an impression of strength and majesty. Each of its four sides, made of roughly cut stones, has been worn to a different shade over time, from silver-grey to dark red ochre. Each side has elegant apertures that light the interior ramp, which can be negotiated on horseback. They are decorated with several layers of arcatures crowned with classical architectural knotwork, with nascent arch motifs that rest on small marble and stone columns, crowned with capitals, some of which came from al-Andalus and date from the Caliphate of Córdoba (AH 4th / AD 10th century).  
The mausoleum of King Muhammad V (1927–61) was constructed between 1961 and 1969 inside the wall of the great mosque, which is now lost.

Having completed the outer wall of his future capital, Ya'qub al-Mansur started building a magnificent mosque with a prayer room of more than 2 ha, a roof supported by 300 columns and 100 pillars, and a minaret more than 80 m high. Work stopped with the king's death and the building went on to suffer serious damage (earthquake, fire, plunder, etc.).  
The esplanade, part of the outer wall, the colonnades and part of the minaret have survived. Each side of the minaret, now rising to 44 m, is decorated differently, with its apertures adorned with arches, interlacing designs and columns with capitals.
artist: Almohad king Abu Yusuf Ya‘qub al-Mansur (AH 579–95 / AD 1184–99).
The name ‘Hasan’, which appears on the monument, could be the name of its architect, about whom we have no information.
keywords: Religious architecture; stone; marble
partner: Ministry of Culture, Directorate of Cultural Heritage

es.name: Mezquita Hasan.
description:
Al acceder al trono, Yaqub al-Mansur decidió edificar una nueva capital, Ribat al-Fath. Eligió un emplazamiento próximo a la alcazaba del *wadi* Sala (actual Salé), mandó cercarlo con una gran muralla y construir una colosal mezquita, la mayor del Occidente musulmán, con capacidad para albergar todo un ejército.  
Para este proyecto se movilizó a una ingente mano de obra, entre la que hubo 700 prisioneros cristianos; sin embargo, las obras se paralizaron a la muerte del califa y la mezquita quedó inconclusa. Varios acontecimientos contribuyeron a su completa degradación: los pillajes y la reutilización de sus materiales (piedras y mármol para la edificación de otras obras, madera para la construcción de barcos…), las ondas del seísmo de Lisboa de 1755, que decapitaron el alminar, y un incendio, cuyas huellas fueron descubiertas durante la construcción del mausoleo de Mohamed V.  
La mezquita debía poseer una sala de oración de más de dos hectáreas y media, con una techumbre sustentada por 300 columnas y 100 pilares, así como un alminar de 64 m de altura (más de 80 con la linterna).  
El recinto del santuario, de 183 m de largo por 139 de ancho, debía contar con 12 puertas y con una inmensa sala distribuida en 19 naves de 21 tramos cada una.  
Las columnas, de estilo romano bizantino, formadas por tambores superpuestos rematados con capiteles sólo esbozados, son piezas únicas del arte religioso almohade.  
Dominando el valle y frente al mar se encuentra el alminar (la “torre Hasan”), símbolo de la ciudad de Rabat y su monumento más célebre. En la actualidad se eleva hasta los 44 m, lo que, junto con su base cuadrada de 16,20 m de lado y sus muros de 2,50 m de grosor, le confiere una imagen de fuerza y majestuosidad.  
El paso del tiempo ha hecho que cada una de sus cuatro esquinas, en aparejo de piedra, haya adquirido un tono diferente, del gris plata al rojo ocre oscuro. A cada lado se abren elegantes vanos que iluminan la rampa interior, que podía subirse a caballo. Están decorados con varias arquerías coronadas por redes de entrelazados arquitectónicos clásicos, con motivos que arrancan de columnitas de mármol y piedra rematadas por capiteles; algunos de estos, procedentes de al-Andalus, datan del califato de Córdoba (siglo IV / X).  
El mausoleo del rey Mohamed V (1927-1961) se construyó entre 1961 y 1969 dentro del perímetro de la gran mezquita desaparecida.

Después de levantar la muralla de su futura capital, el monarca Yaqub al-Mansur emprendió la construcción de una grandiosa mezquita, con una sala de oración de más de 2 hectáreas, una techumbre sustentada por 300 columnas y 100 pilares, y un alminar de 80 m de altura.  
Los obras se paralizaron a su muerte y el edificio sufrió graves daños (terremoto, incendio, reutilizaciones…).  
Se conserva la explanada, trechos del muro exterior, las columnas y parte del alminar, actualmente de 44 m de altura. Cada una de las fachadas de este presenta una decoración diferente, con vanos adornados con arquerías, lacería y columnillas con capiteles.
dates: Siglo VI de la Hégira / XII d. C.
artist: El califa almohade Abu Yusuf Yaqub al-Mansur (579-595 / 1184-1199).
keywords: Arquitectura religiosa; piedra; mármol.
partner: Ministry of Culture,Directorate of Cultural Heritage

fr.name: Mosquée Hassan.
description:
Lorsque Yacoub al-Mansour monte sur le trône, il décide de créer une nouvelle capitale, Ribat al-Fath. Il choisit un site à proximité de la *casbah* de Ouadi Sala (l'actuelle Salé), l'entoure d'un énorme rempart et y entame la construction d'une gigantesque mosquée, qui devait être la plus spacieuse de l'Occident musulman et capable d'accueillir une armée tout entière.  
  
Le projet mobilisa d'énormes effectifs, dont 700 captifs chrétiens, mais la construction fut arrêtée à la mort du monarque et l'édifice inachevé subit à différentes périodes de graves dégradations : pillage et réutilisation des matériaux (pierre et marbre pour la construction d'autres bâtiments, bois pour la construction de bateaux…) ; séisme (ondes de choc du séisme de Lisbonne en 1755, qui décapitèrent le minaret) ; incendie dont les traces ont été découvertes lors de la construction du mausolée Mohamed V.  
  
La mosquée devait comporter une salle de prière de plus de deux hectares et demi, avec une toiture supportée par 300 colonnes et 100 piliers, ainsi qu'un minaret de 64 m de haut (plus de 80 m avec le lanternon supérieur).  
  
L'enceinte de l'édifice, longue de 183 m et large de 139 m, devait être percée de 12 portes et son immense salle devait s'ordonner en 19 nefs de 21 travées chacune.  
  
Les colonnes, de style romain byzantin, formées de tambours superposés surmontés de chapiteaux à peine ébauchés, constituent une exception dans l'art religieux almohade.  
  
Dominant la vallée du fleuve et le front de mer, le minaret (“la tour Hassan”), symbole de la ville de Rabat et son monument le plus célèbre, s'élève actuellement à 44 m et dégage, avec sa base carrée de 16,20 m, ses murs de 2,50 m d'épaisseur, une impression de force et de majesté. Chacun de ses quatre côtés, en pierre de gros appareil, a été patiné par le temps d'une nuance différente, allant du gris argent au rouge ocre foncé. Chaque côté est percé d'élégantes ouvertures qui éclairent la rampe intérieure que l'on pouvait gravir à cheval. Elles sont décorées de plusieurs registres d'arcatures surmontées de réseaux d'entrelacs architecturaux classiques, avec des motifs naissants d'arcs qui reposent sur des colonnettes de marbre et de pierre, surmontés de chapiteaux dont quelques-uns uns, provenant d'al-Andalus, datent du califat de Cordoue (IVe siècle H / Xe siècle J.-C.).  
  
Le mausolée du roi Mohamed V (1927-1961) a été construit entre 1961 et 1969 à l'intérieur de l'enceinte de la grande mosquée disparue.

Après l'enceinte de sa future capitale, Yacoub al-Mansour entreprit la construction d'une mosquée grandiose, avec une salle de prière de plus de 2 ha, une toiture supportée par 300 colonnes et 100 piliers, et un minaret de 80 m de haut.  
Les travaux furent arrêtés à la mort du monarque et l'édifice subit de lourds dommages (séisme, incendie, remplois…).  
Il en subsiste l'esplanade, une partie du mur d'enceinte, les colonnades et une partie du minaret. Haut de 44 m, chacun de ses côtés porte une décoration différente, avec des ouvertures ornées d'arcatures, de réseaux d'entrelacs et de colonnettes à chapiteaux.
dates: VIe siècle de l’Hégire (XIIe siècle J.-C.).
artist: Le souverain almohade Abou Youssef Yacoub al-Mansour (579-595 H / 1184-1199 J.-C.).
Le nom de “Hassan” que porte le monument pourrait être celui de son architecte, sur lequel on ne possède aucune information.
keywords: architecture religieuse; pierre; marbre
partner: Ministry of Culture,Directorate of Cultural Heritage

en.name: *Dallah* (Coffee pot), *Khamra*; preparing stage largest pot
description: This copper *dallah* goes back to a type allegedly first used in 17th-century Baghdad, and by the 19th century, there were several production centres in the Arabian peninsula. Its design cleverly reflects its functional needs. The broad base ensures stability on the fire or in the sand, whilst the large spout prevents too much coffee sediment from reaching the cup. The lid is purposely weighted to avoid it opening during the pouring process. Throughout the Near and Middle East coffee lay at the heart of social rituals and hospitality, while providing sustenance during chats, debate and political discourse in the many coffee houses in the region. In this light, the quality of the coffee served was an important indicator of both the wealth of the host and status of the guest. In continental Europe, the fashion for coffee was at its height in the 17th and 18th centuries, with coffee houses the preferred meeting places for intellectuals and artists. In Britain, meanwhile, tea soon overtook coffee in popularity, even though certain religious organisations tried to promote coffee houses for the poor in order to steer them away from public houses that primarily sold alcohol.
dates: Hegira late 13th – early 14th century / AD late 19th – early 20th century
keywords: dallah; coffee pot

ar.name: أبو اسحق إبراهيم بن محمد الفارسي الاصطخري ، كتاب صور الأقاليم
description:
إن رسالة التخطيط المسماة ترجمة المسالك والممالك كانت قد كتبت بالعربية من قبل أبو اسحق إبراهيم بن محمد الفارسي الاصطخري (تقريبا 340 هجري / 951-2 ميلادي) وهو أحد أكثر الجغرافيين شهرة. وهذه النسخة الفارسية من القرن السادس عشر سميت كتاب صور الأقاليم ويمكن أن تكون قد صنعت في القسطنطينية أو في مركز آخر للسلطة العثمانية في النصف الأول من القرن السادس عشر ولا تعطي معلومات الناسخ أي شيء عن سياق المخطوطة ما عدا نسبة العمل خطأ لنصر الدين الطوسي والذي كان فلكيا وعالم دين في القرن الثالث عشر وفي الصفحة 1a&157b هناك خاتمي طغراء عثمانية تركية بشكل لوزي باسم أحمد مظفر خان واللتين بمكن التعرف عليهما بشكل غير واضح.  
وهذا يبين أن المخطوطة لا بد أنها كانت جزءا من مجموعات عثمانية قبل أن تصل للمكتبة الوطنية النمساوية في عام 1920/30.  
ويفتتح النص بلوحة زخرفة نمطية (عنوان / سارلوح) و تتضمن رسوم لخرائط بحجم صفحة كاملة عددها 21 وهي منمنمات ملونة بشكل ناصع التي تمثل أشكال زخرفية وشخوص وعناصر لمشاهد وإن نوعية الرسوم يمكن أن تقول بانها صنعت من قبل رسام فارسي الذي هاجر لتركيا. والرسام يمكن أن يكون قد استخدم أيضا نماذج قديمة مشابهة بشكل خاص للمخطوطة من القرن الخامس عشر وربما أصلها من شيراز الموجودة في متحف توبكابي (تحت رقم B. 334 ).
dates: النصف الأول من القرن السادس عشر

en.name: Abu Ishaq Ibrahim b. Muhammad al-Farisi al-Istakhri, *Kitab Suwar al-Aqalim* (Book of Images of the Lands)
description: The cartographic treatise called “*Tarjamat al-Masalik wa al-Mamalik*” was written in Arabic by Abu Ishaq Ibrahim b. Muhammad al-Farisi al-Istakhri (c. 340 AH / 951–2 AD), one of the most famous geographers. This 16th-century Persian copy, referred to as “*Kitab Suwar al-Aqalim*” (Book of Images of the Lands), may have been made in Constantinople or in another centre of Turkish power in the first half of the 16th-century. The colophon offers no contextualising information except for an erroneous attribution of the work to Nasir ad-Din Tusi, who was an astronomer and theologist in the 13th-century. On fol. 1a and 157b, there are two almond-shaped Turkish-Ottoman *tughra* stamps, with the name of Ahmad Muzaffar Khan indistinctly recognizable. This shows that the manuscript must have been part of Ottoman collections before it came to the Austrian National Library in 1820/30. The text opens with a typical ornamental panel (*‘unwan/sarlauh*) and includes 21 full-page map illustrations. These brightly coloured miniatures represent stylised maps, occasionally showing decorative motifs, figures, and scenic elements. The quality of the depictions may suggest that they were made by a Persian painter who had emigrated to Turkey. The painter may have also used older models, particularly comparable to a 15th-century manuscript, possibly from Shiraz, in the Topkapı Sarayı (B. 334).
keywords: Cartography; Caspian Sea; geography; island; map; Mediterranean; ta'liq
materials: Ink, colour and gold on Venetian paper. Calligraphic large *ta'liq* script of 15 lines per page.

en.name: Mosque of al-Jawali
description:
The Mosque of al-Jawali shares a corridor with the Haram al-Ibrahimi and looks as though it is joined with it. From the outside the walls of the two buildings can hardly be distinguished from each other.The west wall of the al-Jawali Mosque is in fact the eastern wall of the Haram al-Ibrahimi building, while the east wall of the mosque, hewn from the rock, cannot be seen from the outside at all. The same applies to the northern and southern walls, which are also hewn from the rock. Built in 720/1320–1321 by the *amir* ‘Alam al-Din Sanjar al-Jawali, the inspector (*nadir*) of the two *haram*s of Jerusalem and Hebron, it can be reached through the Mosque’s south-east portal. The first thing one encounters after walking through the marble double door is a hall. A marble inscription stone is seen above the second of these doors, which bears the name of the founder and the date of construction. This door leads to both mosques. Some bands of Qur’anic writing are found on marble stone plaques on the façades of the two portals. The Mosque of al-Jawali can also be reached through the door situated to the northeast of the Haram al-Ibrahimi.  
The mosque consists of three aisles covered by cross vaults that are carried on gigantic stone pillars. A fine stone dome covers the centre of the mosque, whose corners are decorated by *muqarnas*. Many windows are found on the drum of the dome. On the *qibla*’s side is a *mihrab* cut into the rock and covered in coloured marble. The mosque rises above the level of the corridor leading to the Haram al-Ibrahimi, especially from the eastern side, in order to separate the women’s section from the men’s, lately the northern (rear) part of the mosque has been elevated by three steps.

es.name: Mezquita al-Yawali
description:
La mezquita al-Yawali tiene un pasillo en común con al-Haram al-Ibrahimi, al que está integrada. Desde el exterior, resulta difícil distinguir sus propios muros de los de al-Haram. Su pared oeste constituye el muro este del recinto de al-Haram, y su pared este, tallada en la roca, no puede verse desde el exterior. Lo mismo ocurre con los muros norte y sur, también construidos en la roca.  
La mezquita fue edificada en 720/1320 por el *emir* ‘Alam al-Din Sanyar al-Yawali, custodio (*nadir*) de los *haram*s de Jerusalén y de Hebrón. Se accede por el pórtico sureste, que conduce a una gran sala por un doble portal de mármol. La segunda puerta, coronada por una inscripción con el nombre del fundador y la fecha de construcción del edificio, comunica con la mezquita. En las fachadas de ambas puertas hay placas de mármol con bandas de inscripciones coránicas. El segundo acceso a la mezquita al-Yawali se realiza por la puerta situada al noroeste de al-Haram al-Ibrahimi.  
La mezquita consta de tres naves con bóvedas por arista que se apoyan en enormes pilares de piedra. En el centro de la mezquita hay una elegante cúpula de piedra, cuyas pechinas están decoradas con *muqarnas*. En el tambor de la cúpula se abre una serie de ventanas y en el eje de la *qibla* se sitúa un *mihrab* tallado en la roca y revestido de mármol de colores. La mezquita se eleva por encima del nivel del pasillo que conduce a al-Haram al-Ibrahimi, especialmente por el lado este. Posteriormente, para separar la sección de las mujeres de la de los hombres, se procedió a elevar el lado norte (el posterior) de la mezquita una altura de tres escalones.

fr.name: Mosquée al-Jawali
description:
La mosquée al-Jawali a un couloir en commun avec le Haram al-Ibrahimi, dont elle semble indissociable. De l’extérieur, il est difficile de distinguer ses propres murs de ceux du Haram. Son mur occidental constitue le mur oriental de l’édifice du Haram al-Ibrahimi, tandis que son mur oriental, taillé dans le roc, est invisible de l’extérieur. La même remarque s’applique aux murs nord et sud, eux aussi construits dans le roc. La mosquée fut construite en 720/1320 par l’émir ‘Alam al-Din Sanjar al-Jawali, gardien (*nadir*) des deux *harams* de Jérusalem et d’Hébron. On y accède par le portail sud-est, qui conduit à une grande salle par un double portail de marbre. La deuxième porte, surmontée d’une inscription précisant le nom du bâtisseur et la date de la construction, dessert la mosquée. Des bandeaux d’inscriptions coraniques se trouvent sur des plaques de marbre des façades des deux portails. Le deuxième accès à la mosquée al-Jawali se fait par la porte située au nord-ouest du Haram al-Ibrahimi.  
La mosquée présente trois nefs voûtées d’arêtes reposant sur d’énormes piliers en pierre. Une élégante coupole en pierre couvre le centre de la mosquée, dont les angles sont décorés de *mouqarnas*. Le tambour est percé d’une série de fenêtres. Dans l’axe de la *qibla*, un *mihrab* taillé dans le roc est orné de marbre de couleur. La mosquée s’élève au-dessus du niveau du corridor menant au Haram al-Ibrahimi, notamment du côté est; ultérieurement, de façon à séparer la section des femmes de la section des hommes, la partie nord (la partie arrière) de la mosquée a été surélevée de trois marches.

en.name: *Peace on Earth* (*The Four Human Temperaments*)
description: The ceiling of the vestibule shows the Four Human Temperaments – *collerico*, *sanguigno*, *flemmatico*, *malinconico* – sitting on the terrestrial globe, seen against the light and alludes to earthly harmony; the allegories of the Four elements – fire, water, earth and air – are painted in the pendentives. The hardy scorcio and the energetic figures sitting on the terrestrial globe give the impression of a vast space, amplified by the light and its movement against the airy background of the sky. The light creates a deep illusive depth in part because of the star architectural frame.
partner: Musei Civici d’Arte Antica di Bologna in cooperation with the Province of Bologna

it.name: *La Concordia sulla terra* (*I quattro temperamenti*)
description: L'affresco, nella volta della sala di accesso, mostra i quattro temperamenti dell'uomo – *collerico*, *sanguigno*, *flemmatico*, *malinconico* – adagiati sul globo terrestre visto in controluce, alludendo alla Concordia terrena. Le allegorie dei quattro elementi corrispondenti – fuoco, acqua, terra e aria – sono rappresentate nei pennacchi. Gli arditi scorci, insieme all'energia delle figure e alla volumetria della superficie terrestre su cui queste poggiano, contribuiscono ad accentuare il senso dell'amplificazione spaziale, affidato alla luce e al suo irradiarsi sullo sfondo arioso del cielo. Essa  contribuisce a creare un particolare senso di profondità spaziale illusoria anche attraverso il risalto che conferisce alla singolare invenzione della cornice architettonica, che nel gioco delle sporgenze e delle rientranze crea tutt'intorno alla base dell'affresco un originale motivo a stella.
place: Biblioteca, S. Michele in Bosco, Bologna

en.name: Clashes between agricultural labourers on strike and the mounted police in Cerignola (Foggia, Apulia, in southern Italy)
names: *I gravi disordini a Cerignola (Foggia): la polizia disperde i contadini rivoltosi*
short_description:
Agricultural workers were at the forefront of Italian labour movement. In 1901, they created the National Federation of Agricultural Workers (Federazione nazionale dei lavoratori della terra).  
In 1904, at Cerignola, the police violently repressed a protest of agricultural workers, killing 4 and injuring 40.
holder: State Library of Modern and Contemporary History
partner: MIBACT | State Library of Modern and Contemporary History

ar.name: نقش ديار بكر.
description:
القطعة عبارة عن لوح رخامي يحوي نقشاً غائراً كتب بالخط الكوفي البسيط. ثبّت اللوح في إحدى الدارين اللتين كانتا قائمتين عند باب حطة، أحد بوابات الحرم الشريف الواقعة في الجدار الشمالي للحرم. ويتحدث النص عن وقف بيتين على الزوار (الحجاج) من ديار بكر الذين كانوا يحضرون إلى القدس بعد عودتهم من الحج إلى مكة المكرمة. وكان هؤلاء الحجاج يقيمون في هذين البيتين أثناء تواجدهم في مدينة القدس. وقد وقف البيتين حاكم ديار بكر في تلك الفترة، أبو النصر ناصر الدولة أحمد بن مروان. ونص النقش كما يلي:  
"\[بسم\] الله الرحمن الرحيم هذا ما وقف وحبس الامير السيد الاجل  
\[…\] الدولة وعمادها ذو الصرامير\[؟\] ابا نصر احمد ابن مرو\[ان\]  
\[احسن\] الله ثوابه واحسن ما به بهاتين الدارين المتلاصقتين  
\[و\]حدودهما وحقوقهما على جميع الواردين من ديار بكر على ما  
\[ذكر\] في كتاب وقفهما فمن غيره او بدله فعليه لعنة الله وذلك  
\[بتاريخ\] رمضان سنة خمس واربعين واربعماية اثابه الله."

نقش غائر، محفور على لوح رخامي، بالخط الكوفي البسيط. والنص عبارة عن وقفية لدارين، وُقفتا على حجاج ديار بكر، الذين ينزلون القدس من أجل تقديس حجتهم، بعد عودتهم من الحج إلى مكة المكرمة، وكان هؤلاء الحُجّاج يقيمون في هذين البيتين أثناء تواجدهم في القدس، وقد أوقف البيتين حاكم ديار بكر "أبو النصر أحمد بن مروان".
dynasty: المروانيون (حكموا في ديار بكر في الفترة 372 – 478 / 983 – 1085)
keywords: حفر غائر؛ خط كوفي؛ ديار بكر؛ رخام؛ نقش.

en.name: Waqf inscription panel from Diyar Bakr.
description:
A marble panel that contains an engraved inscription written in simple *kufic* script. The panel was affixed to a wall in one of the two houses located at Bab al-Hitta, a gate located in the northern wall of the Haram al-Sharif. The inscription mentions the *waqf* that related to the houses that were donated for the benefit of pilgrims travelling from the Hajj in Mecca, who might pass through Jerusalem on their journey back to Diyar Bakr. The pilgrims would reside in one of the houses during their stop-off in Jerusalem. The houses were endowed by the ruler of Diyar Bakr, Abu al-Nasr Nasir al-Daula Ahmad bin Marwan al-Diyar Bakri. The inscription, starting with the *Basmala*, reads as follows:  
“In the Name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. This is what has been endowed and made into a religious bequest by Amir al-Sayyad al-Ajal \[…\] al Daula and its support Dhu Saramir \[?\], the father of Nasr Ahmad Ibn Marwan. May God reward his good deeds and bless these two adjoining houses, their delimitations, and their rights for all who come from Diyar Bakr as is (mentioned) in the book and the endowment, and those who change it or replace it, may the curse of God be upon them. This is on the \[date\] Ramadan, in the year 445.”

This is a high relief inscription on a marble panel written in a simple *kufic* script. The text describes the *waqf* (endowment) for two buildings given for pilgrims from Diyar Bakr to lodge in Jerusalem after their return from the Hajj to Mecca. The two houses were endowed by the governor of Diyar Bakir, Abu al-Nasr Ahmad bin Marwan.
holder: Islamic Museum, al-Aqsa Mosque / al-Haram al-Sharif.
keywords: Low relief; kufic script; Diyar Bakr; marble; inscription

es.name: Lápida con inscripción de *waqf* de Diyar Bakr.
description:
Lápida de mármol con inscripción en bajorrelieve, escrita en letra cúfica sencilla. Colgaba de una pared de una de las dos casas de Bab al-Hitta, una puerta del muro septentrional del Haram al-Sharif. En la inscripción se alude a un *waqf* relacionado con estas casas, que fueron donadas por Abu al-Nasr Nasir al-Dawla Ahmad ibn Marwan al-Diyar Bakri, gobernante de Diyar Bakr, para que se alojaran en ellas los peregrinos a su paso por Jerusalén en el camino de vuelta a Diyar Bakr tras el *hayy* a La Meca. La inscripción comienza con la *basmala* y dice así:  
”En el nombre de Dios, el misericordioso, el compasivo. Esto ha sido donado como ofrenda religiosa por el emir al-Sayyad al-Ayal \[…\] al-Dawla y su sostén Du Saramir \[?\], padre de Nasr Ahmad ibn Marwan. Que Dios recompense sus buenas acciones y bendiga estas dos casas, sus límites y los derechos de todos los que vienen de Diyar Bakr, tal y como se menciona en el libro y la donación, y que Dios maldiga a aquellos que lo cambien o lo sustituyan. En ramadán del año 445”.

Lápida de mármol con una inscripción en altorrelieve escrita en letra cúfica sencilla. El texto habla del *waqf* (donación) de dos edificios para se alojaran en ellos los peregrinos de Diyar Bakr a su vuelta del *hayy* a La Meca. El gobernador de Diyar Bakr, Abu al-Nasr Ahmad ibn Marwan, donó estas dos casas.
keywords: Bajo relieve; escritura cúfica; Diyar Bakr; mármol; inscripción.
partner: Museo islámico en la mezquita de Al-Aqsa

fr.name: Panneau d’inscriptions du *waqf* de Diyar Bakr.
description: Panneau en marbre à inscription gravée rédigée en écriture coufique simple. Il était fixé au mur de l'une des deux maisons de Bab al-Hitta, près de la porte de la muraille nord du Haram al-Charif, citées par le texte. Celui-ci mentionne le *waqf* concernant ces deux maisons offertes pour servir de pension aux pèlerins de Diyar Bakr (Diyarbakir) de retour de La Mecque en passant par Jérusalem, par le souverain de Diyar Bakr, Abou al-Nasr Nasir al-Daoula Ahmad bin Marwan al-Diyar Bakri. L'inscription, qui débute par une *basmala*, se lit ainsi : “Au Nom de Dieu, le Clément, le Miséricordieux. Ceci est ce qui a été donné en legs religieux par Amir al Sayyad al-Adjal \[…\] al Daoula et son soutien Dhou Saramir \[?\], père de Nasr Ahmad Ibn Marwan. Que Dieu le récompense de cette bonne action et bénisse ces deux maisons adjacentes, leurs limites, et leurs droits à tous ceux qui viennent de Diyar Bakr comme il est (mentionné) dans le livre et la charte et que la malédiction de Dieu retombe sur ceux qui le changent ou qui le remplacent. Ceci le \[date\] de *ramadan* en l'an 445.”

Panneau en marbre à inscription gravée rédigée en écriture coufique simple. Le texte décrit la donation (*waqf*) consentie par le gouverneur de Diyar Bakr, Abou al-Nasr Ahmad bin Marwan, de deux maisons destinées à héberger, à Jérusalem, les pèlerins de retour de La Mecque.
holder: Musée islamique, mosquée al-Aqsa / Haram al-Charif.
keywords: gravure ; écriture coufique ; Diyar Bakr ; inscriptions ; marbre

en.name: God Is Sublime
description: In his practice, Haji Noor Deen employs, develops and further interprets Sini calligraphy. The Sini style, which emerged in the 14th century AD, fuses Chinese and Arabic calligraphic traditions. Born in 1963 in Shangdong province, China, Haji Noor Deen graduated from Egypt Sadat Calligraphy School and obtained his calligraphy *ijaza* in Istanbul. This scroll is made of patterned dark red silk with mounted calligraphy on paper. The almost opaque Arabic calligraphy in black ink has been executed in broad brushs trokes. The title of the work appears in black ink on the left, above two red seals. A third red seal appears on the top right.
materials: Ink and red seal colour on rice paper, mounted on silk

en.name: Hemispherical cup on trumpet foot
description:
The hemispherical cup resting on a trumpet-shaped foot belongs to a typology that developed in Iran between the late 12th and early 13th centuries, also spreading to the Syro-Mesopotamian area.  
The outer wall is engraved with apical medallions decorated with arabesques and rosettes with geometric motifs and stylized flowers.  
The upper rim of the cup features an inscription characterized by rods ending in human heads, while the lower part of the letters features recognizable animal heads, including birds, which are also found in the interstices on the swirled base.  
The animated inscriptions are typical of Khorasan metalwork and are reflected in the ornithomorphic inscriptions on ceramics from the Samanid period.  
The auspicious inscription on the rim reads: "Everlasting glory, healthy life, complete prosperity, full success, increasing fortune, favorable destiny, eternal delight, happiness, health, favor, generosity, peace, intercession... long life to the owner." The inscription on the body reads "for Khalīf son of al-Jūlakī (?).  
The cup was probably used to hold beverages and drinking water, which was traditionally stored in large clay jars that preserved its freshness and were covered with cloth, palm branches, or other leaves.
holder: Museo e Real Bosco di Capodimonte

en.name: Volkswagen Kübelwagen
description:
The genesis of Volkswagen was with the KdF-Wagen (“Strength Through Joy vehicle”) launched in 1938 by the German government. After World War II, this model became known as the “Beetle”. In parallel, two military models were built with the capacity to face inaccessible terrain. Such was the versatility of not only this small car but also the Volkswagen engineers and the brand itself.  
  
With the outbreak of World War II, the popular KdF-Wagen was adapted by Ferdinand Porsche to meet the needs of the German army. Out of that came two all-terrain vehicles that stake their claim in history as Volkswagen’s first: the Kübelwagen and the Schwimmwagen.  
  
Using the KdF-Wagen’s four-cylinder engine along with the chassis and torsion bar suspension, the Kübelwagen was developed by Ferdinand Porsche for tactical support and military transport purposes. It was widely used in combat by German forces in North Africa and the campaign on the Russian front.  
  
Although it was known internally as Type 82, it quickly gained the nickname *kübel-wagen*, or the “Bucket Car,” because of its shape.  
  
Even without the four-wheel drive of its Jeep opponent, the Kübelwagen used the excellent traction of the KdF-Wagen chassis and drive to move over rough terrain, while the inverted wedge shape of its bodywork and tall ride height allowed it to pass unscathed over the most difficult routes.

en.name: Hijaz Railway gold medal
description: Medals offered to those who had provided a personal charitable donation to the Railway endeavour displayed a locomotive (with the common 2-6-0 wheel configuration) within a laurel wreath. Above the locomotive was the tughra of Sultan Abdülhamid II and beneath it the Hijri date. On the reverse side, an inscription described the award as ‘The Hamidiyah Hijaz Railway for Enthusiastic Service’. The medals were made of different metals which were composed in accordance to the amount of the donation. They were generally presented with a red or green ribbon and accompanied by an official firman. The gold medal was given to the highest donors and was therefore rarer than the other types (silver or cupro-nickel). Firmans without medals could also be awarded for smaller contributions, which gave even the poorest of donors formal recognition of their piety. The religious aspect of the venture was reinforced by the almost complete lack of financial corruption in its financial administration. At a time when the abuse of official position was commonplace throughout the empire, it was a remarkable and indeed unifying feature of the project that the running of its affairs was carried out with virtually no reports of misappropriation.
holder: Khalili Family Trust – Hajj and the Arts of Pilgrimage Collection
place: Khalili Family Trust – Hajj and the Arts of Pilgrimage Collection

en.name: Incense burner
description: Incense burners like this are usually made of clay mixed with water and kneaded until a mixture is formed that can then be shaped. The burner is then adorned with engravings, intricate drawings, and different colors. The incense burners are then fired in a kiln, after which they are ready for use. Note the handle; it makes the burner safe to carry from room to room. Incense occupies a central place in Omani life, as the passing of a fragrant burner at the end of a visit is customary in every region of the country.
holder: The national Museum - Sultanate of Oman

cs.name: Sv. Řehoř
description: Podstatnou složkou výmalby kostela je iluzivní architektura a dekorace, která tvoří také pozadí jednoho z církevních otců ve cviklech klenby. V postavě svého jmenovce spatřujeme portrét donátora kostela, uměnímilovného opata louckého kláštera Řehoře Lambecka. Na malbách církevních otců, proroků a evangelistů se podílel Maulbertschův žák a nejbližší spolupracovník J. Winterhalder ml.
artist: Franz Anton Maulbertsch (1724 Langenargen am Bodensee – 1796 Vídeň), – Josef Winterhalder ml. (1743 Vöhrenbach – 1807 Znojmo)

en.name: St. Gregory
description: Illusionary architecture and ornamentation make up a major part of the church decoration. They also provide a background for one of the Church Fathers in a vault joint. St. Gregory is a crypto-portrait of his namesake, Řehoř Lambeck, a benefactor of the church and art-loving abbot of Louka Monastery. J. Winterhalder Jr., a pupil and close associate of Maulbertsch, participated in the painting of the Church Fathers, Prophets and Evangelists.
place: Pilgrimage Church of the Scourged Saviour, Dyje, detail of the Fresco
artist: Franz Anton Maulbertsch (1724 Langenargen am Bodensee – 1796 Vienna) – Josef Winterhalder Jr. (1743 Vöhrenbach – 1807 Znojmo)

en.name: Limestone gravemarker
description: This gravestone shows a shallow niche topped by a *muqarnas* design. Within, a worn cursive inscription gives the name of the deceased, Mahmud ibn Muhammad. Above, the upper part of the panel contains verse 26 of *sura Al-Rahman* from the Holy Qur’an. A date appears to the left of the niche: ‘In \[the month of \] Muharram 809’.

ar.name: زخرفة غطاء للرأس
description: القطعة عبارة عن زخرفة لغطاء للرأس مع بورتريه لفتح علي شاه ( 1797 -1834) في مينا مطلي. ويأخذ شكلها نصف قمر مجموع مع شمس مرتفعة / مشرقة التي كانت شعار الحكم للدولة الفارسية التي أسست من قبل شاه في عام 1807. والتاج الإمبراطوري المرصع بالمجوهرات يشير للوحات زيتية لاحقة له منذ السنوات الأولى لحكمه حيث كانت ترسم بورتريهات له في التوربان الملكي التقليدي الذي يعلوه حلية للرأس.
