fr.name: Qasr al-Khayr al-Gharbi.
description:
Qasr al-Khayr al-Gharbi est un complexe palatial omeyyade en plein désert. Il regroupe un barrage, un système de canalisations souterraines, un lac, un moulin, un *khan*, un hammam et la résidence palatiale. Les califes omeyyades, en particulier Hicham bin Abd al-Malik, se flattaient de pouvoir transformer le désert en jardins luxuriants pour mener une vie de cour et de plaisirs, consacrée en particulier à la chasse.  
Le barrage, dit de Kharbaqa, se trouve à 16 km au sud-ouest du palais. Ses eaux sont distribuées via une canalisation souterraine qui le relie au palais et aux autres installations du site. Le jardin est un rectangle clos de mur de 1050 x 442 m qui comprend encore des vestiges de la canalisation le long des restes du logement des gardiens. Le *kahn* (Kahn al-Milh), situé à 10 km au nord-ouest du palais, est en forme de biseau. Il mesure environ 55 m de long. Ses murs en briques de terre posées sur un socle de maçonnerie entourent une cour centrale. Le hammam, également au nord-ouest, comprend deux parties : le *frigidarium* de quatre pièces dont l'une dotée d'un *mihrab* et le *caldarium* de trois pièces, au-dessus de la chaufferie.  
Le palais proprement dit présente une façade extérieure évoquant un fort, mais dont les éléments défensifs sont en réalité purement décoratifs. Il est de forme carrée, de 70 m de côté environ. Ses murs sont en calcaire scié sur une hauteur de 2 m environ puis se poursuivent en brique crue. À trois des angles extérieurs s'élève une tour ronde, celle de l'angle nord-ouest étant carrée et datée du VIe siècle (Byzance). Entre chaque angle se dresse une paire de tours semi-rondes. Sur l'enceinte orientale, ces deux tours sont plus espacées pour encadrer l'entrée principale ornée d'une abondante décoration de stuc à motifs sculptés floraux et architectoniques, importants merlons en partie supérieure, et fenêtres étroites qui font penser à des archères. Dans les années 1940, cette façade d'entrée monumentale a été transférée au Musée national de Damas dont elle constitue aujourd'hui l'entrée.  
L'entrée franchie, un corridor conduit à un portique sous toiture entourant une vaste cour centrale carrée entourée de bâtiments sur deux niveaux, probablement de plan identique. On a retrouvé des preuves de l'existence de deux escaliers. Ces deux niveaux sont divisés en six sections indépendantes, chacune comprenant plusieurs pièces, un hall et des toilettes. Au-dessus de l'entrée de chacune de ces sections figurent des fenêtres en arc décorées de stuc ajouré qui laissent passer à la fois l'air et la lumière. Des peintures, des sculptures et de splendides statues ornaient cet intérieur, dont beaucoup appartiennent aujourd'hui aux collections du Musée national de Damas. Malgré ce décor prestigieux et l'utilisation intelligente de l'environnement, la rareté des fragments de céramique et de verre sur le site confirme la brièveté de l'occupation omeyyade. Sous les Ayyoubides et les Mamelouks, le palais fut utilisé par les armées avant d'être finalement abandonné lors de l'invasion mongole du VIIe siècle H (XIIIe siècle J.-C.).

Dans la quantité de peintures et de stucs sculptés découverts dans ce complexe palatial omeyyade se trouvent certains des meilleurs exemples du syncrétisme de l'art préislamique, en particulier dans le contexte de la vie de cour. L'ensemble a été construit par Hicham ibn Abd al-Malik sous forme de vastes enceintes renforcées de tours semi-circulaires, à l'exception de l'angle nord-ouest où se dresse une tour de guet byzantine rectangulaire. Ce complexe est daté de 109 H / 727 J.-C. par une inscription figurant sur un linteau de porte près du *khan*.
artist: Hicham ibn Abd al-Malik (r. 105-125 H / 723-742 J.-C.).
Thabit ibn Thabit, qui supervisa la construction du khan al-Milh.

short_description: A colossal statue of Cypriot Bes was found near the agora of the ancient city of Amathus in 1863. The British government attempted to obtain it for the British Museum but it was sent to Constantinople on order of the Porte. This illustrates the beginnings of a more official policy to claim antiquities for the Ottoman state and to exhibit them in museums. The first Ottoman Law on antiquities was passed in 1869, followed by a more detailed one in 1874.
keywords: museums

en.name: Jade pendant
description: This jade plaque once belonged the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan (r. AH 1037-68/ AD 1628-58). It is inscribed on the front and back with verses from the Qur'an, a scrolling floral design, and two dates: AH 1041 (corresponding to AD 1631-32); and the regnal year 4 (also corresponding to AD 1631-32). The plaque was probably an amulet, based on the selection of Quranic verses and date, which follows the death of his wife, Mumtaz Mahal, suggesting that it was made to help him through this time of grief.

en.name: Saracen Bridge
description: A few meters from the mouth of the stream of San Michele, near the homonymous Norman church (also known with the title of Santa Maria di Campogrosso) there is a small bridge of modest dimensions and only one arch, called “Ponte Saraceno” (Saracen Bridge), dating from the Norman period. The masonry structure of its base is still visible, intact, together with the pointed arch, the level of the crossing having disappeared. The old road from Termini to Palermo passed over this bridge, the ramp of which still retains some traces of cobbled paving.

es.name: Puente Sarraceno
description: A pocos metros de la desembocadura del torrente San Michele, en las cercanías de la homónima iglesia normanda (conocida también con el título de Santa María de Campogrosso), se alza un puente de modestas dimensiones y una única arcada, llamado Puente Sarraceno, que puede datarse en el periodo normando. Aunque desaparecido el plano de la calzada, la estructura mural del basamento se presenta todavía intacta, lo mismo que el arco apuntado. Sobre este puente, cuya rampa conserva restos de pavimentación, pasaba la única carretera que unía Termini con Palermo.

ar.name: طبق
description: يمكن أن يكون الطبق هذا جزءا من مجموعة أدوات المائدة أو من مبخرة. وهو مزين بحرفية بنموذج حفر ومطعّم بالمعادن النفيسة،وتتحدث القطعة لنا باستخدام الرموز الإيرانية الأساسية للرياسة والسعادة.وفي الوسط توجد الشمس والتي تشع ضوءا يمنح الحياة. وحولها وبين بتلات الوردة الصغيرة هناك ستة أزواج من الطيور وكل زوج يجثم على طرف مقابل من الوعاء. ويوجد طائران يشربان من الوعاء أو الخزان وهو رمز قديم من غرب آسيا للجنة وخلود الروح.وكذلك يوجد عبارات تهنئة مكتوبة بخط النقش على الجدران الخارجية وهي دنيوية جدا: "" المجد المديد ، الحياة الرغيدة ، النجاح العظيم ، علو المقام"" ومثل هذه الأمنيات كانت معهودة في ذلك الوقت وبالتالي يمكن معرفتها بسهولة بغض النظر عن الخلفية التعليمية للقارئ.وإن النموذج بشكل Z للخلفية ينبئ أن الطبق يمكن أن يكون أصله من الجزء الغربي من إيران.

en.name: Plate
description: The plate could be part of a tableware set or an incense burner. Decorated with a masterful engraving pattern and inlaid with precious metals, the object speaks to us using key Iranian symbols of lordship and happiness. In the centre is the Sun, which radiates life-giving light. Around, between the petals of the rosette, there are six pairs of birds, each pair sitting on opposite sides of a bowl. Two birds drinking from a bowl or fountain is an ancient Western Asian symbol of Paradise and immortality of a soul. Yet the Arabic blessings inscribed in *naskh* on the exterior walls are very "earthly": "Long glory, prosperous life, great success, growth of majesty". Such wishes were typical at the time, thus easily recognizable regardless of the level of education of the reader. The Z-shaped pattern of the background suggests that the plate could originate in the western part of Iran.
keywords: Metalwork; Plate; Copper alloy; gold and silver inlay; Iran
materials: Copper alloy (bronze); cast, engraved, inlaid with gold and silver

en.name: Arraiolos rug
description: During the 17th century, oriental carpets were an important source of inspiration for production in Arraiolos. However, throughout the 18th century, the impact of Eastern patterns would gradually fade from Portuguese carpets. This rug is a good example of such a process. A highlight of the old Arraiolos production, it is wool-embroidered, in small stitches, onto burlap, with the outlines of the motifs featuring stem-stitch, characteristic of early Arraiolos rugs. Its rich chromatic scheme varies from yellow to deep blue and includes red, green and black. It is decorated with the so-called “animal pattern”, itself quite representative of that industry’s tendencies during the first half of the 18th century. In this pattern both animal figuration of erudite and popular inspiration and floral motifs abound. Both in the field, with its central medallion, and on the border, birds, quadrupeds and mythological animals are combined with winding vegetation and flower vases. These still denote the influence of other oriental textiles besides carpets, namely the *colchas* (coverlets), made in India since the middle of the 16th century for the Portuguese market.
holder: Museum of Portuguese Decorative Arts – Ricardo do Espírito Santo Silva Foundation

ar.name: مكيال زكاة (مُدّ).
description:
يتكون هذا المكيال الخاص بالزكاة ذو الشكل المخروطي من ثلاثة أجزاء ملتحمة. تتوزّع الزخرفة على ثلاثة أشرطة. يحتوي الشريط العلوي على بداية نقيشة كتابية بأحرف مغربيّة تشير إلى أنّ القطعة قد تمّ صنعها بناء على أمرٍ من السلطان أبي الحسن، وإلى وظيفة القطعة. أُثث الفراغ الذي تركته الكتابة بسعفات مزدوجة؛ وزُين الشريط الأوسط بأربعة قويسات زخرفيّة؛ يحتوي كل واحد منها على نقيشة كتابية بأحرف مغربيّة تتمّم النقيشة الموجودة على القويس الزخرفي الذي يسبقه؛ وتكمل إحداهم كتابة الشريط العلوي. تقدّم هذه النقائش الكتابيّة الأربعة معلومات عن نسب الحاكم الذي ينحدر من الرسول محمّد صلى الله عليه وسلم، ومعلومات عن أصل المعايرة (عيار المعدن). زُخرفت المساحة الواقعة بين القويسات بسعفات مزدوجة وبزهيرات. وزُين الشريط السفلي بخطّين منحنيين مجدولين. يحمل هذا المكيال الخاص بالزكاة مشبكا تعلق به سلسلة مكونة من كُلاب على شكل غصنيّة، يتخذ طرفاها هيئة سعفات مزدوجة ويرتبطان بحلقتين.  
كان هذا المعيار لقياس زكاة عيد الفطر (زكاة انتهاء صيام شهر رمضان)، المستخدم أيضاً لقياس مختلف أنواع الحبوب، يستعمل في التبادلات التجاريّة.
مكيال خاص بالزكاة يحمل زخرفة موزعة على ثلاثة أشرطة؛ تندمج داخلها نقيشة كتابية بأحرف مغربية؛ تمت الإشارة ضمنها إلى الحاكم ووظيفة القطعة التي كانت تستعمل لوزن زكاة الفطر أو للمعاملات التجارية.
dates: مابين عام 731 و 749 هجري / 1331 و 1348 ميلادي.

en.name: Measuring instrument (*mudd*).
description:
This measuring instrument, shaped like a trunk, consists of three welded pieces. The decoration is featured along three bands. The upper band holds the beginning of an inscription written in Maghrebi characters, which indicates that the object was made under the orders of the sovereign, Abu al-Hasan, as well as indicating its function. The space left empty by the writing is decorated with double palms. The middle band is adorned with four arches; each holds an inscription in Maghrebi characters that completes the preceding one; and one of these completes the inscription on the upper band. These four inscriptions offer information on both the genealogy of the sovereign and the calibration's origin, which goes as far back as the Prophet Muhammad. The space between the arches is decorated with double palms and floral ornaments. The lower band is decorated with two curving interlacing lines. This measuring instrument features a slit-pin to which a chain is attached made of foliage hooks at either end of which are double-palm shapes that are linked to two rings.  
This measuring weight of the *zakat al-fitr* (alms of the breaking of the *Ramadan* fast), used to weigh out the various cereals, was also used in commercial transactions.

Alms-measure divided into three decorative sections including an inscription in Maghrebi characters mentioning the sovereign and the purpose of the object: to measure the *zakat al-fitr* (religious alms) or commercial transactions.
holder: National Museum of Antiquities and Islamic Arts
keywords: Measuring instrument; mudd; epigraphy; copper; floral decoration; Marinid; zakat al-fitr; fasting; Lettering; floral adornments; abstaining; gauging tool
partner: National Museum of Antiquities and Islamic Art

es.name: Medida de limosna *(mudd)*.
description:
Esta medida de limosna de forma troncocónica está compuesta por tres partes soldadas. La decoración se distribuye en tres franjas. La superior comprende el comienzo de una inscripción en letra magrebí que informa de la función del objeto y de que fue fabricado por orden del soberano Abu al-Hasan. Los espacios entre las letras están rellenados de dobles palmetas. La franja mediana, la más ancha, está decorada con cuatro arcos, cada uno con una inscripción en caracteres magrebíes que continúa la anterior, y una de ellas completa la inscripción de la banda superior. Estas cuatro inscripciones proporcionan información sobre la genealogía del soberano y el origen de la medida, que se remonta a la época del profeta Muhammad. Entre los arcos hay una decoración de palmetas dobles y florones. La franja inferior está adornada con dos líneas curvas entrelazadas. La medida de limosna lleva una clavija de la que cuelga una cadena formada por dos anillas y, entre ellas, un gancho en S cuyos extremos adoptan la forma de palmetas dobles.  
Este patrón de medida de la *zakat al-fitr* (limosna al final del mes de ramadán), utilizado igualmente para medir cereales, servía también en las transacciones comerciales.

Medida de limosna cuya decoración incluye una inscripción en letra magrebí, distribuida en tres franjas. Se hace referencia al soberano y a la función del objeto, que se utilizaba para medir la *zakat al-fitr* (limosna que se da al final del mes de ramadán) o en transacciones comerciales.
holder: Museo Nacional de Antigüedades y Arte Islámico
dates: Entre 731 y 749 de la Hégira / 1331-1348 d. C.
keywords: medida; mudd; epigrafía; cobre; decoración floral; meriníes; zakat al-fitr; limosna; ayuno
partner: Museo Nacional de Antigüedades y de Arte Islámico

fr.name: Mesure d’aumône (mudd).
description:
Cette mesure d'aumône de forme tronconique est composée de trois parties soudées. Le décor se répartit sur trois bandeaux. Le bandeau supérieur comporte le début d'une inscription en caractères maghrébins, qui indique que l'objet a été fabriqué sur l'ordre du souverain, Abou al-Hassan, et la fonction de l'objet. Le vide laissé par l'écriture est meublé de doubles palmes. Le bandeau médian est décoré de quatre arcatures ; chacune contient une inscription en caractères maghrébins, qui complète celle de la précédente ; une d'entre elles complète l'inscription du bandeau supérieur. Ces quatre inscriptions donnent des informations sur la généalogie du souverain et l'origine du calibrage, qui remonte au prophète Muhammad. L'espace entre les arcatures est décoré de doubles palmes et de fleurons. Le bandeau inférieur est orné de deux lignes courbes entrelacées. Cette mesure d'aumône porte une goupille à laquelle se rattache une chaîne constituée d'un crochet en rinceau dont les deux extrémités prennent la forme de doubles palmes et sont reliées à deux anneaux.  
  
Cet étalon de mesure de la *zakat al-fitr* (aumône de rupture du jeûne du *ramadan*), également utilisé pour mesurer les différentes céréales, servait aussi dans les transactions commerciales.

Mesure d'aumône portant, réparti sur trois registres, un décor dans lequel s'insère une inscription en caractères maghrébins. Il y est fait référence au souverain et à la fonction de l'objet, qui servait à mesurer la *zakat al-fitr*, l'aumône religieuse, ou des transactions commerciales.
holder: Musée national des antiquités et des arts islamiques
keywords: mesure ; mudd ; épigraphie ; cuivre ; décoration florale ; Mérinides ; zakat al-fitr ; aumône ; jeûne
partner: Le Musée national des antiquités et d’art musulman

en.name: Wall hanging with scenes from the *Tale of Tristan and Iseult* (2 fragments)
description:
The frieze in the bottom section of this wall hanging depicts the tragic love story of Tristan and Iseult (alternatively Isolde). A short introductory text and banners with caption complete the visual narrative. The story begins with the wedding of Tristan’s parents and his birth. This is followed by the young hero's first deeds at the behest of his uncle, King Mark of Cornwall, and his subsequent journey to Ireland to propose to princess Iseult for his uncle. The last part of the tale, depicting their return to Cornwall, the wedding of Iseult and Mark, and the tragic ending of Tristan and Iseult, is missing, due to the fragmentary condition of the hanging.  
The décor in the upper section of the hanging is inspired by ornaments of oriental carpets, which were commonly used as tablecloths during the 16th century. These precious predecessors were either knotted or woven. In the Upper-Rhenish region, this type of design was achieved by embroidering the textile. This hanging was presumably produced in 1539 in Strasbourg, which is evident in the date on the cartouche as well as the coats of arms of four Strasbourgian families. It was rediscovered in 1883 in the church of Schwarzenberg in the Ore Mountains. How the embroidered work got from Strasbourg to Schwarzenberg or why only two fragments of the hanging remain today is unknown.
holder: GRASSI Museum of Applied Art, Leipzig

en.name: Ewer
description:
This brass ewer stands out among a series of distinctive brass vessels in the FBQ museum that are known for their unique shapes, sizes, and intricate designs. Many examples feature cylindrical bodies with fluted or faceted patterns and lions in relief on their necks. These Persian Islamic ewers served various purposes, including holding beverages, serving at parties, holding water for hand washing, or ablutions for affluent owners and guests. Crafted by artisans for the ruling class and aristocrats, this handle-less ewer is meticulously embossed and engraved with mythical creatures, calligraphy, and arabesques. The neck of the ewer bears two seated lions and a deer in relief, while the flattened shoulder displays an unusual pseudo-Kufic script and a human head. The faceted body is adorned with richly detailed decoration divided into four horizontal sections, featuring winged hares (some with human heads) and pseudo-Kufic script (some letters are human-headed).  
The use of a ewer carries religious significance, as running water is necessary for Muslims to perform ritual ablutions before prayer. Thus a family member would pour fresh water from the ewer over the individual’s hands, symbolising purification and spiritual cleansing. Crafted from brass, this ewer showcases meticulous beating and engraving techniques characteristic of Persian Islamic metalwork from the 12th to 13th centuries. The relief craftsmanship depicting mythical creatures and calligraphy would have been achieved through embossing and engraving, while the pseudo-Kufic script and arabesque designs show the influence of Islamic artistic tradition. The richly detailed decoration reflects the skill and artistry of the artisans of Khorasan or Herat in Iran during this period.
holder: Sheikh Faisal Bin Qassim Al Thani Museum
His Excellency Sheikh Faisal Bin Qassim Al Thani

en.name: Bird *Uşak* (fragment)
description: The Viennese bird *Uşak* is a fragment: the border of the bottom narrow side was sewn onto the shortened carpet field, whereby the original length of the carpet cannot be reconstructed. The eponymous rapport pattern unit of the white-grounded carpet field, four birds around a rosette, is repeated four times horizontally and seven times vertically. This special interpretation of the otherwise figureless *Uşak* carpets, is preferred again today, since an Ottoman source of the 17th century apostrophises the “crow pattern”. Moreover, it was established that numerous white-grounded carpets from the Ottoman region are located in the Habsburg inventories of the late 16th century that can possibly be indentified with bird *Uşak*s.

Lukash Madrasa
description:
Intended as lodgings for students who came to study in Tétouan for their secondary education, the *madrasa* was built in 1171/1758 under the orders of Sultan Sidi Mohamed Ibn ‘Abd Allah and *qa’id* ‘Umar Lukash. Whether fact or fiction, it is said that the students refused to move into the charitable foundation until it had been proved to them that the Lukash family had amassed its fortune honestly and without corruption.  
The students were housed on the ground and first floors, in 54 little rooms covering 6 sq. m. in surface area, surrounded by two interior courtyards. On the first floor, gangways overlooking the central patio lead to a second set of rooms. A library reserved for the students was constructed on the terrace.  
The ornamental decor was minimal and low-key: the ground was tiled with *mzehri*, the columns were surfaced with *zellij*, and, in the guardroom, gangways were open, smaller ones of which were pierced in the form of a *mrachat*.

es.name: Medersa Lukach
description:
Destinada a albergar a los estudiantes llegados a Tetuán para seguir la enseñanza secundaria, esta medersa se construyó en 1171/1758 por orden del sultán Sidi Mohamed Ibn Abdallah y del caíd Omar Lukach. Se cuenta, sea historia o leyenda, que los estudiantes rehusaron instalarse en esta fundación de caridad porque no se les había demostrado que la familia Lukach hubiese amasado su fortuna honradamente.  
Los estudiantes se alojaban en las plantas baja y primera, en 54 pequeñas habitaciones de 6 m2 de superficie dispuestas alrededor de dos patios interiores. En la primera planta, unas crujías suspendidas sobre el patio central daban acceso a un segundo conjunto de habitaciones. En la terraza se había dispuesto una biblioteca reservada a los estudiantes.  
La decoración ornamental es sobria: el suelo recubierto con un embaldosado de *mzehri*, las columnas con azulejos y, en el cuerpo de guardia, las crujías abiertas y unas pequeñas aberturas en forma de *mrachat*.

fr.name: Médersa Loukach
description:
Destinée à loger les étudiants venus à Tétouan pour y suivre l’enseignement secondaire, la médersa fut construite en 1171/1758 sur ordre du sultan Sidi Mohamed Ibn Abdallah et du caïd Omar Loukach. Histoire ou légende, on rapporte que les étudiants refusèrent de s’installer dans cette fondation charitable tant qu’on ne leur auvait pas prouvé que la famille Loukach avait amassé sa fortune honnêtement.  
Les étudiants étaient logés au rez-dechaussée et à l’étage, dans 54 petites chambres de 6 m2 de superficie, disposées autour de deux cours intérieures. À l’étage, des coursives surplombant le patio central donnaient accès à un second ensemble de chambres. Sur la terrasse était aménagée une bibliothèque réservée aux étudiants.  
Le décor ornemental était traité avec sobriété: le sol, recouvert d’un carrelage en *mzehri*, les colonnes de *zellige* et, dans le corps de garde, des coursives ont été ouvertes ainsi que des petites percées en forme de *mrachat*.

ar.name: جهاز قياس الدم (كتاب الحيل النفيسة) كتاب معرفة الأجهزة الميكانيكية البارعة
description: هذه اللوحة أتت من رسالة شائعة حول الأجهزة الميكانيكية والأنظمة الآلية المكتوبة في 1206 ونسخت باستمرار في القرون التالية. والجزري مؤلف الرسالة المسماة  كتاب الحيل النفيسة أورد وصفا لأكثر من مائة جهاز في رسالته وواحد من هذه الأجهزة يرى هنا.  وهذا الجهاز الرائع يستند لفكرتين علميتين فصد الدم كعلاج طبي واستخدام الآلات البسيطة لتشكيل مجموعة آلية معقدة وعلاج الأمراض المختلفة بفصد الدم كان شائعا حتى القرن التاسع عشر وهو أمر لا يحتاج بوضوح لمثل هذا الجهاز المعقد وهنا يضع المريض اصبعه المجروح في ثقب في حوض ويسيل الدم عبر قنوات إلى الحجرة السفلية مما يزيج ثقلا عائما والثقل العائم متصل من طرف له بقضيب الذي من الطرف الآخر متصل بقلم في يد  الكاتب في الجهة اليسرى العلوية . وعندما يرتفع مستوى الدم في الحوض فإنه يدفع بالثقل العائم للأعلى ويحرك قلم الكاتب ويشير لعلامات على لوح الكتابة لديه.

en.name:
A blood-measuring device  
*Kitab al-Hiyal al-naficah* (The Book of Knowledge of Ingenious Mechanical Devices)
description: This painting comes from a popular treatise on mechanical devices and automata written in 1206 and copied continuously in the following centuries. Al-Jazari, the author of *Kitab al-Hiyal al-naficah* (The Book of Knowledge of Ingenious Mechanical Devices), included descriptions of more than a hundred devices in his treatise, one of which can be seen here. This fascinating device builds on two scientific ideas: bloodletting as a medical treatment and the use of simple machines to create complex automata. The treatment of various ailments through bloodletting was common until the nineteenth century, and it clearly did not need such a complex device. Here, the patient puts a cut finger into a hole in the basin and blood falls through channels into a lower chamber, displacing a float. The float is attached to one end of a rod that, on its other end, attaches to the pen in the hand of the scribe on the upper left. As the level of the blood in the basin rises, it pushes the float up, moving the scribe’s pen and indicating marks on his writing board.
keywords: Painting; work-on-paper; works-on-paper; science; learning; science-and-learning
materials: Opaque watercolour, ink, and silver on paper
tags: Opaque watercolour, ink, and silver on paper

en.name: Sweetmeat dish
description: This sweetmeat dish was probably created in the Hirschberger Valley. The design is evidence of the highest mastery of glass engraving, using a combination of intaglio engraving and relief carving. On the base, the rim of the foot and the stem, there are ground and brightly polished sections. The bowl is oval in cross-section and has raised palmettes on three sides, which are also polished. The dish is largely covered with wheel engraving, which is mainly left matte. Both the smooth walls and the palmette leaves are covered in detailed ornaments and motifs, ranging from foliate scrolls and ribbon work to scalloped or dotted ornaments and miniature landscapes. On the one narrow side of the cup is a hitherto uninterpreted coat of arms with a crest and the initials “R H G V D”. The curved edge of the bowl is cut and polished; the form follows the outline of the palmette scroll.
keywords: Glass; sweetmeat-dish;  Hirschberger Tal; engraved decoration; Initials: R H G V D
tags: Initials: R H G V D

en.name: Ritual ladle for the Taghounja festival
description: The ritual ladle used in the Taghounja festival reflects the intersection of water, fertility, and collective ritual in Moroccan rural life. During this traditional celebration communities would gather to invoke rain, fertility, and divine blessing. The ladle, carved from wood, was used to pour or sprinkle water in symbolic gestures of renewal and abundance. Its simplicity belies a profound cultural meaning: water as the essence of life, shared collectively through ritual. Its preservation illustrates how intangible heritage and material culture merge to tell the story of Morocco’s spiritual relationship with water.
holder: Mohammed VI Museum of Water Civilisation
place: Collected as ethnographic testimony of ritual practice
keywords: Taghounja; ritual ladle; festival; rain prayers; water symbolism
partner: Mohammed VI Museum for the Civilisation of Water in Morocco

ar.name: باب المعبد.
description:
عُرف باب السور المحصن للقصبة (ألكاشوفا) باسم بورتا دو تيمبلو. وقد أطلق عليه هذا الاسم منذ الحقبة المسيحية بسبب قربه من ممتلكات عقارية أعطيت للتنظيم الديني والعسكري لفرسان المعبد، وذلك مباشرة بعد دمج إلفاس في مملكة البرتغال.  
والواقع، أن هذا المدخل يمكن أن لايتبدى للعيان بالنسبة لمن يريد البحث عن أطلال ألكاشوفا التي تعود إلى العصر الإسلامي، وذلك بسبب اندماجه - كما هو الحال بالنسبة لأطلال أخرى من الماضي الإسلامي للمدينة- داخل باحات وبيوت في ملكية الخواص. وللدخول إلى الفضاء المخصص للألكاشوفا الإسلامية، يجب المرور تحت قوس منكسر على اليمين، منفتح في الحائط المبني بالطابية للسور المحصن. كان هذا المدخل في الماضي، ولأسباب دفاعية، مكوّناً من مدخل مزدوج ذو زاوية حادة من 90 درجة. يتكون هذا المدخل المزدوج من برج منفصل عن السور يتصل به عبرحائط ذي زاوية قائمة، مما يفرض المرورعبر البوابتين المزدوجتين المفصولتين بواسطة هوّة. يتموضع المدخل الأول بشكل متعامد مع السور، ويفضي إلى غرفة تسبق مدخل العبور إلى السور المحصن، والذي كان يتم من خلال باب ثاني مبني داخل السور.  
فيما عدا الاستخدام الكثيف للطابية (التراب المدكوك)، استُعملت في بناء هذا الباب أحجارغرانيتية غير منحوتة تستند إلى عضادات على شاكلة الأبواب الأندلسية الأخرى. وفي القرن التاسع عشر، بُدأ بتهديم هذا الباب ثم توقف المشروع من بعدها. ولتدارك الهدم الحاصل، أعيد بناء أعلى الأقواس باستعمال ملاط حديث يحاول تحقيق الشبه مع الأصلي. أما على مستوى الأساس، وحتى منطقة انطلاق الحدوات الحدوية، كما في الحجرة الخارجية عند مدخل الألكاشوفا، فقد تم الحفاظ على الخصائص والقياسات الأصلية. أما بقايا إطار القوس أو الألفيز فهي أصلية. تبلغ مساحة هذه الحجرة الوسطى 12 مترا مربعاً وهي ذات شكل رباعي الزوايا.  
من جهة البنية والنمط، وعن طريق المقارنة بأبنية أخرى ذات طابع دفاعي، يمكن التأكيد على أن بناء هذا المدخل المكوّع قد تم خلال الفترة الموحدية.

يمثلُ البابُ القديمُ لقلعة يابرة (إيفورا) اليوم جزءا من إقامة خاصة. يجمعُ بناؤه بين الطابية (التراب المدكوك)، المستعملة بشكل خاص في التطبيقات العسكرية ومدخل مكوع بسيط؛ ويتكون من برج متقدم تمَّت تقويةُ مَداخلِه بأكتاف من الأحجار غير المنجورة وبعقود على شكل حدوة حصان، مؤطرة بألفيزات؛ وهو ترتيب يسمحُ بالمقابلة مع بنايات مشابهة بمدينة باداخوس الموحدية. وفي القرن 19، جرى البدءُ في مشروع يهدفُ تهديمَ المبنى، إلا أنه تم التخلي عنه لاحقا؛ ورُممت الأجزاءُ العلوية بملاط حديث مشابه للأصيل.
dynasty: الفترة الموحدية، القرن 6 – 7 الهجري / القرن 12 – 13 الميلادي.
keywords: إلفاس؛ باب؛ باب المعبد؛ تراب مدكوك؛ الطابية ، سور؛ عمارة عسكرية؛ غرانيت؛ موحدون.
partner: Archaeological Area and Museum of Mertola, Mertola

en.name: Temple Gate.
description:
This gate in the walled precinct of the Citadel seems to coincide with the one which came to be known in the Christian period as the Porta do Templo or Temple Gate, since buildings located close to it were devoted to the military and religious Order of the Templars after the integration of Elvas into the Portuguese crown.  
However, this entrance can easily pass unnoticed by those looking for traces of the citadel from the Islamic period because, like many other remnants of the Islamic past in this town, it is largely integrated into the properties of private houses.  
Today, in order to enter the interior of the Islamic Citadel, you have to pass through an archway opening directly through its surrounding *tabiyya* (dry mud) wall. Earlier, however, for defensive reasons, access was through a double-gate system with a 90-degree angle or bend in it. This double entrance consisted of a tower standing proud of the wall and joined to it by a wall at right angles, making it necessary for anyone who wanted to enter the citadel to pass through two gates and through an intermediate space. The first entrance was thus perpendicular to the wall and gave access to a chamber which preceded the entrance into the walled precinct, which was through a second gate made in the wall itself.  
In terms of construction materials, in spite of the dominant use of *tabiyya*, this gateway, as in several other fortifications in al-Andalus region, is flanked by granite blocks. In the 19th century, its destruction was begun, but this project was abandoned. In order to remedy the effect of the work that had been started, the upper part of the arches was rebuilt, and more recent mortar can be seen here, where an attempt has been made to make it similar to the original. However, from the levels of the base to the springers of the surmounted arches, as well as in the outer chamber of the entrance to the citadel, the original characteristics and dimensions have been retained. The vestiges of the frame or *alfiz* of the arch are also original. The aforementioned intermediate chamber is square in plan and its area is approximately 12 square metres.  
In structural and typological terms this L-shaped entrance, on the basis of parallels with other defensive structures, may have been built in the Almohad period.

The old entrance to the Évora citadel is now part of a private residence. Its construction combines the adobe typically used for military applications and a single chicane entrance created by an advanced tower the entrances to which had entrances strengthened with ashlar gateposts and horseshoe arches with *alfiz* frames. This combination suggests a parallel with similar construction from Almohad Badajoz. A project to demolish it was started in the 19th century, but subsequently abandoned. The upper parts of the arches were then restored using modern mortar similar to the original.
keywords: Temple Gateway; Elvas; Almohad; garden; wall; tabiyya; granite; military architecture
partner: Archaeological Area and Museum of Mertola, Mertola

es.name: Puerta del Templo.
description:
Esta puerta del recinto amurallado de la alcazaba parece coincidir con aquella conocida, ya en el periodo cristiano, como Puerta del Templo por encontrarse junto a inmuebles donados a la orden religioso-militar de los Templarios tras la incorporación de Elvas a la corona portuguesa.  
Esta entrada puede pasar desapercibida para quien intente encontrar rastros de la alcazaba musulmana, dado que, al igual que ocurre con otros vestigios del pasado islámico de la ciudad, se encuentran en gran medida dentro de patios y casas particulares.  
Hoy en día, para entrar en el espacio de la alcazaba islámica, hay que atravesar un arco abierto frontalmente en la pared de tapial (*tabiyya*) del recinto amurallado. Antes, sin embargo, el acceso se hacía, por cuestiones defensivas, por un sistema de doble puerta en ángulo, o codo, de 90º. Esa entrada doble estaba formada por una torre separada de la muralla y unida a ella por un muro en ángulo recto, lo que obligaba a quien quisiera entrar a pasar por las dos puertas y el espacio intermedio. La primera puerta era, pues, perpendicular a la muralla y daba acceso al espacio que antecedía a la entrada en el recinto amurallado a través de una segunda puerta, ésta ya en la muralla.  
En cuanto a los materiales de construcción, pese a que predomina el tapial, esta puerta, como ocurre en algunas otras fortificaciones de al-Andalus, presenta sillares de granito en las jambas. En el siglo XIII / XIX se empezó a desmantelar, pero el proyecto fue abandonado y se intentó remediar el efecto de las obras iniciadas rehaciendo la parte superior de los arcos, de ahí que se observen argamasas más recientes que intentan imitar las originales. Con todo, desde el nivel de la base hasta el arranque de los arcos de herradura, así como en el espacio que precede la entrada en la alcazaba, se mantienen las características y dimensiones originales. Los restos del alfiz son también originales. El espacio intermedio es de planta cuadrangular, con un área aproximada de 12 m².  
En términos estructurales y tipológicos, esta entrada acodada, por sus semejanzas con otras obras defensivas, pudo construirse en época almohade.

Esta antigua entrada de la alcazaba de Elvas se encuentra hoy dentro de una casa particular. En ella se unen la construcción en tapial de tipo militar y una puerta acodada simple formada por una torre avanzada de vanos reforzados con jambas de sillería y arcos de herradura con alfiz. Estas características la aproximan a las construcciones del periodo almohade de Badajoz. En el siglo XIII / XIX llegó a empezarse su desmantelamiento, pero la obra se abandonó y se reconstruyó la parte superior de los arcos, donde se observan argamasas más recientes que intentan imitar las originales.
dates: Siglos VI-VII de la Hégira / XII-XIII d. C.
keywords: Muralla; tapial; granito; arquitectura militar
partner: Archaeological Area and Museum of Mertola, Mertola

fr.name: Porte du Temple.
description:
Cette porte de l'enceinte fortifiée de l'*alcáçova* semble être la porte connue comme la Porta do Templo, déjà à la période chrétienne, en raison de la présence dans son voisinage des biens immobiliers cédés à l'ordre religieux et militaire des Templiers, immédiatement après l'intégration d'Elvas à la couronne portugaise.  
Cette entrée, par ailleurs, peut passer inaperçue de ceux qui recherchent des vestiges de l'*alcáçova* d'époque islamique en raison de son intégration – à l'instar d'autres vestiges du passé islamique de la ville – dans des cours et des maisons particulières.  
Pour pénétrer dans l'espace de l'*alcáçova* islamique, on doit passer sous un arc brisé à droite, sur le mur en pisé *(tabiyya*) de son enceinte fortifiée. Jadis, son accès, pour des raisons défensives, était constitué d'un système de double entrée, avec un angle ou coude à 90°. Cette double entrée était composée d'une tour détachée de la muraille et reliée à elle par un mur en angle droit, rendant obligatoire le passage par les doubles portes avec un sas intermédiaire. La première entrée se trouvait ainsi perpendiculaire à la muraille et donnait accès à une pièce qui précédait l'entrée de l'enceinte fortifiée, qui se faisait par le franchissement d'une deuxième porte, déjà à l'intérieur de l'enceinte.  
En termes de matériaux de construction, malgré l'utilisation massive du pisé, cette porte présente, comme d'autres d'al-Andalus, des moellons de granit sur les jambages. Au XIXe siècle, on a commencé sa démolition, projet qui a été interrompu ; pour remédier à cela, on a refait la partie supérieure des arcs à l'aide de mortiers plus modernes, qui essaient de ressembler aux originaux. Au niveau de la base, toutefois, jusqu'aux départs des arcs outrepassés, ainsi que dans la pièce extérieure à l'entrée de l'*alcáçova*, on a maintenu les caractéristiques et les dimensions originales. Les vestiges de l'encadrement de l'arc ou *alfiz* sont également d'origine. Cette pièce intermédiaire se développe sur un plan quadrangulaire avec une surface approximative de 12 m2.  
En termes structurels et typologiques, cette entrée coudée semble, par comparaison avec d'autres ouvrages à caractère défensif, avoir été construite à l'époque almohade.

La vieille entrée de la citadelle d'Évora fait aujourd'hui partie d'une résidence privée. Sa construction allie le pisé, typiquement utilisé pour les applications militaires, et une entrée coudée simple, constituée d'une tour avancée dont les accès sont renforcés par des jambages en moellons et des arcs en fer à cheval encadrés d'*alfiz*. Cette combinaison établit un parallèle avec des constructions similaires de la ville almohade de Badajoz. Un projet de démolition fut amorcé au XIXe siècle, mais ultérieurement abandonné. Les parties supérieures de l'arc furent alors restaurées avec un mortier moderne similaire à l'original.
keywords: Porta do Templo ; Elvas ; Almohades ; porte ; muraille ; pisé ; granit ; architecture militaire
partner: Archaeological Area and Museum of Mertola, Mertola

pt.name: Porta do Templo.
description:
Esta porta do recinto amuralhado da Alcáçova parece coincidir com aquela que vem a ser conhecida, já no período cristão, como Porta do Templo, por junto a ela se localizarem bens imobiliários doados à Ordem religiosa-militar dos Templários logo após a integração de Elvas na coroa portuguesa.  
  
Porém, esta entrada pode passar algo despercebida a quem tente encontrar traços da alcáçova de época islâmica dado que, à semelhança do que se passa com outros traços do passado islâmico desta cidade, eles encontram-se em grande medida dentro de quintais e de casas particulares.  
  
Para hoje se entrar no espaço da Alcáçova islâmica atravessa-se um arco rasgado a direito na parede de taipa (*tabiyya*), do seu recinto amuralhado. Antes, porém, o seu acesso era, por uma questão defensiva, formado por um sistema de porta dupla, com um ângulo ou cotovelo de 90°. Essa entrada dupla era formada por uma torre destacada da muralha e ligada a ela por uma parede em ângulo recto, tornando obrigatória, para quem quisesse entrar na muralha, a passagem por duas portas e por um espaço intermédio; a primeira entrada encontrava-se, assim, perpendicular em relação à muralha e dava acesso a uma câmara que antecedia a entrada no recinto amuralhado, feita a través da transposição de uma segunda porta, esta já na muralha.  
  
Em termos de materiais de construção, apesar de dominar a utilização da taipa, este porta, como acontece em algumas outra fortificações do *al*\-*Andalus*, apresenta silhares de granito nas ombreiras. No século XIX chegou a iniciar-se a sua destruição mas esse projecto foi abandonado; tentando remediar o efeito das obras iniciadas, a parte superior dos arcos foi refeita, observando-se aí argamassas mais recentes que tentam assemelhar-se às originais. Porém, desde os níveis da base, até aos arranques dos arcos "ultrapassados", bem como na câmara exterior à entrada na alcáçova mantêm-se as características e dimensões originais. Os vestígios de moldura do arco ou "alfiz", esses são também originais. A referida câmara intermédia apresenta uma planta quadrangular com uma área aproximada de 12 m2.  
  
Em termos estruturais e tipológicos esta entrada em cotovelo, pelos paralelos que tem com outras obras defensivas pode ter sido construída em época almóada.

Esta antiga entrada na alcáçova de Elvas encontra-se hoje dentro de uma casa particular. Alia a existência de taipa de tipo militar a uma porta em cotovelo simples, formada com uma torre avançada, onde se encontram entradas reforçadas com ombreiras em silharia e arcos em ferradura com "alfiz". Este conjunto de circunstâncias aproxima-a das construções do período almóada de Badajoz. No século XIX chegou a iniciar-se a sua destruição mas esse projecto foi abandonado; a parte superior dos arcos foi então refeita, observando-se aí argamassas mais recentes que tentam assemelhar-se às originais.
keywords: Porta do Templo; Elvas; almóadas; orta; muralha; taipa; granito; arquitectura militar
partner: Archaeological Area and Museum of Mertola, Mertola

en.name: House
short_description: The existence of structures with similar architectonic features in the Reka Area, the territory of Metochia, Albania, Greece, Bulgaria and Bosnia confirms the common concept of expression in dwellings of "tower" type in the traditional architecture of the Balkans. This three-storey house of symmetrical layout is built of stone. It shows some features of tower-houses with its very small windows built extremely high at the ground floor and symmetrically positioned bigger windows on upper stories. The house is distinguished by the interesting entrance portion.
dates: End of 19th – beginning of the 20th century
history: The first mention of the Debar-Reka art school in the sources was in the 10th century. The centre of the art school was in the village of Galichnik. Activities of the Debar-Galichnik art centre throughout the centuries have given rise to the development of diverse crafts related to construction and architectural decoration, as well as icon-painting, woodcarving, sculpture, etc. The male population of the Reka area was traditionally widely known for their construction skills. These native architects used to work in groups called *tajfas*. *Tajfas* consisted of around ten men, including builders, wood-carving masters and stone cutters. The leader of the *tajfa*, i.e. the person that used to organize the construction activities, was called *ustabashiya*.
keywords: art school; architectural decoration crafts

en.name: Mulay Idriss Mausoleum
description:
The mausoleum of Fez’s patron Mulay Idriss, otherwise known as Idriss II or even as Idriss al-Azhar, stands within an urban development called *horm*, “forbidden”, which includes:  
1\. The “House of the Tent”, *Dar al-Gaytun*, which was Mulay Idriss’ dwelling place during the construction of the town in 192/808.  
2\. The *al-Achraf* Mosque, “Mosque of the Nobles”, where the town’s founder prayed.  
3\. A fountain and a building reserved for ablutions, *Dar al-Wudu’*.  
The mausoleum was originally a large and beautiful mosque, the al-Achraf Mosque, erected whilst the town was being constructed, and which risked losing an element of its prestige when the Qarawiyin mosque, to where Friday prayers was transferred, was built in the 4th/10th century. The building kept its original design up until 707/1308, when it was rebuilt by Idrissid *shorfa*s, descendants of Idriss II. A century later, part of the mosque was allowed to deteriorate, and one of its walls crumbled down.  
In the 9th/15th century, a mystical movement spread throughout Morocco which called for the renaissance of religious *Sufi* practices. Numerous saints crisscrossed the country. The most famous of these were buried in mausoleums, and were surrounded by important religious ceremony. At the same time, the Merinid political authorities were on the search for the burial place of Idriss II which ancient texts had positioned to be in the al-Ashraf Mosque. During restoration work to the mosque carried out in 840/1437 under the Merinids, the sarcophagus of Idriss II, believed to have been buried in Volubilis, was discovered, and a convex construction was erected on the site of the discovery to distinguish it from the tombs of other saints.  
Since then, a veritable cult established itself around the Mulay Idriss Mausoleum. The veneration accorded to this human being is based on two factors: on his origin, Mulay Idriss being the sixth descendant of the Prophet; and on the basis of his political position, as the son of the founder of the Idrissid dynasty of Morocco, and as founder himself of the town of Fez.  
Each dynasty following on from the Merinids engaged itself in the embellishment of this sanctuary, in particular the Sultan Mulay Isma‘il (1082/1672–1139/1727), who supervised the construction of a green pyramidal dome, the *qubba*, which hangs over the building. The tomb was covered by a canopy of sculpted wood encrusted with copper and gold, and was then surrounded by several columns made of black-and-white marble. Finally, he also oversaw the construction of a magnificent fountain in the courtyard, and built a tasteful, multicoloured minaret, the highest in the *medina*. All of these works would have been undertaken by volunteers, and the materials would have been donated by the sultans free of charge.  
When it came to his turn, the Sultan Mulay ‘Abd al-Rahman constructed a new mosque in 1239/1824 which adjoined the dome, as well as restoring the house of al- Gaytun, the previous residence of Mulay Idriss, which brought to light a small, previously closed-off room, and an ablutions stone. The decor was, for the most part, restored by King Mohamed V, after 1956. The vestibule, elaborately but heavily decorated, with its lamps and chandeliers, is closed off by a sort of gigantic folding screen made of red wood of an extraordinary colour. The floor, paved with multicoloured *zellij*, adds – along with the chandeliers and the chiselled, coloured ceiling – to the creation of a mysterious atmosphere, which is particularly strong in the evening, when the smaller lamps hanging from the dome create a garland of golden lights.  
A *mashrabiyya* stands to demarcate the whole of this urban compound, (which is thought of as sacred and hence called *horm*); it is made of cedar wood and has a hole at its centre, which is the shaft through which offerings can be made. Fine mosaics decorate its base, next to a fountain which is protected by a small, iron-forged gate. The wall above is decorated with carved plaster, highlighted with remarkable delicacy through the careful use of colour and gold-leaf. The interlacing and rosette motifs, crafted like lace, surpasses, in terms of perfection, the most beautiful decorations of this type found in any *madrasa*. The whole of it, surmounted by panelling, is adorned with a cedar canopy covered in glazed tiles.

es.name: Mausoleo de Mulay Idris
description:
El mausoleo del patrono de la villa de Fez, Mulay Idris o Idris II (también, Idris al-Azhar), forma parte de un conjunto urbano denominado horm, “prohibido”, que comprende:  
1\. La Casa de la Tienda de Campaña, *Dar al-Kaitun*, residencia de Mulay Idris durante la construcción de la villa, en el 192/808.  
2\. La mezquita *al-Achraf*, o Mezquita de los Nobles, donde oraba el fundador de la ciudad.  
3\. Una fuente y un edificio reservado a las abluciones, *Dar al-Wudu’*.  
Al principio, el mausoleo era una mezquita grande y hermosa —la mezquita al-Achraf— construida durante la fundación de la ciudad y que perdería parte de su prestigio en el siglo IV/X con la construcción de la Qarawiyin, a donde se trasladó la plegaria del viernes. El edificio conservó su planta original hasta 707/1308, fecha en la que fue reconstruido por los *chorfa* idrisíes, descendientes de Idris II. Un siglo después se deteriora en parte; uno de sus muros se vino abajo.  
En el siglo IX/XV se propagó por Marruecos un movimiento místico que proclamaba el renacimiento de las prácticas religiosas sufíes. Numerosos santos recorrían el país. Los más célebres fueron enterrados en mausoleos, en medio de ceremoniales religiosos muy importantes. En la misma época, la autoridad política meriní indagaba el paradero de la sepultura de Idris II, que los textos antiguos situaban en la mezquita al-Achraf. Durante los trabajos de restauración de la misma realizados en 840/1437, bajo la dinastía meriní, se descubrió el sarcófago de Idris II, que se creía enterrado en Volubilis. En el lugar donde se encontró se erigió una construcción convexa, a fin de distinguirlo de las tumbas de los demás santos.  
Desde entonces se instauró en el mausoleo de Mulay Idris un auténtico culto. La veneración a este personaje se debe a dos razones: sus orígenes, puesto que era el sexto descendiente del Profeta, y su papel político como hijo del fundador de la dinastía idrisí en Marruecos, y fundador él mismo de la ciudad de Fez.  
Tras los meriníes, todas las dinastías se dedicaron a embellecer el santuario. Se distinguió el sultán Mulay Ismail (1082/1672-1139/1727), quien hizo construir una cúpula piramidal verde, *qubba*, dominando el edificio. Recubierta de un baldaquino de madera tallada con incrustaciones de cobre y oro, la tumba está rodeada de numerosas columnas de mármol blanco y negro. También hizo construir en el patio una magnífica fuente y un alminar policromado, el más alto de toda la *medina*. Todos estos trabajos los llevaron a cabo voluntarios, y los materiales fueron suministrados gratuitamente por las autoridades.  
Por su parte, en 1239/1824 el sultán Mulay Abderrahman hizo construir junto a la cúpula la nueva mezquita, y la casa de al-Kaitun, antigua residencia de Mulay Idris, fue objeto de una restauración que permitió descubrir una pequeña cámara ciega y una piedra de ablución. La decoración ha sido restaurada en su mayor parte por el rey Mohamed V, después de 1956.  
El vestíbulo, ricamente decorado aunque algo recargado, está cerrado por una especie de enorme biombo de madera roja, de un color extraordinario, con sus lámparas y arañas. El suelo, embaldosado con *zelish* policromados, contribuye, junto con las arañas y los techos cincelados de vivos colores, a crear un ambiente de misterio, especialmente por la tarde, cuando las lamparillas que cuelgan de la cúpula forman guirnaldas de luces doradas.  
Un mocárabe de cedro delimita este conjunto sagrado o *horm*, en cuyo centro, perforado, está el tronco de las ofrendas. Delicados mosaicos revisten el zócalo, donde hay una fuente protegida por una pequeña cancela de hierro forjado. Por encima, el muro está adornado con yesería cincelada, realzada con colores y dorados, de una finura notable. Las lacerías y rosetones, trabajados como encaje, superan en perfección a los más bellos ornamentos de este género que encontramos en las *medersa*s. El conjunto, rematado por el artesonado, tiene un tejadillo de cedro cubierto de tejas vidriadas.

fr.name: Mausolée Moulay Idriss
description:
Le mausolée du patron de la ville de Fès, Moulay Idriss ou Idriss II, ou encore Idriss al-Azhar, est inclus dans un ensemble urbain appelé *horm*, “interdit”, qui comprend:  
1\. La “Maison de la Tente”, *Dar al-Gaytoun*, logement qu’a occupé Moulay Idriss lors de la construction de la ville, en 192/808.  
2\. La mosquée *al-Achraf*, “Mosquée des Nobles”, où priait le fondateur de la ville.  
3\. Une fontaine et un bâtiment réservé aux ablutions, *Dar al-Woudou*’.  
À l’origine, le mausolée était une large et belle mosquée, la mosquée al-Achraf, construite lors de la fondation de la ville et qui allait perdre une partie de son prestige avec la construction, au IVe/Xe siècle, de la mosquée Qaraouiyine, où fut transférée la prière du vendredi. L’édifice conserva son plan d’origine jusqu’en 707/1308, date à laquelle il fut reconstruit par les *chorfa*s idrissides, descendants d’Idriss II. Un siècle plus tard, la mosquée se détériora en partie, et l’un de ses murs s’écroula.  
Au IXe/XVe siècle, se propageait au Maroc un mouvement mystique qui appelait à la renaissance des pratiques religieuses soufies. De nombreux saints sillonnaient le pays. Les plus célèbres étaient enterrés dans des mausolées, et étaient entourés d’un cérémonial religieux très important. À la même époque, l’autorité politique mérinide était à la recherche de la sépulture d’Idriss II que les textes anciens avaient située dans la mosquée al-Achraf. Lors des travaux de restauration de la mosquée, en 840/1437, sous la dynastie mérinide, on découvrit le sarcophage d’Idriss II, que l’on croyait enterré à Volubilis, et on érigea à l’emplacement de la découverte une construction convexe afin de la distinguer des tombeaux des autres saints.  
Depuis lors, un véritable culte a été instauré dans le mausolée Moulay Idriss. La vénération accordée à ce personnage tient à deux choses: à son origine, Moulay Idriss étant le sixième descendant du Prophète; et à son rôle politique en tant que fils du fondateur de la dynastie idrisside au Maroc, et fondateur lui-même de la ville de Fès.  
À la suite des Mérinides, chaque dynastie s’est employée à embellir ce sanctuaire, et particulièrement le sultan Moulay Ismaïl (1082/1672-1139/1727), qui fit construire une coupole pyramidale verte, koubba, surplombant l’édifice. Recouvert d’un baldaquin en bois sculpté, à incrustations de cuivre et d’or, le tombeau est entouré de nombreuses colonnes en marbre blanc et noir. Il fit aménager dans la cour une magnifique fontaine, et construisit un élégant minaret polychrome, le plus haut de toute la médina.Tous ces travaux auraient été entrepris par des volontaires, et les matériaux fournis gratuitement par les sultans.  
Le sultan Moulay Abderrahman fit, à son tour, construire la nouvelle mosquée, en 1239/1824, attenant à la coupole, et la maison d’*al-Gaytoun*, ancienne résidence du Moulay Idriss, fut l’objet d’une restauration qui permit de mettre au jour une petite chambre sans ouverture, et une pierre à ablutions. Les décorations ont, pour la plupart, été restaurées par le roi Mohamed V, après 1956.  
Le vestibule richement, mais lourdement, décoré est fermé par une sorte de gigantesque paravent de bois rouge d’une extraordinaire couleur, avec ses lampes et ses lustres. Le sol, pavé d’un *zellige* polychrome, contribue, à côté des lustres, des plafonds ciselés et coloriés, à créer une ambiance de mystère, et ce, particulièrement le soir, lorsque les veilleuses accrochées au dôme forment des guirlandes de lumières dorées.  
Un moucharabieh de cèdre délimite cet ensemble urbain, considéré comme sacré, appelé *horm*, et est percé en son centre d’un trou: le tronc des offrandes. Des mosaïques délicates revêtent le soubassement, à côté d’une fontaine protégée d’une petite grille de fer forgé.Au dessus dessus, le mur s’orne de plâtres ciselés, rehaussés de couleurs et de dorures, d’une finesse remarquable. Les entrelacs et les rosaces, ouvragés comme des dentelles, dépassent en perfection les plus belles décorations de ce genre que nous retrouvons dans les médersas. L’ensemble, surmonté de boiseries, s’agrémente d’un auvent de cèdre couvert de tuiles vernissées.

en.name: Hanging (*sitara*) for the Mosque of the Prophet, Medina al-Munawwarah
short_description: This hanging of red, yellow-golden and green silk is richly embroidered with silver and silver-gilt inscriptions and designs. Above, a lamp with invocations to Allah as the Opener or Judge (ya Fattah) appears suspended from an arched niche resting on two columns. Its spandrels display two roundels with the Islamic profession of Faith (shahada). Below, a quote from chapter 2 (Al-Baqarah), verse 197 of the Holy Qur’an appears: ‘…and the best provision is Al-Taqwa (piety, righteousness)’. In the lower half of the hanging, four roundels with the names of the rightly-guided caliphs surround the imperial Ottoman emblem or tughra of the sultan Abd al- Hamid II  (1293 H/1876 AD – 1327 H/1909 AD), who commissioned this curtain.. Hangings like this one may have been intended for the prayer niche of the Prophet’s mosque, as earlier examples of this type often include the inscription ‘this is the mihrab of the Prophet (pbuh)’.
holder: Sharjah Museum of Islamic Civilisation / Sharjah Museums Authority
dates: Hegira mid 13th century / AD mid 19th century

ar.name: زبدية ذات غطاء.
description:
زبدية بيضوية منخفضة من عجينة الكوارتز (فريت)، ذات غطاء مقبب له من الأعلى قبضة من النحاس المذهب، وفي أسفلها زخرفة من الورود بالأزرق والأحمر والأخضر. تبدأ الزخارف على الغطاء من الزخرفة تحت القبضة بتعريقات ورقية، وأربع ورقات من نموذج الساز التخيلي الأزرق الملون في الوسط بالأحمر، وهي تتحرك عكس عقارب الساعة. تظهر أربعة أزواج من الأزهار بين أوراق الساز تتألف كل منها من زنبقة زرقاء وياقوتية حمراء برتقالية، وهي تنبثق أيضاً من سوق ورقية تتقاطع معاً.  
تم تزيين طرف الحافة بتموجات بيضاء على أرضية زرقاء، وفي وسط كل منها نقطة باللون الأسود. ويحيط بالجزء العلوي ضفيرة باللونين الأحمر والأخضر، وتحتها تسع أزهار خزامى زرقاء اللون مع تفاصيل نقطية حمراء تعوم حول الزبدية مع عقارب الساعة مما يعطي الإحساس بوجود إكليل أفقي على الرغم من أن جميعها تنبثق من القاعدة. يظهر شريط آخر أسفل الخزامى، مؤلف من أزهار القرنفل التي تدور بعكس عقارب الساعة، والتي تنبثق سوقها هي الأخرى من القاعدة. تم تزيين قعر الزبدية بحليات زخرفية محددة بثلاثة إطارات، وهي تضم خمسة تنسيقات زهرية ذات بتلات حمراء وزرقاء، وتملأ ستة نماذج مجردة باللون الأزرق المساحة المتبقية.  
يذكر شكل الزبدية بالزبديات الإيرانية الخزفية والمعدنية التي تعود إلى القرن السابع/ الثالث عشر، وهي تذكر أيضاً بأدوات المائدة في البلاط الإيطالي خلال القرن الخامس عشر (كما يبدو ذلك على سبيل المثال في اللوحة المنفذة بطريقة الحفر لماتينيا حيث يظهر تابع يخدم المائدة خلال لعبة ورق). أما في البلاط العثماني، فقد تم إنتاج مثل هذه الزبديات من النحاس الأحمر المذهب (تومباك)، وكانت جزءاً لا يتجزأ من أدوات المائدة لتقديم الطعام خلال الوجبات.

كانت الزبادي، ذوات الأغطية، الشبيهة بهذه، تُصنَّع في البلاط العثماني، من النحاس الأصفر اللمَّاع (سبيكة التمبك)، كما من الخزف، وقد شكَّلت جزءاً لا يتجزأ من الفخاريات، والخزفيات، وأواني الصيني المستخدمة لتقديم الطعام في الوجبات. من شأن أسلوب زخرفها، أن يضعها بين الأواني الخزفية الازنيقية، المزَهَّرة العائدة إلى القرن العاشر الهجري/ السادس عشر الميلادي.
holder: المتحف الملكي، المتحف الوطني في اسكتلندا NMS.
keywords: تومباك؛ عجينة الكوارتز (فريت).

en.name: Lidded bowl.
description:
A squat, elliptically shaped, lidded bowl of stone-paste (fritware) with a flattened domical lid topped by a gilded copper-alloy finial. A blue, red and green rosette enhances the base of the finial; the pattern on the lid itself then opens out from the base of the finial where, from leafy stems, four mythical, blue, serrated *saz* leaves with red centres sprout, moving in an anti-clockwise direction, their stems crossing. In between the *saz* leaves, there are four floral pairs, each consisting of a blue lily and a red-orange hyacinth. These also emerge from leafy stems, sinuously crossing over each other.  
The edge of the rim is decorated by a scalloped border of white on blue, a black dot in the centre of each scallop. The upper edge of the body receives a guilloche border rendered in red and green. Below, nine blue tulips with red dotted detailing flow around the bowl in a clockwise direction, giving the impression of a horizontally disposed garland, although they all rise in fact from the base. A second band below the tulips is composed of carnations, this time flowing in an anti-clockwise direction, their stems again springing from the baseline below. The well of the bowl receives a decorative roundel defined by three linear borders. It contains five flower sprays with red and blue petals. Six abstract motifs in blue fill the remaining spaces.  
The shape of this bowl recalls Iranian metal and ceramic bowls dating to the AH 7th / AD 13th century and also appears among the tableware of the Italian courts during the 15th century (as seen, for example, in an engraving by Mantegna where an attendant serves at table during a card game). In Ottoman court culture lidded bowls such as this were produced in gilt copper (*tombak*), and occurred as an integral part of the tableware used to serve food at mealtimes.

In Ottoman court culture lidded bowls like this one were produced in gilt copper (*tombak*) as well as pottery and occurred as an integral part of the crockery used to serve food at mealtimes. Its style of decoration places it among other floral Iznik wares dated to the AH 10th / AD late 16th century.
keywords: Iznik; stone-paste (fritware); tombak
materials: Stone-paste (fritware), blue, green, black and bole-red underglaze, over which a clear glaze.
tags: Stone-paste (fritware), blue, green, black and bole-red underglaze, over which a clear glaze.

es.name: Cuenco con tapadera
description:
Cuenco elíptico hecho en pasta de piedra (frita), con tapa en forma de cúpula achatada con un remate de aleación de cobre. La base de este remate está realzada con una roseta azul, roja y verde. El resto de la tapadera está decorada con una ancha banda en la que se han dibujado cuatro hojas dentadas de *saz*, la planta mítica, con la parte central roja; entre ellas se han dispuesto cuatro pares cruzados de tallos de azucenas y jacintos de color rojo anaranjado. El borde se ha decorado con festones punteados blancos sobre fondo azul.  
En la parte superior hay un guilloché rojo y verde; por debajo de él, nueve tulipanes azules con puntos rojos, muy inclinados, forman una especie de guirnalda horizontal, aunque nacen de la base; completa la decoración del cuerpo una línea de claveles rojos cuyos tallos salen, asimismo, de la base. En el interior, el fondo del cuenco está decorado con un medallón de triple borde que contiene cinco ramos de flores de pétalos rojos y azules. Seis motivos abstractos rellenan el espacio restante.  
La forma de este cuenco recuerda la de los cuencos cerámicos y metálicos iraníes del siglo VII / XIII, que también formaban parte de las vajillas de las cortes italianas del siglo XV (pueden verse, por ejemplo, en un grabado de Mantegna, en el que un criado sirve una mesa durante una partida de cartas). En la corte otomana, estos cuencos con tapadera solían ser de cobre dorado *(tombak)* y formaban parte de los recipientes en que se servía la comida.

En la corte otomana, estos cuencos con tapadera solían ser de cobre dorado *(tombak)* y formaban parte de los recipientes en que se servía la comida. El estilo de su decoración lo agrupa con otras cerámicas florales de Iznik datadas en el siglo X de la Hégira (finales del XVI d. C.).
dates: Siglo X de la Hégira / finales del XVI d.C.
keywords: Iznik; pasta cerámica (frita); tombak
materials: Pasta de piedra (frita) pintada en azul, verde, negro y bol rojo bajo vidriado claro.
tags: Pasta de piedra (frita) pintada en azul, verde, negro y bol rojo bajo vidriado claro.

fr.name: Coupe à couvercle.
description:
Coupe à couvercle de forme elliptique en céramique frittée à couvercle en dôme aplati surmonté d'une prise en alliage de cuivre doré se détachant d'une rosette peinte bleue, rouge et verte. Le décor du couvercle lui-même part de la base de la prise. Il se compose de quatre feuilles *saz* dentelées bleues à rehaut central rouge, partant de tiges feuillues et alternant avec quatre paires de fleurs (un lys bleu et une hyacinthe rouge orangé), le tout dans le sens contraire à celui des aiguilles d'une montre.  
Le bord du couvercle est décoré d'une bordure festonnée blanche sur fond bleu, chaque feston comportant en son centre un point noir.  
La partie supérieure du corps de la coupe est ornée d'une bordure guillochée verte et rouge. En dessous, neuf tulipes bleues à rehauts de points rouges courent autour de la panse dans le sens des aiguilles d'une montre, donnant l'impression d'une guirlande horizontale, bien que les fleurs partent toutes de la base. Le bassin présente un rondeau décoratif défini par trois filets linéaires contenant cinq bouquets de fleurs à pétales bleus et rouges. Six motifs abstraits bleus comblent les espaces restants.  
La forme de cette coupe rappelle certains modèles iraniens en métal et en céramique du VIIe siècle H (XIIIe siècle J.-C.) et la vaisselle des cours italiennes du XVe siècle (cf. une gravure de partie de cartes de Mantegna montrant un serviteur tenant une de ces coupes). À la cour ottomane, les coupes à couvercle de ce type étaient souvent en cuivre doré (*tombak*) et faisaient partie de la vaisselle de table.

À la cour ottomane, les coupes à couvercle de ce type étaient en cuivre doré (*tombak*) aussi bien qu’en céramique et faisaient partie de la vaisselle de table. Le style décoratif de celle-ci la classe dans un groupe de céramiques à décor floral datées du Xe siècle H (fin XVIe siècle J.-C.).
dates: Xe siècle de l’Hégire (fin XVIe siècle J.-C.).

en.name: *Shasha* reed bundle raft
description:
The *shasha* (reed boat) of the Iraqi marshlands is a type of raft constructed from reeds, using a bundle technique similar to that of architectural structures such as the *mudhif* (reed meeting-house). This ancient boat type exists around the world wherever there are wetlands.  
  
The simplest and smallest *shashas*– around 2-3 metres in length – were seen in the marshes until at least the AH 1390s / AD 1970s, typically made and used by children for play or fishing. The bundles were bound with cordage made from twisted strips of reed. Larger *shashas* may have used cordage of palm leaf or palm fibre (as does this reconstruction). They largely disappeared from use during the first half of the AH 14th / AD 20th century as the industrial era made wood more accessible to marsh dwellers; previously, only local elites could afford wooden boats, and reed boats of various types were far more common.  
  
Textual archaeological evidence suggests sea-going ships of Sumerian times used vast tonnages of reeds and of palm-fibre rope. There is much debate over their form and building technique. In AH 1397 / AD 1977, Thor Heyerdahl experimentally reconstructed a Sumerian ship based on a similar form to the *shasha*: the “Tigris”, measuring 18m x 6m, followed trade routes from Iraq across the Indian Ocean to Pakistan, then westward to Djibouti. Rashad Salim, who was among the crew, questions whether such craft could have carried cargo, as they lack a hold and have considerable drag even without additional weight. An alternative design for Sumerian trading ships could resemble the *zaima*, another marsh boat made of many narrow bundles of reeds connected in parallel to create the shell of a boat with a central hold.  
  
The *shasha* in the collection of the Open Museum for Water Culture (Basra) was built in AH 1443 / AD 2021 by a team of craftsmen skilled in reed architecture, as part of the Material Cultural Heritage Lab, where architecture students from Basra University studied traditional building techniques.
holder: Open Museum Initiative for Water Cultures
keywords: Watercraft; boat; basketry; transport.
materials: Reeds, palm fibre cordage; bundle construction.
partner: Open Museum Initiative for Water Cultures

en.name: Perpetual calendar
short_description: This perpetual calendar is contained within a cylindrical silver casing with a rounded shoulder. Four lateral knobs, two on either side, move the calendar's paper and textile elements, giving the month, the date and probably the day (this section is damaged). Above, a circular medallion contains the start year of the calendar, 1327 H/ 1909 AD.  The calendar is decorated all over with delicate niello deccoration. The front, with three superposed and elongated cartouche-shaped openings, is ornamented with a lobed panel containing naturalistic flower sprays. Below, a panel with three loop extensions contains an Arabic inscription - taqweem da'imi - that identifies the object's function. In the Tanzimat period, and up to 1926, the Mailya or Rumi calendar was introduced, which was based on the Julian solar calendar but started in the year of the Prophet's (pbuh) move from Makkah to Madina in 1 H/ 622 AD. It used old Syrian names for the months and was intended to ease the annual tax and fiscal calculations and payments.
holder: Sharjah Museum of Islamic Civilisation / Sharjah Museums Department

materials: Nielloed silver, copper alloy, iron, wood, printed paper, printed textile

ar.name: محمل

المحمل المعروض عبارة عن مقصورة خشبية مُثبّتة على أعمدة خشبية كبيرة مع أرضية منسوجة وسقف مُقوّس. فضلا عن ذلك، تتنوّع الزخارف المنقوشة لأستعراض مكانة السلطة الملكية .  
  
وحدهم الرجال من طوائف معينة أو الفيلة هم من باستطاعتهم حمل الهوادج التي تنقل أفراد العائلة الملكية في رحلات طويلة أو العرائس إلى حفلات الزفاف.عادة هذا النوع من المحمل يُغطى لستر الركاب من نظرات الغرباء، كما أنها تُشير إلى أن المستخدمين هم من علية القوم وأصحاب الثروات .  
  
في جميع أنحاء شبه الجزيرة العربية، يُطلق على المحمل اسم "هودج" الذي يحمل نساء البدو على ظهر الجمل، وغالبا ما يقع ذكره في أشعار قبيلة بنو مرّة. أما اليوم، فيمكن اعتبار المحمل بمثابة النسخة القديمة من السيارات المضادة للرصاص وذات الزجاج المُلوّن التي يركبها أفراد العائلة المالكة وحاشيتهم.

en.name: Palanquin
description:
The palanquin from India, a symbol of royal power, is comprised of a wooden compartment with a woven floor and roof resembling an arch or two oyster halves seated on large poles. Engraved decorations, various shapes and motifs enhance the carriage. Thin drapes protect from prying eyes and cover the fortune carried inside the carriage. Only men of certain castes or elephants were allowed to bear the palanquin transporting royals on long journeys and brides to their wedding ceremony.  
  
Across the Arabian Peninsula, palanquins receive the name *howdah* (*hawdaj*,) and carried Bedouin women on a camel’s back, frequently appearing in the poetry of the Murrah tribe. Since 1266, another variation called *mahmal* ceremonially transferred the cover of the Kaaba with the Egyptian pilgrimage to Mecca. Today, palanquins might be represented as the predecessors of bullet-proof cars with tinted windows, escorting royals and their entourage.

en.name: Epitaph Tablet for Anna Kun, wife of István Tárkányi
description: Wooden epitaphs are found in many 17th-century church interiors. The most wonderful examples are displayed still *in situ* in Csetnek and Lőcse (Levoča). The epitaph tablet of Anna Rozsályi Kun, wife of István Tárkányi, was made in the second quarter of the 17th century and acquired from the church of Kisszekeres, the burial place of the Rozsályi Kuns. It strongly resembles other wooden epitaphs originating from around the same time, as far as the composition, the architectonic design, and the decoration – both painted and sculptural – are concerned. On the painting in the central part of the epitaph, which is a little larger than the usual size, we see Anna Kun wearing a widow's dress under the cross, the Tree of Redemption, accompanied by both of her husbands as well as the children from both marriages. The frame is decorated with dynamically designed herm pilasters and harmoniously coloured openwork carvings with elements of the so-called “pinna” or “cartilage” style. Similar combinations of motifs (that originate from Silesia) are seen on contemporary altars, choir-screens, pulpits and organs. It is not inconceivable that the master who made the Tárkányi epitaph also helped to decorate the interior of the Church of St. Jacob in Lőcse (Levoča), for the sharply defined features of the herms decorating the frame on both sides, as well as the grotesque grimace of the cherub above the carving, all derive from the herms decorating the steps to the pulpit in the Church of St. Jacob.

The high points of epitaph tablets, which are mainly found in Protestant churches, are the rich wood carving and colourful painting. The person who commissioned this epitaph can be identified by the inscription.
type: Painting woodwork of the carved frame
place: Tárkányi family in Kisszekeres , placed in the Reformed Church in Kisszekeres
artist: Workshop in Upper Hungary, artist unknown
keywords: Funerary object; epitaph; Counter-Reformation; Lutherans; Protestants; costume; Anna Rozsályi Kun; Upper Hungary; Lőcse; Levoča; funerary inscription; wood; gilding; painting

en.name: Centerpiece
description: This piece is colourless cut crystal glass with a tall stem and oval-shaped, shallow, polygonal-cut bowl with a slightly corrugated wall. It is from the Series Strnad, AD 1910: In AD 1909, the architect Oskar Strnad started teaching at the School of Arts and Crafts. After 1910, he also worked for Lobmeyr (a pioneering glass manufacturing house in Austrian /Bohemian crystal production), with whom he remained in close contact until his death. This colourless cut crystal glass is one of the first designs Strnad created for Lobmeyr, using thick-walled crystal glass. The designs are simple and created by means of sharply cut edges. For the jars especially he sketched out variations of painting or cutting surface designs. These artworks by Strnad were part of a series applying “rock crystal-like cutting”. Some of them were presented at the Exhibition of Works from the Austrian Arts Industry in the Museum of Art and Industry in AD 1910/11. According to Fischel, "New paths have been broken in crystal cutting. Mr. F. Alber, O. Hofner, P. Philipp, A. Horvath and Professor Strnad were active here. They succeeded in combining elegant lines and delicate modelling in such a way that an extremely noble effect was achieved on some beautiful pieces. the high gloss of the water-bright, polished crystal comes into its own best when the softly curved surface supports it." see: H. Fischel in KKH.
artist: Strnad, Oskar (design); Meyr's Neffe (manufacturer); J. & L. Lobmeyr (client / customer)
partner: MAK – Austrian Museum of Applied Arts / Contemporary Art

en.name: Namban Oratory
description:
This rectangular oratory surmounted by a triangular pediment with the monogram *IHS* (the abbreviation of the Greek *IHSOUS*, or JESUS) located at the centre, has two side-panels enclosing a painting of the Virgin Mary holding the infant Jesus. Although the lacquer decoration presents a predominantly Japanese ornamental grammar – especially a floral one – both its form and the iconography embody Christian cultural references. The pictorial image is itself an example of the possible interaction between the Jesuit painting school – operating in Japan since the 1580s – and the Japanese pupils that quickly demonstrated skill in Western-style painting.  
As it is, such a hybrid object, that crosses different artistic backgrounds, could only have been made during the Portuguese presence in Japan, during the period spanning approximately 1549 to 1640.  
The oratory is mentioned in the *Inventário Artístico de Santarém* (Santarém Artistic Inventory) as Indo-Portuguese lacquer work. Such misinformation reveals how, in the middle of the 20th century, such an item was unfamiliar to the European public in general, but that was not the case in the late 16th and beginning of the 17th century, at least not for the Portuguese elite. Such a statement can only be based on the remaining objects – with or without associated painting – the number of which has expanded increasingly during the last three decades (this example did not come to light until 1985). A fact that also draws attention to the demands of the Iberian market for these objects at the time.  
The Sardoal Oratory has the particularity of being associated with a religious space, thanks to an inscription located on the altar of Nossa Senhora da Esperança in the Church of Nossa Senhora da Caridade. This text, dated 1670, is the earliest known reference in Portugal to a reminiscent *Namban* object.
A lacquered *Namban* oratory with a floral design in gold and silver powder (*maki-e)* and mother of pearl inlay (*raden*) with a painting of the Virgin Mary holding the infant Jesus.
holder: Sardoal's Holy House of Mercy, Sardoal
place: Convent of Santa Maria da Caridade, Sardoal
keywords: Lacquer ware; *urushi*; Jesuit; Jesuit school of painting; religious furnishing; inlay; floral decoration
materials: Painting: oil on copper; frame: wood, lacquer (*urushi*), gold powder, silver powder (*maki-e*), copper and mother of pearl inlay (*raden*)
tags: frame: wood, lacquer (urushi), gold powder, silver powder (maki-e), copper and mother of pearl inlay (raden)

pt.name: *Oratório Namban*
description:
Oratório rectangular, sobrepujado por frontão triangular em que se inscreve o monograma IHS, no centro, com duas portas, por detrás das quais se encontra uma pintura com a representação da Virgem com o Menino.  
Apesar da decoração em laca apontar para uma gramática decorativa essencialmente japonesa, sobretudo de carácter vegetalista, tanto a forma como a iconografia da pintura remetem para referências essencialmente cristãs. A imagem pictórica é, em si mesma, um exemplo da possível interacção entre o seminário de pintura jesuíta, que funcionou no Japão a partir da década de 1580, e os alunos nipónicos que rapidamente demonstraram uma apetência especial na cópia de modelos e técnicas da pintura ocidental.  
Deste ponto de vista, um objecto artístico com estas características sincréticas só poderia ter surgido no contexto da presença portuguesa no Japão durante o período balizado entre 1549 (estabelecimento da primeira missão jesuíta no Japão) e 1640 (ano do banimento dos portugueses do arquipélago).  
A peça é referida no *Inventário Artístico de Santarém* como um oratório indo-português, uma informação errónea que demonstra até que ponto, em meados do século XX, os objectos *namban* continuavam a ser pouco conhecidos, o que não acontecia, certamente, em finais do século XVI e início do século XVII, pelo menos para uma elite portuguesa, como o prova a descoberta de uma série de oratórios deste tipo, com ou sem pintura associada, ao longo das últimas três décadas (este exemplar foi revelado pela primeira vez em 1985), facto que aponta também para o dinamismo do mercado ibérico na procura de uma produção específica.  
O oratório do Sardoal apresenta a particularidade de estar associado a um espaço religioso, como o atesta a inscrição localizada no altar de Nossa Senhora da Esperança, na igreja de Nossa Senhora da Caridade. O texto, datado de 1670, é a mais antiga referência que se conhece em Portugal associada a uma peça *namban*.

Oratório *namban* lacado com desenhos florais em *maki-e* (pó de ouro e de prata polvilhado sobre a superfície) e *raden* (incrustação de madre-pérola), com pintura inclusa representando a Virgem com o Menino.
holder: Santa Casa da Misericórdia do Sardoal.
keywords: *Namban*; laca; *urushi;* seminário de pintura jesuíta; Sardoal
materials: Madeira, laca (*urishi*), pó de ouro, pó de prata, cobre, incrustação de madre-pérola.
tags: Madeira, laca (urishi), pó de ouro, pó de prata, cobre, incrustação de madre-pérola.
