cs.name: Zámek Kunín
description: Jednoduchá podélná stavba vyniká především členěním fasády a dekorativními prvky. Jednotný koncept architekta realizovala řada umělců a řemeslníků. R. 1733 byl v zámecké kapli instalován dnes nezvěstný oltář, který byl vytvořen opět podle Hildebrandtova návrhu malířem Johannem Georgem Schmidtem a sochařem Tobiasem Krackerem.

Stavba zámku byla inspirována architekturou, kterou přední rakouský architekt Hildebrandt vytvořil pro knížete-arcibiskupa Franze Antona Harracha a jeho letní palác Mirabell v Salcburku. Reprezentativní průčelí zámku zde však nemělo demonstrovat sílu a bohatství hraběcí rodiny, jako spíše navodit atmosféru klidného, příležitostného venkovského sídla členky rodu, jehož příslušníci byli svými úřady spojeni s největšími metropolemi tehdejší Evropy. Pozoruhodností zámku jsou Hildebrandtovo hlavní schodiště a zcela unikátní barokní komínové systémy.
artist:
Hraběnka Marie Eleonora z Harrachu, rozená princezna z Liechtenštejna (1702–1757), Marie Walburga z Truchsess-Waldburg-Zeilu, rozená z Harrach-Hohenemsu (1762–1828), Friedrich Emil Schindler (1828–1870), landkrabě Ernst Egon z Fürstenberka (1816–1889), Josef Friedrich z Fürstenberka (do 1895),  
Dr. Viktor rytíř Bauer (1876–1939)

Johann Lucas von Hildebrandt (1668 Janov – 1745 Vídeň), Johan Georg Schmidt,  
zv. Wiener-Schmidt (1685 Čechy – 1765 Vídeň), Tobias Kracker (1658 Vídeň – 1736 Vídeň)
history: Zámek vznikl radikální přestavbou jednopatrové patrně renesanční tvrze pro manželku předního císařského diplomata a státníka Friedricha Augusta hraběte Harracha. Největšího rozkvětu se dočkal na přelomu 18. a 19. století za osvícené majitelky Marie Walburgy, která zde ve styku s brněnskými zednáři a ilumináty vybudovala filantropium – jeden z nejmodernějších vzdělávacích ústavů tehdejší střední Evropy. Jeho nejznámějším žákem byl pozdější “Otec národa”, historik František Palacký. Mimo jiné podnikla hraběnka na svém panství první očkování dětí na Moravě. Posledním majitelem byl dr. Viktor Bauer z Brna. Pro něj měl vytvořit novou instalaci zámku Adolf Loos. Zámek byl zcela zdevastován sovětskou armádou r. 1945. Později sloužil jako sklad a ubytovna. Po rozsáhlé rekonstrukci se do něj díky ochotě předchozích majitelů vracejí původní zámecké sbírky.

en.name: Kunín Chateau
description: The simple longitudinal building features a segmented frontage with decorative elements. The architect’s unified concept was executed by a number of artists and craftsmen. In 1733 an altar (now lost) was installed in the chateau chapel. The altar was designed by Hildebrandt and created by the painter Johann Georg Schmidt and the sculptor Tobias Kracker.

The chateau building was inspired by constructions created by the leading Austrian architect, Hildebrandt, for Count Archbishop Franz Anton Harrach, and was especially influenced by the Mirabell summer palace in Salzburg. The spectacular frontage of the Kunín Chateau was not, however, intended to demonstrate the power and wealth of its aristocratic owners, but was designed to induce the peaceful atmosphere of a country house for a family whose members held offices associated with the largest metropolises of Europe. The chateau features a remarkable staircase that Hildebrandt designed and unique Baroque chimneys.
artist: Countess Marie Eleonora of Harrach, née Princess Liechtenstein (1702–1757), Marie Walburga of Truchsess-Waldburg-Zeil, née Harrach-Hohenems (1762–1828), Friedrich Emil Schindler (1828–1870), Ernst Egon of Fürstenberk (1816–1889), Josef Friedrich of Fürstenberk (until 1895), Dr. Viktor Knight Bauer (1876–1939)
Johann Lucas von Hildebrandt (1668 Genoa – 1745 Vienna), Johan Georg Schmidt (1685 in Bohemia – 1748 Krems) Tobias Kracker (1658 – 1736, Vienna)
history: The chateau came into existence through a radical reconstruction of a single-floor Renaissance fortress, undertaken for the wife of Friedrich August Count Harrach, a major imperial diplomat and politician. The chateau had its heyday at the turn of the 18th century, when it was owned by the enlightened Marie Walburga who, with the assistance of Brno stonemasons and illuminati, established a “*philantropium*” in the chateau, one of the most advanced educational institutions in Central Europe at the time. Its most famous student was the historian František Palacký, “Father of the Czech Nation”. Among other things, the countess initiated Moravia's first vaccination programme for children in her demesne. The last owner was Dr. Viktor Bauer from Brno, who chose Adolf Loos to design a reconstruction of the chateau, but whose plans were thwarted by the Second World War. The chateau was completely ruined by the Soviet army in 1945 and later served as a warehouse and hostel. After an extensive overhaul, original art collections are being installed in the chateau thanks to the helpfulness of the former owners.

de.name: Kanzel
description: Schönes Beispiel einer frühklassizistischen Kanzel in strengen, kaum mehr ornamentalisierten Formen. Auf ein Bildprogramm ist hier verzichtet. Statt barocker Rhetorik – die auch vom Prediger nicht mehr erwartet wird – soll die Kanzel den würdigen Rahmen einer erbaulichen Rede an die Gläubigen bilden. Den Entwurf lieferten Hagenauer und Nesselthaler, die Ausführung besorgte der aus Thannheim in Tirol stammende Peter Pflauder, ein Stuckateur und Altarkistler.

en.name: Pulpit
description: A beautiful example of an Early Classicist pulpit in austere forms virtually without ornamentation or pictorial programme. Instead of Baroque rhetoric—which was no longer expected of the preacher—the pulpit was designed to provide a dignified frame for an edifying sermon. The design originates from Hagenauer and Nesselthaler and was executed by Peter Pflauder, a stucco mason and altar carpenter from Thannheim in Tyrol.

en.name: Coffee Cup Holder
description: The rim is decorated with filigree. There are three coats of arms on it. There is a row of coral ornaments on the rim and triangular coral ornaments between the crests.
holder: The Republic of Türkiye Ministry of Culture and Tourism

ar.name: لوحة زلّيج (قاشاني) على شكل لوحة جبهة.
description: لوحة من الزليج (القاشاني المغربي،*azulejos* ) زُخرفت بالأزرق والفيروزي والأخضر والأحمر. تمت إحاطة التكوين المركزي بلفائف من السحب المجردة التي تشكل شريطاً ثعباني الشكل يحيط، ضمن إطار ثلاثي الفصوص، بزهرة لوتس. تمتد أغصانٌ على شكل حلزوني انطلاقاً من الشكل المركزي نحو الأوراق وبراعم الزهور وأشكال الهاتاي hatayi (أكاليل من الزهور المستوحاة من الصين). وعلى الرغم من أن لوحات الزلّيج في العمارة العثمانية مخصصة لتزيين الفراغات الداخلية، فإن مصدر هذه اللوحة لم يتأكد بعد، لكن من الأكيد أنها تنتمي إلى مجموعة من اثنتي عشر لوحة جبهية، متشابهة تقريباً،ً كانت تزين بناءاً تم تشييده بأمر من بيال باشا، رئيس الإمارة وأحد المقربين من السلطان سليم الثاني. لكن شكاً يتعلق بغائية البناء يبقى قائما: هل كان مسجداً أم قصراً؟ وحسب الرأي الشائع، فإن هذه اللوحات قد انتزعت من مسجد بيال باشا (اسطنبول) الذي بناه سنان في عام 980 – 981 هجري / 1573 – 1574 ميلادية، وهو مايؤكده اختفاء مجمل لوحات جبهة البناء وحفظ المحراب وحده.
كانت هذه اللوحة الزليجية تنتمي إلى مسجد بيال، باشا مدينة إسطنبول. تهيمن على القطعة أشكال نباتية؛ وأُطرَ الترتيبُ المركزي بسُحُبٍ مبسطة تشكلُ شريطا يحيط بزهرة لوتس، تنطلق منها أشكال أخرى نباتية.

en.name: Tile panel in the shape of a tympanum.
description:
Panel of glazed tiles decorated in blue, turquoise, green and yellow. The central composition is framed by scrolls of stylised clouds forming a serpentine band which encloses a lotus flower in a trefoil knot. Unfurling in a spiral from the central motif are slender boughs with leaves, flower buds and *hatayi*\-style motifs (garlands of flowers of Chinese inspiration). In Ottoman architecture panels of tiles were used mainly to decorate interior rooms.  
It has been claimed that this panel belongs to a set of around twelve almost identical tympana, which decorated a building commissioned to be built by Piyale Pasa, Lord of the Admiralty and protégé of Sultan Selim II. There was some doubt as to which building this might be: the mosque or the palace. The most widely held view is that the panels were removed from the Mosque of Piyale Pasa in Istanbul, probably built by the architect Sinan in AH 980–1 / AD 1573–4, since all the tympana disappeared and only the *mihrab* (prayer niche) remains.

This tile panel belonged to the Piyale Pasa Mosque in Istanbul. The piece is dominated by plant motifs. The central composition is framed by stylised clouds forming a strip enclosing a lotus flower, from where other plant motifs are developed.

es.name: Panel de azulejos en forma de tímpano.
description:
Panel de azulejos decorado en azul, turquesa, verde y rojo. La composición central está articulada por un roleo de nubes estilizadas en una cinta serpentiforme que encierra, en un lazo trilobulado, una flor de loto. A partir del motivo central se desarrollan en espiral ramas delgadas con hojas, capullos de flor y motivos *hatayi* (festones de flores de inspiración china).  
En la arquitectura otomana, los paneles de azulejos decoraban principalmente espacios interiores. Aunque la proveniencia de este panel no está confirmada, se afirma que pertenece a un conjunto de unos 12 tímpanos casi idénticos que decoraban un edificio mandado construir por Piyale Pasa, jefe del almirantazgo y protegido del sultán Selim II. La duda reside en saber si el edificio era una mezquita o un palacio. La opinión más generalizada sostiene que los paneles fueron retirados de la mezquita de Piyale Pasa en Estambul, construida probablemente por Sinan en 980-981 / 1573-1574, ya que todos los tímpanos desaparecieron y sólo queda el mihrab.

Panel de azulejos que probablemente decoró la mezquita de Piyale Pasa en Estambul. En él predominan los motivos vegetales, articulados en la composición central por una cinta de nubes estilizadas que encierra una flor de loto.
dates: Hacia 980 de la Hégira / 1573 d. C.
keywords: Lazo trilobulado; loto; hatayi.

fr.name: Panneau d’azulejos en forme de tympan.
description: Panneau d'*azulejos* décoré en bleu, turquoise, vert et rouge. La composition centrale est encadrée par des enroulements de nuages stylisés formant un ruban serpentiforme qui entoure, dans un enlacement trilobé, une fleur de lotus. À partir du motif central se développent en spirale de fines branches aux feuilles, aux boutons de fleurs et aux motifs *hatayi* (festons de fleurs d'inspiration chinoise). Bien que, dans l'architecture ottomane, les panneaux d'*azulejos* décorent essentiellement des espaces intérieurs, la provenance de ce panneau n'est pas encore confirmée mais il est certain qu'il appartient à un ensemble d'environ douze tympans presque identiques, qui décoraient un édifice construit sur ordre de Piyale Pacha, chef de l'amirauté et protégé du sultan Sélim II. Une incertitude concerne la finalité de l'édifice : mosquée ou palais ? Selon une opinion répandue, ces panneaux auraient été retirés de la mosquée de Piyale Pacha (Istanbul), bâtie probablement par Sinan en 980-981 H / 1573-1574 J.-C., ce que confirme la disparition de la totalité des tympans et la conservation du seul *mihrab*.

Ce panneau d'*azulejos* appartenait à la mosquée Piyale Pacha d'Istanbul. La pièce est dominée par des motifs végétaux. La composition centrale est encadrée par des nuages stylisés formant un ruban qui entoure une fleur de lotus, d'où s'échappent d'autres motifs phytomorphes.

pt.name: Painel de azulejos em forma de tímpano.
description: Painel de azulejos decorado a azul, turquesa, verde e vermelho. A composição central está emoldurada por enrolamentos de nuvens estilizadas formando uma fita serpentiforme que encerra, num laço trilobado, uma flor de lótus. A partir do motivo central, desenvolvem-se em espiral ramos delgados com folhas, flores em botão e motivos *hatayi* (festões de flores de inspiração chinesa). Na arquitectura otomana os painéis de azulejos decoravam principalmente espaços interiores, no entanto, a proveniência deste painel ainda não está confirmada mas afirma-se que pertence a um conjunto de cerca de doze tímpanos, quase idênticos, e que decoravam um edifício mandado construir por Piyale Pacha, chefe do almirantado e protegido do sultão Selim II. A dúvida reside em se saber que edifício seria esse: a mesquita ou o palácio. A opinião mais generalizada defende que os painéis foram retirados da mesquita de Piyale Pacha em Istambul, construída provavelmente por Sinan, em 980-981 AH / 1573-1574 AD, visto que todos os tímpanos desapareceram e apenas resta o *mihrab*.

Painel de azulejos (c. 980 AH / c. 1573 AD) que terá pertencido à mesquita de Piyale Pacha em Istambul. Os motivos vegetais predominam: a composição central está emoldurada por nuvens estilizadas formando uma fita que encerra uma flor de lótus. A partir daí, desenvolvem-se outros temas fitomórficos.

cs.name: Kartuziánský klášter a kostel Nejsvětější Trojice, Brno-Královo Pole
description: Motty koncepce kláštera byly askeze a kontemplace. Fasádu jednolodní stavby se sochami sv. Jana Křtitele, patrona kartuziánů, a sv. Bruna, zakladatele řádu, sousoším Nejsvětější Trojice se štítem CT (Cella Trinitatis), znakem kartouzy, vytvořil O. Schweigl. Chrámová loď a dvě boční kaple si zachovaly původní gotické rysy. Chórové lavice z počátku 17. století patří mezi nejvzácnější na Moravě. Sochařská výzdoba oltářů pochází od O. Schweigla (1763), na hl. oltáři jde o sv. Jana Křtitele a sv. Bruna. Obraz je novodobou kopií skicy J. Sterna. Tzv. Švédská kaple na severní straně s freskou Oslava Nejsv. Trojice je uzavřena, jakož i vchodové dveře do chrámu, bohatě zdobenou rokokovou mříží. Protože u kartuziánů byla chrámová hudba vyloučena a charakteristickým prvkem obřadu byl gregoriánský zpěv, byla kruchta vestavěna až dodatečně (1903). Uprostřed velkého ambitu se nachází refektář se štukovou výzdobou (G. A. Corbellini), v patře byla knihovna.

Jediný dochovaný kartuziánský komplex na Moravě byl založen moravským markrabětem. Motty řádu byly askeze a kontemplace. Na barokní přestavbě kláštera se podíleli přední umělci z okruhu vídeňské akademie. Prior A. Gottfried patřil mezi významné sběratele a představitele osvícenské společnosti v Brně. Interiér dotvářejí fresky zobrazují zjevení – anděly jako Boží posly vystupující ve scénách ze Starého a Nového zákona jako sny, zjevení a zvěstování, oslavu církve a řádu ve smyslu historie, exempla a vize. R. 1782 byl klášter v rámci josefínských reforem zrušen.
artist: Jan Jindřich Lucemburský (+ 1375), Prokop Lucemburský (+ 1405) Jošt Lucemburský (+ 1411); Řád kartuziánů, Athanasius Gottfried (1738 Polná – 1814 Brno)

Ondřej Schweigl (1735 Brno – 1812 Brno), Franz Anton Maulbertsch (1724 Langenargen am Bodensee – 1796 Vídeň), Felix Ivo Leicher (1727 Bílovec – 1812 Vídeň), Josef Stern (1716 Štýrský Hradec – 1775 Brno), Martin Johann Schmidt (Kremser-Schmidt) (1718 Grafenwörth – 1801 Stein an der Donau), Bartolomeus Zindtner, Mořic Grimm (1669 Achdorf – 1757 Brno), Giacomo Antonio Corbellini
history: Zakladatelem kláštera byl moravský markrabě Jan Jindřich, bratr českého krále a císaře Karla IV. Klášter mimo městské hradby býval často poškozen válečnými událostmi. Po řadě oprav získal svou dnešní podobu barokní přestavbou celého areálu, na níž se podíleli zejména umělci z okruhu vídeňské akademie. Prior A. Gottfried patřil mezí významné sběratele a představitele osvícenské společnosti v Brně. R. 1782 byl klášter, jako mnoho dalších, „jež žádných škol neb nemocnic nevydržují, nebo jejichž členové nezastávají úřad kazatelský a kněžský, anebo nevynikají studiemi“ zrušen Josefem II. , určen pro využití vojskem a upraven zejména v letech 1871–1877. Vojáci objekty obývali do konce roku 1963, kdy klášter převzalo Vysoké učení technické v Brně.

en.name: Carthusian Monastery and the Church of The Holy Trinity, Brno-Královo Pole
names: Carthusian Monastery and the Church of the Holy Trinity, Brno-Královo Pole
description:
The Carthusian order was dedicated to asceticism and contemplation. The frontage of the single-nave building with statues of St. John the Baptist, Patron Saint of the Carthusians, St. Bruno, founder of the order, a sculpture of the Holy Trinity and the shield with CT (*Cella Trinitatis*), the symbol of the monastery, are by O. Schweigl. The nave and two side chapels have preserved their original Gothic appearance. The gallery pews, from the early 17th century, are among the most precious in Moravia. The sculpted decoration of the altars was created by O. Schweigl (1763); the high altar features St. John the Baptist and St. Bruno. The altarpiece holds a replica of the sketch by J. Stern, *The Celebration of the Holy Trinity*. The entrance door to the church is secured by a richly ornamented rococo grid.  
As instrumental music was excluded from Carthusian masses Gregorian chant was a characteristic part of the service. A gallery was added later in 1903. In the middle of a large cloister is a refectory with stucco decoration by G. A. Corbellini. There was once a library on the first floor.

This monastery, the only preserved Carthusian complex in Moravia, was founded by a Moravian margrave. The order was dedicated to asceticism and contemplation and leading artists from the Vienna Academy participated in its Baroque reconstruction. Prior A. Gottfried was a renowned art collector and exponent of the Enlightenment in Brno. The interior is adorned with frescos featuring revelations: angels as God’s messengers in mystical scenes from the Old and New Testaments. The monastery was dissolved in 1782 as part of religious reforms undertaken by Joseph II.
artist: Jan Jindřich of Luxembourg (d. 1375), Prokop of Luxembourg (d. 1405) Jošt of Luxembourg (d. 1411); Carthusian order, Athanasius Gottfried (1738 Polná – 1814 Brno)

Ondřej Schweigl (1735–1812, Brno), Franz Anton Maulbertsch (1724 Langenargen am Bodensee – 1796 Vienna), Felix Ivo Leicher (1727 Bílovec – 1812 Vienna), Josef Stern (1716 Graz – 1775 Brno), Martin Johann Schmidt (Kremser-Schmidt), Bartolomeus Zindtner, Mořic Grimm (1669 Achdorf – 1757 Brno), Giacomo Antonio Corbellini
history: The monastery was founded by Moravian margrave, Jan Jindřich, brother of the Czech King and Emperor Charles IV. The monastery, situated outside the town walls, suffered damage in several successive wars. It acquired its present appearance through a Baroque reconstruction of the whole complex following a number of minor repairs. Leading artists from the Vienna Academy participated in the reconstruction. Abbot A. Gottfried was a renowned art collector and exponent of the Enlightenment in Brno. The monastery was dissolved in 1782 as part of the religious reforms undertaken by Joseph II and was among many others that “[did] not support schools or hospitals, and whose members [did] not hold positions as preachers or priests”. The monastery was commissioned for military purposes and rebuilt, in particular in 1871–1877. Soldiers used the premises until the end of 1963 when the monastery was taken over by the Technical University of Brno.

en.name: Frontal with St. Alexander pope
description:
This frontal originally decorated the front of the former altar in the church of Vergiano. It is a good example of the art of scagliola, a technique of using plaster to create imitation marble or stone. This method was invented in Emilia, in Carpi, a small town near Modena, at the beginning of the seventeenth century.  
The art of scagliola is very old. In antiquity it was common to decorate surfaces in order to imitate marble, but examples of decorations made of plaster powder imitating marble start only from the sixteenth-century. Scagliola is a cheaper technique compared to precious stone inlaid. For this reason and for its rapidity of execution it soon became very popular. This explains the ample presence of scagliola artefacts in Italy made exclusively for churches and mostly altar frontals. Guido Fassi (1584–1649), an architect and engineer from Carpi, was the first to employ this technique for altar frames. Later his collaborators and pupils painted on the scagliola surface first, then imitated stone inlay thus creating in Carpi the first Italian school of scagliola.  
The artist who made this frontal, Carlo Antonio Bini, is a member of this school. He employs the typical decorative naturalistic patterns (flower wreaths, small birds, fantastic creatures) against a black background. In the middle Pope St. Alexander I is kneeling in front of a monstrance, wearing a cope.

This altar frontal represents St. Alexander pope kneeling in front of the Eucharist. Against a black background one can see the naturalistic patterns (flower wreaths, small birds, fantastic creatures).
keywords: Antependium; St. Alexander pope; Scagliola; floral decoration; animal decoration; imaginary animal; zoomorphic imagery

it.name: Paliotto con Sant’Alessandro Papa
description:
Questo paliotto, che decorava il fronte dell'antico altare della chiesa di Vergiano, è un tipico e felice esempio dell'arte della scagliola, nata in area emiliana, a Carpi (Modena), all'inizio del XVII secolo.  
L'arte della scagliola ha origini remote poiché fin dall'antichità era frequente decorare superfici a imitazione del marmo, ma l'utilizzo della polvere di gesso mescolata a fingere il marmo e abbinata ad una tecnica ad intarsio è documentata solo a partire dal XVI sec. Si tratta di una tecnica più economica rispetto al commesso di pietre dure ma il successo della scagliola fu determinato, oltre che dalla sua economicità, dalla velocità di esecuzione delle opere. Per questi motivi si spiega l'ampia diffusione di manufatti di scagliola in Italia. La committenza è quasi esclusivamente religiosa ed in particolare le richieste riguardano proprio i paliotti d'altare. Guido Fassi (1584–1649), architetto e ingegnere di Carpi, per primo applicò questa tecnica alla realizzazione di cornici per altare. Furono i suoi collaboratori e allievi ad utilizzare il piano di scagliola come base per dipingere immagini prima e come imitazione del commesso per paliotti poi, dando vita alla prima scuola italiana di scagliola, quella carpigiana.  
L'artista che firma il paliotto di Sant'Alessandro, Carlo Antonio Bini, è riconducibile a questa scuola di cui ripercorre i motivi ornamentali, basati sulla rappresentazione naturalistica su sfondo nero di ghirlande di fiori, arricchite da virtuose rappresentazioni di uccellini e animali fantastici. Al centro è raffigurato Sant'Alessandro Papa, inginocchiato, vestito con il piviale, mentre prega di fronte all'ostensorio.
Questo paliotto rappresneta S. Alessandro papa in ginocchio davanti all'eucaristia. Contro un fondo nero compaiono dettagli naturalistici (corone di fiori, piccoli uccelli, creature fantastiche).
keywords: S. Alessandro papa; Scagliola; decorazione floreale; decorazione con animali; animale immaginario; immaginario zoomorfico

cs.name: Oltář sv. Kříže
description: Štuková výzdoba oltářů a kazatelny je dílem předního brněnského sochaře, činného dříve v Olomouci. Zachycení duševního hnutí postav, nedramatická gesta, měkce plastický tvar a prostorová koncepce sousoší zvyšují účinek epicky podané scény. Dílo sochaře, jenž vytvořil řadu oltářů v Brně i okolí, se vyznačuje reprezentativní formou, vycházející z italského (Bernini) a vídeňského sochařství (Donner). Ve štuku byl ovlivněn zejména B. Fontanou.

en.name: Altar of the Holy Cross
description: The stucco decoration of the altars and the pulpit was created by a prominent Brno artist, previously active in Olomouc. The way in which the artist approaches the spiritual movement of the figures, the non-dramatic gestures, the soft relief shapes and the spatial concept of the sculpture, enhance the effect of an epic scene. The sculptor’s oeuvre includes many altarpieces in Brno and its surroundings, typified by a spectacular form derived from Italian (Bernini) and Viennese (Donner) sculpture. The artist’s stucco work was particularly influenced by B. Fontana.

en.name: *Academia Poetica qve Dedica ala Catholica Magestad de la Reyna Madre Nvestra Senora Dona Maria Ana De Austria La Academia literaria de Valencia con Los assumptos del sitio y torna de Buda Celebrada …*
description:
The *Academia Poetica* *…* is a compilation of literary pieces that were read to the assembly of Academia Literaria de Valencia on 13 October 1686 in Valencia to commemorate the recapture of Buda from the Turks.  
A poetry competition was announced by the Academia Literaria de Valencia in 1686, and *Academia Poetica* *…* contains all the works from the competition. The enthusiasm that spread all over Christian Europe, the importance of the event and the crusade-like feature of the recapture of Buda from the Turks in 1686, were perhaps why such a great number of poetic and epic pieces of literature glorified the event. Most of the works compiled here were read to the festive assemblies of contemporary literary academies, and some of them were published in printed form. The poems glorify Pope Innocent XI, the Emperor Leopold I Habsburg, members of the Sacra Lega, the chief commanders, Charles Duke V of Lorraine and Maximilian II Emanuel the Bavarian Elector, the soldiers, the glorious siege and the decisive day of recapture on 2 September 1686 and the new cardinals nominated on the same day. This beautifully decorated piece is a rare example of illuminated, hand-written literature.

The *Academia Poetica* … is a compilation of literary pieces that were read to the Assembly of Academia Literaria de Valencia on the on 13 October 1686 in Valencia commemorating the recapture of Buda. A rare example of an illuminated literary document that commemorates the recapture of Buda and a festive event.

en.name: Ford Model T Truck
description:
This extraordinary truck popularised the American movie-snack-popcorn. The Columbia Buddy Company customised one of three Ford T-Model to become a popcorn-machine and vending machine on wheels.  
  
Aside from fresh-buttered popcorn fried with the original Cretors popcorn equipment, this crimson red carriage would sell ice-cold sodas and hot-roasted peanuts.  
  
Although special purpose vehicles were not an unknown concept, as T-Models were also transformed into ambulances and fire trucks, the popcorn wagon presented a unique marketing and entertainment opportunity with its charming circus aesthetic.

en.name: Village of Qara
description: Located 15 km north of Nebek, on the left side of the highway – requiring a detour – is the town of Qara with some striking examples of late antique and medieval Christian architecture. The Church of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, today Greek Orthodox, is located on Omar al-Mukhtar Street, one street before the main town square. It holds some beautiful fresco paintings from the 6th/11th century that are very similar to those of Mar Musa. The nearby mosque with the striking portal in the town centre is a converted Basilica. The remains of Qara Monastery, now heavily renovated, lies 2 km west of the town and includes 7th-/13th-century frescos.

en.name: ‘Attarin Suq
description:
As well as *funduq*s, Fez possessed markets, *suq*s, whose reputation extended far beyond the town walls. The *qaysariya*, a term signifying a commercial neighbourhood, which was situated at the heart of the Qarawiyin Quarter, with its numerous *suq*s and shops, is one of the oldest of its kind, offering goods imported from Europe and the East ever since the Middle Ages.  
Destroyed at first by a great fire in 724/1324, and then by floods in 725/1325, the *qaysariya*, with its thousands of terraced houses, was then rebuilt. The ‘Attarin Suq, one of the most reputable in the *qaysariya*, occupies the length of a long street which links up to the Merinid *madrasa* of the same name, at *Bab al-Faraj*. Complemented by trade on adjacent streets and places, this market extends over more than 600 m. and was equipped with a large gate at each end, whose “*guardians*”, wrote Leon the African, “*do their rounds at night, with dogs, with weapons, holding up lanterns in their hands. They were paid by the traders themselves*”.  
The *suq*, according to Leon the African, consisted of 150 stalls, which grew in number to 170 a few years later according to the Portuguese historian Mármol de Carvajal (16th century). Originally specialising in the sale of medicinal products and groceries, medicinal stalls stood shoulder to shoulder with hardware stalls which were distinct for the opulence of their ornamentation. Doctors themselves made up the medicinal preparations, and then sent them to specialised stalls where staff would dispense them under medical supervision.  
In the 10th/16th century, the *suq*, through the importance it had gained in terms of the geographical area it fulfilled, through the number of important shops it represented and through the abundance of specialised products it sold, was unrivalled. Even if the *suq* of today has lost a little of its identity through the growth of product variety, one can still find some traditional hardware sellers who are living examples of this market, typical of its kind.

en.name: 'Funeral Procession'
description: This illustration is associated with a story related by the hoopoe as a response to a bird who complains about his fear of death. In the story, a son grieves the death of his father in front of his coffin and a sufi soothes him, explaining that his father had experienced much pain and that no one can avoid death. Here, the painter depicts the incident as occurring in front of a cemetery gate. The scene behind the gate is replete with motifs that are irrelevant to the story itself. The viewer at the court may have enjoyed deciphering them.

en.name: The Hijaz Railway Delegations
short_description: The Hijaz Railway ran from Damascus to Medina, through the Hijaz region of Saudi Arabia, with a branch line to Haifa on the Mediterranean Sea. It was a part of the Ottoman railway network and was built to extend the line from the Haydarpaşa Terminal in Istanbul beyond Damascus to the holy city of Mecca. The main purpose of the railway was to establish a connection between the capital of the Ottoman Empire and the seat of the Islamic Caliphate, and Hijaz in Arabia, the site of the holiest shrines of Islam and the holy city of Mecca, the destination of the Hajj annual pilgrimage. Another important reason was to improve the economic and political integration of the distant Arabian provinces into the Ottoman state, and to facilitate the transportation of military forces.
holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
dates: Late 19th century – beginning of the 20th century
keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph The Hijaz Railways
partner: Ministry of Culture and Tourism (General Directorate for Cultural Heritage and Museums)

en.name: *St. Joseph with Jesus and St. John the Baptist*
description: In Croatia and especially in the north, there are a large number of works of the Slovene painter, Valentin Metzinger. An eclectic and accomplished painter, he was inspired by the works of the Bolognese artists Annibale Carracci and Guido Reni, and the paintings of the Venetian Mannerists. From the time of Metzinger’s arrival in Ljubljana in 1727, up to his death in 1759, his name and his works became the trademark of a large number of religious interiors throughout Slovenia and Croatia, particularly within Franciscan churches.

en.name: *St. Frances Landing at the Adriatic Coast*
description: The scenes painted by Bernardo Bobić are set in contemporary late 17th-century Croatia and Zagreb, although they could only have occurred at the beginning of the 13th century.

ar.name: قاعدة شمعدان.
description: شمعدان من النحاس المسبوك والمرصَّع ذو شكل مخروطي مقطوع، وحوافه مائلة من الطرفين العلوي والسفلي. ويطغى على جسمه طوق رئيسي من خط النسخ، منقسم إلى ثلاثة أقسام، مفصولة عن بعضها بعضاً بثلاثة أشكال دائرية تتضمَّن شعارات النبالة المملوكية، وهو نمط يرقى إلى القرن الثامن / الرابع عشر. أما النطاقات الرئيسية للزخرفة فتزيِّنها أنساق من الورد الناعم المطعَّم بالفضة. وقد استُخدمت مادة الميناء السوداء في النقوش كترصيع لملء الخلفية ذات النمط الوردي، وبالتالي، إبراز التفاصيل الرائعة لأنساق الورد. والنقش، المطعَّم بالفضة، يعدِّد مزايا صاحب التقدِمة الذي تبرَّع بالشمعدان. من الممكن أن يكون الكثير من هذه الشمعدانات قد أُهديت إلى المساجد والمقامات والمدارس الدينية في مصر من أجل استخدامها. وقد أصبح الحكام المماليك في مصر وسوريا رعاة كبار للفنون وفن العمارة. فالقاهرة كانت عاصمتهم التي حكموها من عام 647/ 1250 حتى عام 922 / 1517.

صُنع هذا الشمعدان لتقديمه إلى أحد المساجد، أو **المدارس**، وهو مُزيَّن بألقاب المحسن المملوكي الذي أمر بصنعه، حيث يُقال في العبارة المنقوشة: "من الأمير الناصر، صاحب السلطة الأنبل، الأسمى الأعظم؛ صاحب النفوذ الملكي، المؤيد، المانح للحماية؛ صاحب السيادة، الحافظ.."
keywords: رعاية؛ زخرفة كتابية؛ وَقْف.

en.name: Candlestick base.
description: A cast brass, inlaid candlestick of truncated conical form; it has bevelled ridges on both the upper and lower rims. The body is dominated by a central band of *naskhi* script divided into three sections. The sections are separated by three roundels containing Mamluk heraldic emblems, the style dating to the AH 8th / AD 14th century. The main decorative fields are embellished with fine floral scrolls inlaid with silver; a black niello substance is used as inlay to fill in the background of the floral patterns, thus emphasising the fine details of the scrolls. The inscription describes the patron who commissioned the candlestick. Many such candlesticks would have been presented for use in mosques, shrines and religious schools in Egypt. The Mamluk rulers of Egypt and Syria became great patrons of art and architecture. Cairo was their capital, which they ruled from AH 647 / AD 1250 to AH 922 / AD 1517.

This candlestick was made for presentation to a mosque or *madrasa*, and is decorated with the titles of the Mamluk patron who commissioned it, stating: 'by the most noble authority, lofty, lordly, great; the kingly, supportive, … provider of protection; the masterful, maintainer, prince al-Nassiri'.
keywords: Calligraphy; patronage; waqf
materials: Cast brass, with silver and *niello* inlay.
tags: Cast brass, with silver and niello inlay.

es.name: Candelero.
description:
Candelero troncocónico de bronce fundido con incrustaciones. Los bordes superior e inferior están biselados. El cuerpo tiene una banda central en caracteres *nasji*, divida en tres secciones por tres medallones con emblemas heráldicos mamelucos que, por su estilo, corresponden al siglo VIII / XIV. La decoración principal consiste en elegantes volutas florales de plata incrustada sobre un fondo de niel negro que hace destacar los finos detalles de los rollos. La inscripción alude a quien encomendó el candelero.  
Este tipo de candeleros se utilizaban en mezquitas, santuarios y escuelas religiosas de Egipto. Los gobernantes mamelucos de Egipto y Siria se convirtieron en grandes mecenas del arte y la arquitectura. El Cairo fue su capital y la gobernaron de 647 / 1250 a 922 / 1517.

Candelero para alguna mezquita o madrasa, decorado con los títulos grabados del cliente mameluco que lo encargó. La inscripción dice: “Por la más noble autoridad, alta, señorial, grande; el regio, sostenedor... fuente de protección; el poderoso y mantenedor príncipe al-Nasiri”.
dates: Siglo VIII de la Hégira / XIV d. C.
keywords: caligrafía; mecenazgo
materials: Bronce vaciado, con incrustaciones de plata y niel.
tags: Bronce vaciado, con incrustaciones de plata y niel.

fr.name: Chandelier.
description: Chandelier en fonte de cuivre incrustée, de forme tronconique présentant des bourrelets saillants près du bord supérieur et inférieur. L'ornementation du corps est dominée par un bandeau d'écriture *naskhi* divisé en trois sections, séparées par trois rondeaux contenant des emblèmes héraldiques mamelouks dont le style date du VIIIe siècle H (XIVe siècle J.-C.). Les champs décoratifs sont ornés de fins rinceaux floraux incrustés d'argent. Le nielle noir est également utilisé en incrustations pour combler le fond des motifs floraux et mettre ainsi en valeur l'exécution pleine de finesse des rinceaux. L'inscription qualifie le client qui a commandé cet objet. En Égypte, de nombreux chandeliers de ce type étaient offerts à des mosquées, des mausolées et des écoles religieuses. Les souverains mamelouks d'Égypte et de Syrie furent d'importants mécènes des arts et de l'architecture. Le Caire était leur capitale, d'où ils régnèrent de 647 à 922 H (1250-1517 J.-C.).

Ce chandelier fabriqué pour être offert à une mosquée ou une *madrasa* porte les titres du mécène mamelouk qui l’a commandité. Linscription dit : “par l’autorité la plus noble, la plus haute, la plus seigneuriale, la plus éminente ; le protecteur royal, charitable... ; le tout-puissant, le défenseur, le prince al-Nassiri”.
dates: VIIIe siècle de l’Hégire (XIVe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: calligraphie ; mécénat ; waqf
materials: Fonte de cuivre à incrustations d’argent et de nielle.
tags: Fonte de cuivre à incrustations d’argent et de nielle.

ar.name: قلعة صلاح الدين.
description:
يمكن اعتبار قلعة صلاح الدين كأحد أكثر القلاع إتقاناً في بلاد الشام، وهي تحمل مميزات الطرز المعمارية البيزنطية والصليبية والأيوبية والمملوكية بما فيها الأنواع العسكرية والمدنية والدينية والصرحية. تقع القلعة على الجزء الشمالي من الجبال الساحلية مطلة على الطريق الفرعي الذي يمر عبر الجبل بين مدينة اللاذقية وسهل الغاب الشمالي. وقد لعبت القلعة دور القصر السكني للصليبيين والأيوبيين والمماليك.  
خلال القرن الحادي عشر، شغل البيزنطيون الموقع، وبدؤوا حملة تحصين طموحة خلال جهودهم للتوسع، لكن السلاجقة سرعان ما أوقفوهم، ثم انتقلت القلعة إلى الصليبيين في الفترة 7-508/ 1114 و513/ 1119. وعلى إثر تسليمه كإقطاع لروبرت ابن فولك دانجو، أحد فرسان القديس يوحنا (الإسبيتاريه) وخلفائه، تحسن وضع القلعة بشكل واضح، وقد يكون ذلك بمساعدة القوات العسكرية. لكن هذه السيطرة الصليبية قطعت بواسطة السلطان الأيوبي صلاح الدين عام 584/ 1188 بعد ثلاثة أيام من الحصار، وأقطعت إلى الأمير الأيوبي ناصر الدين منكوفريش، وبعد أن عانت من التهديد المغولي في أواسط القرن السابع/ الثالث عشر، استعادها السلطان المملوكي الظاهر بيبرس سلمياً عام 671/ 1272، وعين لها حاكماً. ومع وصول السلطان المنصور سيف الدين قلاوون إلى السلطة عام 679/ 1280، حول الأمير الثائر سنقر الأشقر القلعة إلى مقر لقواته، لكن قلاوون هزمه عام 686/ 1287، فتحولت القلعة إلى مركز إداري محلي في الإمبراطورية المملوكية.  
تم تأسيس القلعة المثلثة الشكل على مرتفع صخري ناتئ منفصل عن الجبل بواسطة خندق صناعي عمقه حوالي 30م. يبلغ طول القلعة من الشرق إلى الغرب حوالي 700م، وعرضها الأعظمي على طول الخندق الشرقي 120م، والمرتفع مقسوم إلى منطقتين طوبوغرافيتين تفرضان حدود الدفاعات. حول الصليبيون الفسحة السماوية العليا التي تشكل قلب القصر البيزنطي إلى منطقة سكنية من خلال بناء حصن مربع ضخم يضم خزاني مياه كبيرين، وتحده أبراج متعددة نصف دائرية ومستطيلة، وحفر الخندق الشرقي. وفيما بعد، حسن الصليبيون الدفاعات باستخدام التحصينات السابقة التي بناها البيزنطيون والصليبيون، وبنوا مجمعاً سكنياً كبيراً يضم حمامات وغرف استقبال على منسوبين، وهو يشبه في طرازه القصر الأيوبي في قلعة حلب، كما تم بناء حمامين وجامع حول المجمع خلال الفترة المملوكية مع برج استقبال عبر الجدار الغربي للفسحة العليا، كما تم تحصين الفسحة السماوية السفلى خلال فترات الإشغال الصليبية والإسلامية عبر بناء برجي ببوابة وسور محيط.

بعد معركة حطين، وبعد أن حرر صلاح الدين مدينة القدس، ذهب صلاح الدين وبمرافقة حملة عسكرية، متجهاً بسرعة في صيف عام 584 هـ/1188 م، في معركة غلب فيها عشرات المراكز العسكرية الفرنجية، الواقعة على طول الشاطيء الشرقي للبحر الأبيض المتوسط، وجبال العلويين. عُرفت هذه القلعة رسمياً باسم "قلعة صهيون"، وهي شمال شرق اللاذقية، وقد وقعت في يد صلاح الدين بعد معركة دامت ثلاثة أيام، وسُمِّيت باسمه. شُيِّدت القلعة بشكل فخم، وذات شكل مثلثي، وتتميز بموقعها على أرض صخرية مرتفعة.
artist: لوردات سايون الصليبيون (4-508/ 14-1188)، الأمراء الأيوبيون (584-671/ 1188-1272)، الأمير الثائر سنقر الأشقر (78-686/ 79-1287)، السلاطين المماليك: قلاوون (78-689/ 79-1290)، الأشرف خليل (89-693/ 90-1293)، الناصر محمد بن قلاوون (الذي حكم ثلاث مرات: 3-694/ 3-1294؛ 698-708/ 1299-1309؛ 9-741/ 10-1341).
partner: Ministry of Culture, Directorate General of Museums and Antiquities

en.name: Qal‘at Salah al-Din (Saladin).
description:
Saladin castle may be considered one of the most elaborate castles of the Bilad al-Sham, featuring the main characteristics of Byzantine, Frankish, Ayyubid and Mamluk architectural styles, including a variety of military, civil, religious and palatial types. The castle is located on the northern buttresses of the Jabal Ansariyya (also known as Jabal Bahra) Mountain, overlooking the minor road that intersected the mountain between the town of Latakia and the northern Ghab plain. For the most part, the castle played the role of a manorial residence for the Crusaders, the Ayyubids and the Mamluks.  
During the 11th century, the site was occupied by the Byzantines who launched an ambitious fortification campaign during their expansionist efforts. They were briefly curtailed by the Seljuqs after-which the castle was conquered by the Crusaders between AH 507–8 / AD 1114 and AH 513 / AD1119. Granted as a fief to one of the Knights Hospitallers, Robert son of Foulques d'Anjou and to his successors, the castle was improved significantly, possibly with the help of the Military Orders. This Crusader stronghold was finally conquered by the Ayyubid, Salah al-Din al-Ayyubi (Saladin) in AH 584 / AD 1188 after a three-day siege and granted as an *iqta'* (property donation) to an Ayyubid prince Nasir al-Din Mengüverish. After being threatened by the Mongols in the middle of the AH 7th / AD 13th century, it was peacefully recovered by the Mamluk Sultan al-Zahir Baybars in AH 671 / AD 1272 and granted to a governor. With the advent of Sultan al-Mansur Sayf al-Din Qalawun in AH 679 / AD 1280, the anti-Sultan Sunqur al-Ashqar transformed the castle into his headquarters. Qalawun conquered it in AH 686 / AD1287. Saladin Castle was then transformed into a provincial administrative centre within the Mamluk Empire.  
The triangular shaped castle is established on a rocky spur isolated from the mountain by a wide artificial ditch whose depth is about 30 m. Measuring east to west almost 700-m long and 120 m of maximal width along the eastern ditch, the spur is divided into two topographical areas that dictated the layout of the defences. The eastern high courtyard, the heart of the Byzantine castle, was transformed into a manorial area by the Crusaders with the building of a huge square keep, of two large cisterns, numerous semi-circular and oblong flanking towers and the partial digging of the eastern ditch. Later, taking advantage of the pre-existing fortifications built by the Byzantines and by the Crusaders, the Ayyubids improved the defences and built a large palatial complex combining baths and reception rooms on two levels following the same model of the Ayyubid palace at Aleppo Citadel. Two *hammam*s and a mosque were also built around this complex during the Mamluk period with a reception tower astride the west wall of the high courtyard. The low courtyard, west, was also defensively fortified during the Crusader and Islamic occupations through the construction of two gate-towers and a surrounding wall.

After the Battle of Hattin in which Salah al-Din reconquered Jerusalem, he went on a quick and efficient military campaign over the summer of AH 584 / AD 1188 in which he defeated over a dozen Crusader strong-points all along the eastern Mediterranean coasts and Jebel (Mount) Ansariyya. This castle, formerly known as Chateau de Saone and located northeast of Latakia, fell to Salah al-Din after a three-day siege and was subsequently named after him. It is elaborately constructed and strangely triangular in shape, taking advantage of the rocky terrain over which it towers.
dynasty: Hamdanid; Byzantine; Seljuq; Crusader; Ayyubid; Mamluk.
artist: Crusader Lords of Saone (AH 508–4 / AD 1114–88); Ayyubid Mengüverish amirs (AH 584–671 / AD 1188–1272), rebel amir Sunqur al-Ashqar (AH 678–86 / AD 1279–87), Mamluk sultans: Qalawun (AH 678–89 / AD 1279–90); al-Ashraf Khalil (AH 689–93 / AD 1290–3) and al-Nasir Muhammad ibn Qalawun (who ruled three times: AH 693–4 / AD 1293–4; AH 698–708 / AD 1299–1309; AH 709–41 / AD 1310–41).
keywords: Military architecture; palatial architecture; Salah al-Din; Baybars; Qalawun
partner: Ministry of Culture, Directorate General of Museums and Antiquities

es.name: Castillo de Saladino (Qal'at Salah al-Din).
description:
El castillo de Saladino puede considerarse uno de los más complejos del Bilad al-Sham y presenta las principales características de los estilos arquitectónicos bizantino, franco, ayyubí y mameluco, aplicadas a varios tipos de edificios militares, civiles y religiosos. El castillo está ubicado sobre los contrafuertes norte del Yabal Ansariyya (también conocido como Yabal Bahra) y domina el camino que cruzaba las montañas entre la ciudad de Latakia y la llanura de Gab, al norte. La mayor parte del tiempo, el castillo cumplió la función de residencia señorial para cruzados, ayyubíes y mamelucos.  
Durante el siglo V / XI, el lugar fue ocupado por los bizantinos, quienes emprendieron un ambicioso proyecto de fortificación durante su campaña expansionista. Fueron frenados por los selyuquíes durante breve tiempo, tras lo cual el castillo fue conquistado por los cruzados, quienes permanecieron entre 507-508 / 1114 y 513 / 1119. El castillo se cedió como feudo personal al caballero hospitalario Robert, hijo de Foulques d'Anjou, y a sus sucesores, quienes lo mejoraron notablemente, quizá con ayuda de las órdenes militares. Finalmente, la fortaleza cruzada fue conquistada por el ayyubí Salah al-Din al-Ayyubi (Saladino) en 584 / 1188 tras un asedio de tres días; después, se donó como *iqta‘* (donación de propiedades) al príncipe ayyubí Nasir al-Din Mengüverish. La construcción sufrió la amenaza de los mongoles a mediados del siglo VII / XIII, pero más tarde, en 671 / 1272, fue recuperada pacíficamente por el sultán mameluco al-Zahir Baybars y cedida a un gobernador. Con el ascenso al poder del sultán al-Mansur Sayf al-Din Qalawun en 679 / 1280, Sunqur al-Ashqar, contrario al sultán, transformó el castillo en su cuartel general. Qalawun lo conquistó en 686 / 1287 y lo convirtió en un centro administrativo provincial del Imperio Mameluco.  
El castillo, de forma triangular, está enclavado en un contrafuerte rocoso, aislado de la montaña por un ancho foso artificial de unos 30 m de profundidad. El contrafuerte, dividido en dos áreas topográficas que determinaron la estructura de las defensas, mide casi 700 m de largo de este a oeste y alcanza una anchura máxima de 120 m en el foso oriental. El patio alto oriental, centro del castillo bizantino, se transformó en zona señorial de manos de los cruzados, quienes construyeron una enorme torre del homenaje cuadrada, dos grandes aljibes, numerosas torres semicirculares y alargadas alrededor, y parte del foso oriental. Más tarde, aprovechando las fortificaciones que habían construido bizantinos y cruzados, los ayyubíes mejoraron las defensas y erigieron un gran complejo palaciego que combinaba baños y salones de recepción en dos niveles, siguiendo el modelo del palacio ayyubí de la ciudadela de Alepo. Además, durante el periodo mameluco se construyeron dos *hammam* y una mezquita, con una torre de entrada sobre el muro oeste del patio alto. El patio bajo, al oeste, también se fortificó durante las ocupaciones cruzada e islámica con la construcción de dos torres de entrada y una muralla.

Saladino, en el verano de 584 / 1188, tras la batalla de Hittin en la que reconquistó Jerusalén, emprendió una campaña militar rápida y eficaz en la que derrotó más de una docena de puntos clave para los cruzados de la costa mediterránea y las montañas Ansari. Este castillo, antes llamado castillo de Saona y ubicado al noreste de Latakia, cayó en manos de Saladino tras un asedio de tres días, por lo que se le dio su nombre. La construcción es muy compleja, con una peculiar forma triangular que aprovecha el terreno rocoso sobre el que se erige.
dates: Siglos IV-VII de la Hégira / siglos X-XIII d. C.
artist: Cruzados de Saona (508-584 / 1114-88); emires ayyubíes Mengüverish (584-671 / 1188-1272); emir rebelde Sunqur al-Ashqar (678-686 / 1279-1287); sultanes mamelucos Qalawun (678-689 / 1279-1290), al-Ashraf Jalil (689-693 / 1290-93) y al-Nasir Muhammad ibn Qalawun (tres mandatos: 693-94 / 1293-94; 698-708 / 1299-1309; 709-741 / 1310-1341).
keywords: arquitectura militar; arquitectura palaciega; Salah al-Din; Baybars; Qalawun.
partner: Ministry of Culture, Directorate General of Museums and Antiquities

fr.name: Qal’at Salah al-Din (Saladin).
description:
Le château de Saladin, l'un des plus remarquables du Bilad al-Cham, présente les principales caractéristiques des styles architecturaux byzantins, francs, ayyoubides et mamelouks, appliquées aussi bien aux bâtiments de type militaire que civil, religieux ou palatial. Il se dresse sur les contreforts nord-est du Djebel Ansariyya (également appelée Djebel Bahra), dominant une petite route qui franchit la montagne entre la ville de Latakia et la plaine du Ghab au nord. Pour l'essentiel de son histoire, il fut une résidence seigneuriale pour les Croisés, les Ayyoubides et les Mamelouks.  
Au XIe siècle, le site fut occupé par les Byzantins qui lancèrent une ambitieuse campagne de fortifications pour accompagner leur expansion. Ils furent brièvement ralentis sous les Seldjoukides, après quoi le château fut conquis et occupé par les Croisés de 508 H / 1114 J.-C. à 513 H / 1119 J.-C. Accordé en fief à l'un des Chevaliers hospitaliers, Robert, fils de Foulques d'Anjou et à ses successeurs, il fut significativement transformé, sans doute avec l'aide des ordres militaires. La place forte fut finalement reprise par l'Ayyoubide Salah al-Din al-Ayyoubi (Saladin) en 584 H / 1188 après un siège de trois jours et confié en *iqta'* (donation en propriété) à un prince ayyoubide, Nasir al-Din Mengüverish. Menacé par les Mongols au milieu du VIIe siècle H (XIIIe siècle J.-C.), il fut repris pacifiquement par le sultan mamelouk al-Dahir Baybars en 671 H / 1272 J.-C.) et confié à un gouverneur. À l'arrivée sur le trône du sultan al-Mansour Sayf al-Din Qalawun en 679 H / 1280 J.-C., l'anti-sultan Sunqur al-Achqar en fit son quartier général dont s'empara Qalawun en 686 H / 1287 J.-C. Le château de Saladin fut alors transformé en centre administratif de la province dans le cadre de l'empire mamelouk.  
L'ensemble de forme triangulaire prend appui sur un promontoire rocheux isolé de la montagne par une douve artificielle de 30 m environ de profondeur. Mesurant d'est en ouest pratiquement 700 m de longueur sur 120 m de largeur maximale le long de la douve orientale, le promontoire se divise en deux zones qui ont dicté le plan des défenses. La cour haute à l'est, cœur du château byzantin, a été transformée en résidence seigneuriale par les Croisés qui y construisirent un énorme donjon carré, deux grandes citernes, de nombreuses tours semi-circulaires, et creusèrent en partie la douve orientale. Plus tard, profitant des fortifications préexistantes des Byzantins et des Croisés, les Ayyoubides améliorèrent les défenses et construisirent un vaste complexe palatial combinant des salles de réception et des bains sur deux niveaux, d'après le modèle du palais ayyoubide de la citadelle d'Alep. Deux hammams et une mosquée furent également édifiés à proximité de ce complexe pendant la période mamelouke ainsi qu'une tour d'entrée contre le mur occidental de la cour haute. La cour basse, à l'ouest, fut également fortifiée par les Croisés et les troupes islamiques qui édifièrent deux tours d'entrée et un mur de clôture.

Après la bataille de Hattin qui lui livra Jérusalem, Saladin poursuivit sa campagne militaire pendant l'été 584 H / 1188 J.-C. et reprit une douzaine de places fortes croisées le long des côtes de la Méditerranée et dans le Djebel Ansariyya. Ce château, anciennement appelé château de Saône, situé au nord de Latakia, tomba après un court siège de trois jours. Sa construction est raffinée, et sa forme triangulaire étrange s'explique par le terrain rocheux sur lequel il s'élève.

de.name:
Mariahilfer Kirche  
Pfarrkirche Mariahilf
names:
Klosterkirche der Minoriten in Graz  
Wallfahrtskirche Mariahilf
description:
Einige Jahre bevor Pietro de Pomis in Graz das Mausoleum erbaute, arbeitete er vermutlich an den Gebäuden des Minoritenklosters und an der Mariahilferkirche. Ganz sicher kann ihm die (erste) palladianische Fassade zugeordnet werden. Hier und dort war Pietro Valnegro für die Bauaufsicht zuständig.  
Mehr als hundert Jahre später wurde die Kirche dem Zeitgeschmack entsprechend modernisiert. Sie bekam den Vorbau in Form von zwei Türmen und einem leicht vortretenden architektonischen Mittelteil, den Portikus. Der Baumeister Joseph Hueber, der von Wien gekommen war, wurde beauftragt, den neuen Bau zu errichten. Er löste das Problem des engen Grundstücks, indem er die vertikalen Elemente betonte. Er baute die schlanken Türme und fügte die Halbsäulen an der Portikus-Fassade sowie die Statuen hinzu. Die Skulpturen sind die Meisterwerke der Fassade und betonen die Plastizität der Ansichtsseite der Kirche.

Als Erzherzog Ferdinand von Innerösterreich, der spätere Kaiser Ferdinand II, seine Studien bei den Jesuiten in Ingolstadt beendet hatte, zog er in die Residenz der Familie in Graz. Einige Zeit, bevor er mit dem Bau des Mausoleums für sich und die Familie begann, unterstützten er und Johann Ulrich von Eggenberg die Minoriten, die eine neue Unterkunft benötigten. Nachdem sich die Franziskaner (1525) geteilt hatten, entstanden zwei neue Gruppen, die sich Observanten (Franziskaner) und Konventuale (Minoriten) nannten. Letztere mussten ihren Besitz in Graz den Franziskanern übergeben und waren daraufhin ohne Unterkunft. Als erste Hilfsmaßnahme überließ ihnen ein früher lebender Fürst Eggenberg sein Sommerhaus, in dem sich auch eine alte Kapelle befand. Ungefähr hundert Jahre später ließ Fürst Johann Ulrich von Eggenberg das Kloster und die Kirche der Minoriten errichten. Vermutlich als einziger Financier. Es heißt, dass der Kaiser das Projekt nur mental unterstützte. Als Dank dafür, was die Eggenberger für die Minoriten gemacht hatten, wurde ihnen die Ewige Ruhe im Kloster gestattet. Drei Familienmitglieder der Eggenberger sind in der Gruft begraben, die sich nahe des Altarraums seitlich des rechten Kirchenschiffs befindet.

history: Durch die rasche Ausbreitung des Franziskaner-Ordens und seiner wachsenden Popularität ergaben sich noch während der Lebenszeit des Hl Franz von Assisi Probleme. Die Ordensangehörigen waren sich uneinig über die Strenge der ursprünglichen Regeln und teilten sich in zwei Gruppen. Die einen nannten sich die Spirituellen. Die Mönche wollten sich strikt an die Regeln und Ideale ihres Gründers halten, während die Mehrheit eine moderatere Auslegung bevorzugte. Nach vielen Jahren der Unstimmigkeiten entschied sich Papst Johannes XXII gegen die Spirituellen und änderte die Regel, die die Armut der Ordensgemeinschaft betraf. Viele Spirituelle, die über diese Entscheidung unglücklich waren und die den Reichtum der Kirche als skandalös empfanden, verließen die Gemeinschaft. Der Orden teilte sich in zwei Gruppen – in die Observanten (Franziskaner) und in die Konventualen, die den Namen Mindere Brüder (Minoriten) annahmen. In Graz mussten letztere ihren Besitz den Franziskanern überlassen und sich nach einer anderen Unterkunft umsehen. Hilfe kam von einem Fürsten Eggenberg, der sie in seinem Sommerhaus wohnen ließ, und später von einem seiner Nachkommen, der den Bau des neuen Klosters und der neuen Mariahilferkirche finanzierte.

en.name:
Church of Mariahilf  
Mariahilf Parish Church
names:
The Minorite´s Monastery Church in Graz  
Pilgrimage Church Mariahilf
description: With the rapid expansion of the order and its growing popularity during the lifetime of St Francis of Assisi, the Franciscans started to experience problems. Members differed in their opinions about whether the original rule was too severe and split into two differing groups of Friars. One of them called themselves the Spirituals. They wanted a precise adherence to the strict rules and the spirit of their founder, while the majority favoured a more moderate interpretation. After many years of discussion, Pope John XXII decided against the Spirituals and reversed the rule concerning corporate poverty. Many Spirituals who were unhappy with the decision and who regarded the wealth of the Church as scandalous left. The order split into two groups, the Observants (Franciscans) and the Conventuals who became known as the Order of Friars Minor (Minorites). In Graz the latter had to sign over their property to the Franciscans and then to look for another dwelling. Help came from a prince of Eggenberg, who let them live in his summer house, and later on from his descendants who financed the building of a new monastery and the new church, dedicated to Mary Help.

When Archduke Ferdinand from Inner Austria, the later Emperor Ferdinand II, had finished his studies with the Jesuits in Ingolstadt he moved to the family´s residence in Graz. Some years before he began to build the Mausoleum for himself and his family, he and Johann Ulrich von Eggenberg supported the Minorites who were in need of a new home. After a split had occurred among the Franciscans (1525), two new groups emerged calling themselves Observants (Franciscans) and Conventuals (Minorites). The latter had to sign over their property in Graz to the Franciscans and were then without dwelling. As a first relief measure an earlier living Prince Eggenberg gave them his summer house including an old chapel. About a hundred years later Prince Johann Ulrich von Eggenberg built the monastery and the church for the Minorites, probably as sole financier. It is said that the emperor supported the project only mentally. As thanks for what the Eggenberg family had done for the Minorites, they were allowed to have their eternal rest in the monastery. Three members are buried in the crypt next to the altar on the side of the right nave.

ar.name: تعليقة صدر.
description: اهتمت المرأة في سورية على مر العصور بالحلي الذهبية والفضية لتزيين وتجميل نفسها وأيضاً كنوع من التأمين المادي. وقد وُجِد في المواقع الأثرية العديد من القطع الذهبية مثل الأساور التي توضع في المعصم أو العضد أو القدم والمشابك والأقراط والخواتم وغيرها. هذه القطعة عبارة عن حلية ذهبية تعلق في الصدر بواسطة دبوس، وهي على شكل قلب مقلوب مصنوع من نسيج ذهبي مفرغ، على أطرافه حلقات صغيرة جداً، عُلق على كل منها سلسلة تنتهي بشكل كرة أو عصفور أو هلال أو عقدة وجميعها مكونة من خيوط ذهبية منسوجة.
حلية لتزيين الملابس (دبوس)، على شكل قلب، تتدلّى منه حلي صغيرة. تعود هذه القطعة إلى العصر الفاطمي، والتي كانت تُعلَّق على الملابس، عن طريق حنية صغيرة على حافتها.

en.name: Brooch.
description:
A gold brooch that was designed to hang from the chest by means of a pin attached to the wearer's clothing. It takes the shape of an upside-down heart and was produced from a web of moulded gold. On its frame are tiny rings, from which hang chains that terminate in different forms: a ball, a bird, a crescent-moon and a knot, all fashioned from woven gold filaments.  
Throughout the ages, the women of Syria held as important gold and silver jewellery for decoration and self-beautification, as well as a source for financial security. Finds from numerous archaeological sites have included bracelets, armlets, anklets, brooches, earrings, and rings.

This heart-shaped pendant with dangling charms is an example of Fatimid jewellery and would have been attached to the clothing by a pin or possibly woven through by using the small loops along its edge.
keywords: Brooch; gold; woven; filigree; bird; crescent-moon; Aleppo; Cairo; Raqqa

es.name: Broche.
description:
Este broche de oro se diseñó para sujetarlo al pecho con un alfiler. Tiene forma de corazón invertido y se fabricó a partir de una malla de oro moldeado. En el borde se aprecian anillas diminutas de los que cuelgan cadenas rematadas por diferentes figuras: una bola, un pájaro, una media luna y un nudo, elaborados con filamentos de oro tejidos.  
En todas las épocas, las mujeres sirias han considerado importante poseer joyas de oro y plata para adornarse y realzar su belleza, y también como fuente de seguridad económica. En numerosos yacimientos arqueológicos se han hallado brazaletes, pulseras, ajorcas para los tobillos, broches, pendientes y anillos.
Este broche con forma de corazón y adornos colgantes es una pieza de joyería fatimí; se prendía a la ropa con un alfiler o cosiéndolo de los aritos que lo circundan.
dates: Siglo V o VI de la Hégira / XI o XII d. C. aproximadamente.
keywords: Broche; oro; trenzado; filigrana; pájaro; media luna; Alepo; El Cairo; al-Raqqa.

fr.name: Broche.
description:
Broche en or qui s'accrochait à la poitrine au moyen d'une épingle. En forme de cœur à l'envers, elle est en filigrane d'or moulé. Sur son pourtour, des chaînettes terminées par diverses amulettes – perle, oiseau, croissant de lune, nœud – en filigrane d'or sont accrochées à de petits anneaux.  
Les femmes syriennes ont de tout temps possédé de nombreux bijoux en or et en argent qui, en dehors de leur fonction esthétique, assuraient leur sécurité financière. De nombreux bracelets, bracelets de cheville, broches, boucles d'oreille et anneaux ont été retrouvés lors de fouilles archéologiques.

Ce pendant en forme de cœur auquel sont accrochés des porte-bonheur est un bel exemple de joaillerie fatimide. Il était attaché au vêtement par une épingle ou peut-être cousu, le fil passant dans les petites boucles de son bord.
dates: Vers le Ve-VIe siècle de l'Hégire (XIe-XIIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: Broches ; or ; filigrane ; croissant de lune ; Alep, Le Caire ; Raqqa

description: During the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries, luster ceramics made in Manises, a suburb of Valencia on Spain’s eastern coast, were made for Italian, Spanish, and French patrons. Accordingly, Christian symbols, Latin inscriptions, and European blazons were standard components of Manises lusterware iconography. This exceptional dish bears the arms (two intersecting maces) of the Gondi banking family of Florence. It can be dated to the late fifteenth century.

en.name: Inscribed textile (*tiraz*)
description:
This *tiraz* was made for the Fatimid caliph al-‘Aziz (Hegira 365–386 / AD 975–996). It testifies to the tractable nature of Fatimid society. Exceptionally, in addition to supplying the caliph’s titles, it gives the name of his chief minister or vizier Ibn Killis (served Hegira 366–380 / AD 977–90). Killis, who was of Jewish origin, was famous for the financial reforms that helped bring enormous prosperity to Egypt as well as to the vizier. The inscription reads,  
Praise to God, Lord of the Worlds, may God bless Muhammad the Prophet. Assistance from God \[to\] Nizar Abu Mansur, the Imam al-‘Aziz billah, Commander of the faithful, God’s blessing upon him and upon \[his pure ancestors\]. From what was ordered by the respectable vizier Abu‘l-Faraj Ya‘qub ibn Yusuf \[Ibn Killis\], vizier of the Commander of the faithful, to be made in the year \[three hundred\] seventy-one.
holder: Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA)

description: هذه الصفحة من نسخة مبعثرة تسمى "" الصغيرة الثانية""  من ملحمة الشهنامة للفردوسي (كتاب الملوك) وتوضح الفترة العائدة لحكم الملك الساساني بهرام (أو فاهرام) الخامس (حكم خلال 420-38) وهي تظهر الزيارة التي قام بها بهرام غور لمنزل أحد رعيته وبهرام غور (يعني الصياد العظيم) قام بمآثر عظيمة بقوسه الكبير وفي هذه المرة قتل زوج من الأسود المتوحشة التي افترست قطيع الأغنام الكبير لمهيار وهذا الراعي لا يعرف بهرام ويتوجه إليه بالكلام راغبا شكره على شجاعته  في الرماية ويمدح الشاه الحاكم بهرام – ما يزال جاهلا لشخصه – ويقرر زيارة بيت صانع المجوهرات حيث يقول الراعي سوف يسمع الأنغام وصوت القيثارة وفي الحقيقة كان لدى مهيار فقط ابنة واحدة والتي تعزف على القيثارة وقد فعلت ذلك وهي جالسة مقابل والدها ذو اللحية البيضاء والشاه.

en.name:
Bahram entertained by Arezu, daughter of Mahyar the jeweller  
Folio from a dispersed copy of Firdausi’s *Shahnameh* (Book of Kings)
description:
This folio from the dispersed copy of the “Second Small” *Shahnameh* (Book of Kings) illustrates an episode concerning the historical Sasanian king, Bahram (or Vaharam) V (r. 420–38). It shows the visit paid by Bahram Gur to the home of one of his subjects.  
Bahram Gur, “that great hunter,” had performed another of many feats with his great bow, this time killing a pair of savage lions who would have preyed on the great flock of Mahyar’s sheep; and the head shepherd, not recognizing Bahram, addresses him, wishing to thank the brave archer and also praising the justice of the Shah’s rule. Bahram—still incognito—decides to visit the jeweller’s house where, says the shepherd, he will hear toasts and the sound of a harp. Indeed, Mahyar has “just one daughter, who plays the harp” and she does so, seated before both her white-bearded father and the Shah.
keywords: Folio; work-on-paper; works-on-paper; hunting; battle; animal; Shahnama; Shahnameh
materials: Ink, colours, gold, and silver on paper
