en.name: Madrasa and Mosque of Sultan Qaytbay.
names: Madrasa and Mosque of Sultan Qaytbay
description:
The principal, northern face of the *madrasa* contains the entrance. The form of the entrance follows the style typical of Mamluk entrances, commonly crowned with a tri-lobed arch that includes carved *muqarnas*. To the left of the entrance is the *sabil*(water dispensary) and above the entrance, a *kuttab* (Qur'anic school). There is a minaret to the right of the entrance, which is considered one of the most complete Mamluk examples as it represents both the architectural harmony and decorative skill of the age.  
The ground plan of the *madrasa* consists of a square courtyard with a polychrome marble floor and a ceiling with a central skylight. The courtyard is surrounded by four *iwan*s, the biggest of which is the *qibla iwan*, which overlooks the courtyard by means of a horseshoe arch. This *iwan* includes a magnificent *minbar* made of wood and inlaid with ivory and mother-of-pearl, decorated with intricate geometric ornamentation. Stuccoed windows, inset with coloured glass characterise the upper portion of the walls. The designer of the building was extremely skilled in filling the interior spaces with a variety of decorations: the embellishment of the wooden ceiling, its gilding and its painting; the arches that assume a number of forms; the stonework, decorated and carved with vegetal designs; the marble floors of the *madrasa*, mausoleum and water dispensary as well as the stucco windows.  
The mausoleum is accessed through a door on one of the side walls of the *qibla iwan*. Its floor plan is square and it is covered by a dome. The transition zone from a square to the circularity of the dome consists of nine tiers of intricately detailed stone *muqarnas*. The dome is decorated on the outside by ornamentation carved in stone, which consists of repetitive vegetal forms and geometric motifs in harmony with it. The design of this dome is considered to be an example of Mamluk stone decoration at its peak.  
The Complex of Qaytbay is considered one of the most innovative and beautiful of architectural complexes in Islamic Egypt. Its importance lies in the detailed decoration, the beauty of its proportions and the harmony of its architectural components, which include the *madrasa*, mosque, water dispensary, Qur'anic school and the mausoleum.

This monument stands in the Mamluk (Northern) Cemetery and is described as the most beautiful of the architectural complexes in Islamic Egypt. It is notable for its fine decoration, its perfect balance and the harmony of its components, which include a mosque, a *sabil* (water dispensary), a *kuttab* (Qur'anic school for children) and a mausoleum, and became known as the 'jewel' of Islamic architecture. Sultan Qaytbay, its patron, ruled for 29 years and has left many charitable monuments in Mecca, Medina, Jerusalem and Egypt.
artist: Sultan al-Ashraf Abu al-Nasr Qaytbay (r. AH 872–901 / AD 1468–96).
keywords: Inlay; stucco interlocked with coloured glass; marble; vegetal decoration; geometric decoration; water dispensary; mausoleum; funerary architecture; religious architecture; civil architecture; Qur’anic school; madrasa; mosque; muqarnas
partner: Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities, Supreme Council of Antiquities

es.name: Madrasa y mezquita del Sultán Qaytbay.
description:
La entrada está en la fachada principal, la norte, y respeta el estilo típico de las entradas de época mameluca, que suelen estar coronadas por un arco trilobulado con mocárabes tallados. A la izquierda de la entrada se halla el *sabil* y, sobre la entrada, un *kuttab* (escuela coránica). A la derecha de la entrada hay un alminar que está considerado como uno de los alminares mamelucos más completos, ya que representa la armonía arquitectónica y la destreza decorativa de la época.  
La planta de la madrasa consta de un patio cuadrado cubierto, con suelo de mármol policromado y un tragaluz en el centro del techo. Está rodeado por cuatro *iwan*, el mayor de ellos el de la *qibla*¸que se abre al patio a través de un arco de herradura. En él hay un *minbar* de madera con incrustaciones de marfil y nácar, decorado con complejos motivos geométricos. La parte superior de los muros destaca por sus ventanas de estuco con vidrios de colores. El arquitecto demostró un gran talento al decorar los espacios interiores en varios estilos: techos de madera dorados y pintados, arcos de diversos perfiles, piedra decorada y tallada con motivos vegetales, suelos de mármol en la madrasa, el mausoleo y la fuente, y ventanas de estuco con vidrios de colores.  
Al mausoleo, de planta cuadrada y cubierto por una cúpula, se entra por el *iwan* de la *qibla*. La transición entre el cuadrado de la planta y la cúpula se hace por medio de mocárabes de piedra con detalles muy trabajados. El exterior de la cúpula está tallado con armónicos motivos vegetales y geométricos reiterativos. El diseño de esta cúpula se considera un ejemplo de la mejor decoración mameluca en piedra.  
El complejo arquitectónico de Qaytbay es uno de los más innovadores y hermosos del Egipto islámico. Su importancia radica en el detalle de su decoración, la belleza de sus proporciones y la armonía de sus elementos arquitectónicos.

Este monumento se halla en el cementerio mameluco (norte) y se ha descrito como el complejo arquitectónico más hermoso del Egipto islámico. Destaca por su sofisticada decoración y por el perfecto equilibrio y la armonía de sus estructuras: una mezquita, un *sabil*, un *kuttab* y un mausoleo. Por todo ello, es conocido como la "joya de la arquitectura islámica". El sultán Qaytbay, el patrocinador, gobernó durante 29 años y donó numerosos monumentos en La Meca, Medina, Jerusalén y Egipto
keywords: incrustaciones; estuco entrecruzado con vidrios de colores; mármol; decoración vegetal; decoración geométrica; fuente pública; mausoleo; arquitectura funeraria; arquitectura religiosa; arquitectura civil; escuela coránica; madrasa; mezquita; muqarnas.

partner: Ministry of Culture,Supreme Council of Antiquities

fr.name: Mosquée et madrasa du sultan Qaytbay.
description:
L'entrée de la *madrasa* s'ouvre sur la façade principale orientée au nord. Elle illustre le style typique des entrées mameloukes, généralement surmontées d'un arc trilobé à *mouqarnas* sculptés. à gauche se trouve le *sabil* (fontaine publique) et au-dessus le *kuttab* (école coranique). à droite se dresse un minaret, considéré comme l'un des plus parfaits exemples du style mamelouk par son architecture harmonieuse et la qualité de sa décoration.  
Le plan de la *madrasa* consiste en une cour carrée à sol de marbre polychrome et plafond doté d'une verrière centrale. Elle est entourée de quatre *iwan*, le plus grand (celui de la *qibla*) ouvrant par un arc en fer à cheval. Il possède un superbe *minbar* en bois incrusté à décor de nacre, d'ivoire et d'entrelacs géométriques.  
La partie haute des murs comporte des fenêtres en stuc à inserts de verres de couleur. L'architecte a fait preuve d'un talent particulier dans l'ornementation des volumes intérieurs : plafonds de bois doré et peint, arcs de diverses formes, travail de la pierre décorée et sculptée de motifs végétaux, sols de marbre de la *madrasa*, du mausolée et de la fontaine publique, fenêtre de stuc à verres de couleur.  
On accède au mausolée par une porte donnant sur le mur latéral de l'*iwan* de la *qibla,* de plan carré et recouvert d'une coupole. La zone de transition entre les murs et la base circulaire de la coupole consiste en neuf rangées de *mouqarnas* de pierre au complexe décor imbriqué. La coupole en pierre est ornée, à l'extérieur, d'une répétition de motifs végétaux et géométriques sculptés. Elle est un brillant exemple des sommets atteints par l'art mamelouk du travail de la pierre. Le complexe de Qaytbay est sans doute l'un des plus novateurs et des plus éblouissants de tous ceux de l'égypte islamique. Son importance tient à sa décoration fouillée, à la beauté de ses proportions et à l'harmonie de ses cinq composants architecturaux.

Ce monument se trouve dans le cimetière mamelouk (cimetière nord) et est décrit comme le plus beau de tous les complexes architecturaux de l'Égypte islamique. Il est remarquable pour ses décorations, son parfait équilibre et l'harmonie de ses composants, qui incluent une mosquée, un *sabil* (fontaine publique), un *kuttab* (école coranique pour enfants) et un mausolée ; il est devenu aujourd'hui le “joyau” de l'architecture islamique. Le sultan Qaytbay, son mécène, a régné pendant 29 ans et a laissé de nombreux monuments de bienfaisance à La Mecque, Médine, Jérusalem et en Égypte.
artist: Sultan al-Achraf Abou al-Nasr Qaytbay (r. 872-901 H / 1468-1496 J.-C.).
keywords: incrustations ; stuc à imbrication de verres de couleur ; marbres ; décoration végétale ; décoration géométrique ; fontaines publiques ; architecture funéraire ; architecture religieuse ; architecture civile ; écoles coraniques ; mosquées ; mouqarnas

en.name: Bowl
description: This bowl is a fine example of pottery from the Samanid (AD 819–1005) workshops of eastern Iran. Its design is stark and striking, featuring a single line of Arabic calligraphy that encircles the deep rim. The script, with its elegantly elongated horizontals and sharp-tipped verticals, is an early form of Arabic calligraphy known as New Style Kufic. The bowl's decoration is minimal yet visually compelling, with the inscription reading: “Knowledge is the most noble lineage and chivalry the most intricate.” The inscription’s meaning is elevated by the artistic manipulation of the letters. Through shortening, bending, and elongating, the script is transformed into abstract motifs of remarkable visual impact. The vertical flourishes interspersed among the horizontal flow create a rhythmic interplay that draws in the viewer. Likely used for serving on special occasions, the bowl’s message about the virtues of knowledge and chivalry is particularly apt.
materials: Earthenware, opaque white glaze with black painting
tags: Earthenware, opaque white glaze with black painting

ar.name: مجمرة.
description:
يعود تاريخ هذه المجمرة المصنوعة من الحديد والبرونز إلى القرن 2 / 8، وهي واحدة من أشهر المجامر وأكثرها اكتمالاً بين المدافئ الواقفة الأموية التي عثر عليها في الأردن. وتعود أهميتها إلى الاكتمال في الصنع من قِبَل الحرفي المنفذ والدقة في الأداء والصنع وخاصة النقش النافر والتماثيل الصغيرة.  
  
الواجهة الأمامية للمجمرة تحتوي على ست كوات محاطة بعقود ترتفع فوق أعمدة. المشاهد الجنسية التي تظهر في الكوات ربما تمثل أسطورة ديونيسيوس. تقف المجمرة على أربعة نسور، أما الزوايا العلوية فيظهر عليها أربعة تماثيل لنساء عاريات يحملن باليد اليسرى طيراً.  
  
يشكل الدمج بين مادة الحديد والبرونز توافقاً تاماً بين شكل القطعة وتصميمها. ولعل الجهات المقنطرة من القطعة تذكر المرء بالأروقه المقنطرة الموجودة في قصير عمرة. كذلك المناظر الجنسية المصورة تذكر المرء باللوحات الجصية الجدارية في الغرفة الباردة من قصير عمرة. أما بالنسبة للنسور التي تحمل المجمرة، وتماثيل النساء العاريات التي تقف كل منهن على قاعدة ضيقة على ارتفاع 47 سم، فتعتبَر جزءاً هاماً من التصوير الشرقي، وهو مزيج من الفن الساساني والفن الإغريقي الروماني.  
  
لعبت المجامر البرونزية دوراً هاماً في مراسم البلاط الأموي. واستخدمت المجمرة في تسخين غرفة الخليفة، وربما استخدمت أيضاً مبخرة في القصر.

منقل من الحديد والبرونز، عائد إلى قصر الفدين الأموي. الواجهة الأمامية مُزيَّنة برسوم حسية، ربما تمثل أسطورة ديونيسوس. كجزء من الأيقنة المشرقية الموروثة، عمد الحرفي إلى المزاوجة بين نزعات ثقافية إيرانية، من جهة، والأسلوب الإغريقي الروماني الشرقي، من جهة ثانية.

en.name: Brazier.
description:
An iron and bronze brazier of the AH 2nd / AD 8th century, perfect in both the craftsmanship of the relief and in the rendition of the figures in the round. This object is probably one of the best-known and complete of all the Umayyad heating stands to be found in Jordan.  
  
The front plaque consists of six niches surrounded by arcades reposed over columns. The erotic scenes that appear in the niches probably represent the myth of Dionysus and his entourage. The brazier stands on four eagles, while the upper angles have four nude female figurines holding a bird in their left hand.  
  
The combination of iron and bronze form a happy union and make for a beautiful design. The arcaded sides remind one of the vaulted halls at Qasr al-Amra, and the erotic scenes depicted (within) call to mind the frescoes on the walls of the apodyterium (dressing room) of the bath complex (*hammam*) at Qasr al-Amra. The eagles that support the stand, together with the nude female figurines that stand 47 cm high on their narrow pedestals. Part of the inherited oriental iconography, the artisan integrates Iranian cultural traits with the oriental Greco-Roman style.  
  
Bronze braziers played an important role in the ceremonials of court life. The main function was to heat the caliph's room but they were also used as incense burners in the palace.

An iron and bronze brazier from the Umayyad palace of al-Fudayn. Its front plaque bears erotic scenes that probably represent the myth of Dionysus. Part of the inherited oriental iconography, the artisan integrated Iranian cultural traits with the oriental Greco-Roman style.
holder: Now on display at Jordan Museum
keywords: Apodyterium; architectural motifs; brazier; eagles; erotic imagery; figurative representation; hammam; iconography; incense burner; metalwork; relief decoration

es.name: Brasero
description:
Brasero de hierro y bronce del siglo II / VIII que presenta relieves y figuras redondeadas de factura perfecta. Probablemente sea uno de los objetos omeyas de este tipo más conocidos y completos de los que se han hallado en Jordania.  
La placa frontal está formada por seis nichos enmarcados en arcos sobre columnas. Las escenas eróticas que aparecen en su interior representan, posiblemente, el mito de Dionisio y su séquito. Las cuatro patas del brasero tienen forma de águila y las cuatro esquinas superiores están rematadas con sendas figuras femeninas desnudas que sujetan un pájaro en la mano izquierda.  
La afortunada combinación de hierro y bronce conforma un hermoso diseño. Los laterales con arcadas recuerdan una de las salas abovedadas de Qusayr Amra y las escenas eróticas que presentan se asemejan a los frescos de las paredes del *apodyterium* o vestuario del *hammam* de dicho palacio. Las águilas que sustentan el brasero y las figuras de mujeres desnudas sobre estrechos pedestales forman parte de una iconografía oriental heredada que mezcla elementos culturales iranios con el estilo grecorromano.  
Los braseros de bronce desempeñaban un importante papel en las ceremonias de la corte. Su función principal era caldear los aposentos del califa, pero en el palacio también se usaban para quemar incienso.

Brasero de hierro y bronce hallado en el palacio omeya de al-Fudayn. Su placa frontal presenta escenas eróticas que probablemente representen el mito de Dionisos. El artesano mezcló elementos culturales iraníes y grecorromanos, propios de la iconografía oriental heredada.
dates: Siglo II de la Hégira / VIII d. C.
keywords: apodyterium; brasero; águilas; imágenes eróticas; representación figurativa; hammam; iconografía; incensario; metalistería; relieve.

fr.name: Brasier.
description:
Brasier en fer et bronze du IIe siècle H (VIIIe siècle J.-C.), aussi raffiné quant au travail du relief qu'au rendu des figures en ronde-bosse. Probablement l'un des appareils de chauffage les plus connus et les plus complets de la période omeyyade.  
La plaque frontale se compose de six niches prises dans une arcature reposant sur des doubles colonnettes. Les scènes érotiques y figurant illustrent probablement le mythe de Dionysos. L'ensemble repose sur quatre aigles tandis qu'à chacun des quatre angles supérieurs se dresse une figurine féminine nue tenant un oiseau dans la main gauche.  
Le fer et le bronze se marient heureusement et participent à la qualité de conception de l'objet. Les arcatures rappellent les salles voûtées de Qasr al-Amra et les scènes érotiques représentées font penser à celles des fresques de l'*apodyterium* (vestiaire) du *hammam* dans le même palais. Les aigles ainsi que les figurines féminines de 47 cm de haut posées sur d'étroits piédestaux renvoient à une iconographie orientale traditionnelle qui mêle éléments culturels iraniens et style gréco-romain d'Orient.  
Les brasiers de bronze jouaient un rôle important dans le cérémonial de la vie de cour. Leur principale fonction était de chauffer la salle où se tenait le calife, mais ils pouvaient aussi servir de brûleurs d'encens.

Brasier en fer et en bronze originaire du palais omeyyade de al-Foudayn. Sa plaque frontale porte des scènes érotiques qui illustrent probablement le mythe de Dionysos. Héritier d’une iconographie orientale traditionnelle, l’artisan a mêlé des éléments culturels iraniens avec le style gréco-romain d’Orient.
dates: IIe siècle de l’Hégire (VIIIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: Brasier ; aigle ; imagerie érotique ; représentation figurative ; hammam ; iconographie ; brûleur d’encens ; travail du métal ; relief

en.name: Textile
description: This textile was displayed in the exhibition about Islamic Art held in Munich in 1910, as part of the Miquel i Badia collection. Afterwards it was acquired by Lázaro Galdiano, one of the most important Spanish art collectors. It is important to note Lazaro Galdiano's interest in and art appraisal of objects from the Spanish Muslim period. He was one of the earliest collectors of Arab art in Spain. The decoration is similar to the Golden Room of the Alhambra palace and it could be the Mohammad V period.
keywords: Nasrid art; islamic influence; orientalism; collectionism
materials: Silk and metallic threads; lampas weave

en.name: Ewer
description: The rounded body has flat sides, and is inscribed with Arabic script. It stands on a conical base with a long, slender neck bearing seven protrusions. The vessel has a lid, broken at the riveted section. From the body rises a long spout, inclined forward, with a hexagonal surface; its tip ends in a spur. An S-shaped handle joins the shoulder to the rim, with two perforations at its lower end and a notched ornament at the centre. The conical base and neck are undecorated, while incised floral motifs adorn the shoulder and body.
keywords: Water; ewer; Ottomans; calligraphy; copper

en.name: Carpet
description:
Spanish carpet of the Holbein series, incomplete.  
Field: The field is divided into two columns with each containing five squares, one of which is incomplete. Each square houses a double-frame octagon, whose vertices are surrounded by radial geometric decorations. These converge on a central eight-pointed star that rotates counterclockwise.  
Each square is separated by a geometric valance, which is repeated successively, and whose motifs could be inspired by calligraphic stylisations.  
The background of the field is formed by reticulated polychrome motifs, leaving no part of the carpet without decoration.  
Border: Only part of border decoration is preserved on one of its narrower sides and consist of stylised plants and trees.  
The carpet utilises wool of blue, red, yellow and green. According to Campana (Campana, M, 1966: Tappeti d’́occidente, p. 38) this carpet is similar to oriental productions that are known as the Holbein series.  
A similar copy is also presented in the catalogue of the Washington Textile Museum, Plate XVI.  
In Spain, very few copies of this series are preserved and the best preserved specimens can be found in the convent of Santa Clara de Medina de Pomar, although it presents great differences in colour.
artist: Workshops of Alcaraz (Old Kingdom of Murcia)

es.name: Alfombra
description:
Alfombra española de serie Holbein, no completa.  
Campo: Dividido en dos calles, y cada una de ellas contiene cinco cuadrados, uno de ellos incompleto. Cada cuadrado aloja un octógono de doble marco, de cuyos vértices salen decoraciones geométricas radiales. Éstas confluyen en una estrella central de ocho puntas que gira en sentido inverso a las agujas del reloj.  
Las calles y registros están separados por cenefas de tipo geométrico, que se repiten sucesivamente, y cuyos motivos podrían estar inspirados en estilizaciones caligráficas.  
El fondo del campo está formado por motivos reticulares polícromos, no dejando ninguna parte sin decorar.  
Marco: Sólo conserva parte de la decoración del marco en uno de sus lados estrechos, compuesta por plantas y árboles esquemáticos.  
La lana utilizada es de color azul, rojo, amarillo, verde y fondo en lana en su color. Según Campana (Campana, M, 1966: Tappeti d´occidente, p. 38) está alfombra es similar a las producciones orientales, conocidas como serie Holbein.  
En catálogo del Textil Museum de Washington, lámina XVI, se presenta un ejemplar semejante.  
En España se conservan muy pocos ejemplares de esta serie, siendo el ejemplar mejor conservado, el del convento de Santa Clara de Medina de Pomar, aunque presenta grandes diferencias en el colorido.

en.name: Processional Altar of St. John the Evangelist
description:
A silver processional altar made at the beginning of the 18th century, which belonged to the Royal Monastery of Our Lady of Conception, and was used in the Procession of the Holy Sacrament in Beja. The social and religious significance of the Corpus Christi Day procession cannot be understated; it represents one of the greatest manifestations of the Portuguese Baroque, which once acknowledged, justifies the sumptuousness of some of the pieces used in these ceremonies. Traditionally, up until 1893, the altar was carried by farmers.  
Rectangular in shape, the *acroteria* (small bases placed at the four extremities) has a beaded edging, and four *albarradas* or ornamental vases, alternate with smaller jars in the middle. The entirety is covered with vegetable and scalloped-shell ornamentation, and St. James' crosses. The wooden carrying rods are also silver plated.  
The octagonal shaped pedestal stands over the main body, decorated with double scalloped-shell ornamentation, pear-shaped “tables” and St. James' crosses. There is also an octagonal platform with small jars placed at each corner of the pedestal.  
An iron column rises above the pedestal, covered with silk cloth embroidered with gold thread. It meets a gold and silver halo embellished with precious stones above which a gold and silver crown rests, also studded with precious stones. In the middle of the altarpiece, the Martyrdom of St. John the Evangelist is played out, the saint graphically shown immersed in boiling olive oil. The wooden effigy of the saint with clasped hands looks straight up at the sky. The silver boiler, standing on a silver tripod above the fire, is kept alight by two multicoloured wooden figures, kneeling at either side of the boiler. One of them is blowing and the other is using a solid-silver pitchfork.  
The patrons of the altarpiece were a group of nuns devoted to St. John the Evangelist. There was another group of nuns in the same convent that devoted themselves to St. John the Baptist and commissioned a similar processional altar in honour of the saint. In fact, both altarpieces date from the beginning of the 18th century and were made in the same workshop. They both show the same crowned stamps of the city of Lisbon and the same maker's letter “M”.

A silver processional altar made at the beginning of the 18th century, it portrays features typical of the Portuguese Baroque at the time of King João V. Designed to represent the Martyrdom of St. John the Evangelist, the piece belonged to the Royal Monastery of Our Lady of Conception and was used in the procession of the Holy Sacrament in Beja, on Corpus Christi Day.
place: Royal Monastery of Our Lady of Conception, Beja
keywords: Processional altar; Mosteiro da Conceição; St.John the Evangelist; worship; Corpus Christi; Beja; religious furnishing; religious object
materials: Gilded and painted wood with silver and precious stones
tags: Gilded and painted wood with silver and precious stones

pt.name: *Altar de procissão de São João Evangelista*
description:
Peça em prata do século XVIII, pertencente ao Real Mosteiro de Nossa Senhora da Conceição, tradicionalmente transportado pelos hortelões de Beja, até ao ano de 1893, na procissão do Santíssimo Sacramento. A procissão era uma das manifestações, por excelência, do Portugal barroco, o que justifica a opulência de algumas peças destinadas a serem exibidas nestas cerimónias.  
Este andor, em prata lavrada de forma «rectangular e de moldura perolada», apresenta nas extremidades quatro albarradas ou vasos ornamentais, alternando, nos espaços intermédios, com o mesmo número de jarrinhas e é revestido por ornamentação vegetalista, vieiras e cruzes de S. Tiago; as varas móveis de transporte em madeira são revestidas de prata.  
Sobrepõe-se a este corpo principal a peanha, de forma octogonal, decorada com duplas vieiras, tabelas em forma de pêra e cruzes de S. Tiago. Ainda sobre este corpo, está um estrado octogonal com jarrinhas colocadas nos quatro vértices da peanha. Sobre esta, encontra-se um varão de ferro revestido de pano de seda bordado a fio dourado, resplendor de prata dourada adornado com pedras preciosas, encimado por coroa de prata dourada e também com pedras preciosas. No meio do andor, o Martírio de S. João Evangelista, com o Santo representado emerso em caldeira de azeite a ferver. A imagem, de madeira, apresenta rosto jovem, mãos postas e olhar direito ao céu. Uma caldeira em prata, sustentada sobre o fogo por uma trempe do mesmo metal, é ladeada por duas figuras masculinas em madeira policroma que, ajoelhadas, espevitam a lenha.  
O andor foi custeado pelo grupo de freiras devotas a S. João Evangelista e que rivalizava, dentro do Convento da Conceição, com o partido das Baptistas, devotas de S. João Baptista. Também estas mandaram fazer um andor em honra de S. João Baptista. Aliás, ambos os andores são datáveis do início do século XVIII, pertencem à mesma oficina e apresentam os mesmos punções, coroados, da cidade de Lisboa e as marcas do ourives, que usou a letra M.

Andor em prata do segundo terço do século XVIII, representando o Martírio de S. João Evangelista, com características barrocas, peculiares do meio artístico português do reinado de D. João V. Pertenceu ao Real Mosteiro de Nossa Senhora da Conceição e saía na procissão do Santíssimo Sacramento, em Beja, no dia de Corpo de Deus.
place: Real Mosteiro de Nossa Senhora da Conceição.
keywords: Andor, Mosteiro da Conceição, S. João Evangelista, Beja, devoção corpo de Deus.
materials: Madeira entalhada e pintada; prata; pedras preciosas.
tags: Andor, Mosteiro da Conceição, S. João Evangelista, Beja, devoção corpo de Deus.

en.name: *Firman*
short_description: The official permit, or *firman*, confirming the appointment of Henry Salt to the post of British Consul in Egypt, dated 23 December 1815. The imperial cipher at the top is flanked by floral motifs. This is a fine manuscript with exquisite Arabic calligraphy and watercolour and gold floral decorations. When Salt arrived in Egypt in 1816 he obtained permission from the Pasha, Mohammed Ali, to collect antiquities for the British Museum.

en.name: Castle
description:
The importance of the Castle of Rometta is largely due to the characteristics of the site on which it is built, favourable to defense from external attack. The Muslims, in the island for about two centuries, managed to overcome the resistance of Rometta, the last of the Sicilian cities to capitulate, only after a long and exhausting siege. With such defensive capacity, sometimes Rometta assumed the role of stronghold for the City of Messina, receiving the citizens every time the city on the straits threatened to cede to adversity. These natural protective works  
were a severe test of the terrible siege carried out by Ibn Amman in 965. In their turn, the Muslims, unable to defend Messina from the attacks of the Byzantine troops led by Giorgio Maniace, moved the main hub of Saracen resistance to Rometta. After the reconquest by the Normans, Federico II of Swabia included Rometta among the strongholds, in his plans for the reconstruction of the defensive system of Sicily.  
The most significant of today’s *castrum* is represented by a group of ruins. Only two of the many buildings that once formed it remain, at both ends of the rise functioning as *masti*, while those in between, which had formed the connecting links, were destroyed. The remaining structures are spread out into  
groups of different lengths: the first, which was by far the largest, in the eastern spur, the second in the western. This diversity in development is the consequence of the orographic  
configuration. The structure of the walls is in general formed by masonry arranged in strata through the introduction of small rows of bricks. The calcareous stone, cut in perfect square  
ashlars, is often used in corners, doors and windows jambs, and arcades.

es.name: Castillo
description:
La importancia del Castillo de Rometta radica en gran parte en las características del lugar en que está ubicado, propicio para la defensa de ataques externos. Los musulmanes, en la isla desde hacía cerca de dos siglos, lograron doblegar la resistencia de Rometta, última de las ciudades sicilianas en capitular, sólo después de un largo y asfixiante asedio. Por esta capacidad defensiva, a veces Rometta desempeñó el papel de plaza fuerte de la ciudad de Mesina, acogiendo a sus habitantes cada vez que la ciudad del estrecho amenazaba con ceder a las adversidades. Estas defensas naturales pusieron a dura prueba el terrible asalto desencadenado en 965 por Ibn Amman. A su vez, los musulmanes, incapaces de defender Mesina de los ataques de las tropas bizantinas guiadas por Giorgio Maniace, desplazaron a Rometta el centro de la resistencia sarracena. Después de la reconquista normanda, Federico II de Suevia incluyó Rometta entre los baluartes de su plan de reconstrucción del sistema defensivo siciliano.  
Lo más interesante del actual *castrum* lo constituye un grupo de construcciones en ruinas. De los numerosos espacios que lo formaban, quedan sólo los de los extremos de la elevación con funciones de *mastio*, mientras que se han destruido los intermedios, de comunicación. Los espacios supervivientes están distribuidos en dos núcleos de diversa extensión: el primero, mucho más vasto, en el espolón oriental; el segundo en el occidental. Tal disparidad en su desarrollo es consecuencia de la configuración orográfica. El aparejo mural es, en general, de albañilería distribuido en estratos mediante la introducción de pequeñas hiladas de ladrillo. La piedra calcárea, cortada en sillares perfectamente escuadrados, se utiliza frecuentemente en cantoneras, jambas de puertas y ventanas, arcadas.

en.name: Mosque of Rihbat al-Andalus
description:
The Mosque of Rihbat al-Andalus is the first Morisco Great Mosque of Testour, as the building dates from 1018/1610. After the building of a new Great Mosque in around 1024/1615, the former lost its place as the town’s first sanctuary; however, it continued to hold a Friday *khutba*. The monument was abandoned towards the middle of the 13th/19th century, a period during which the town went into decline. Since then, the monument became considerably degraded, falling almost entirely to ruin. In fact, the only remains that can be seen today are a half demolished minaret, two corners of the walls of the oratory, and various other remains that are barely apparent. The corners of the walls that still stand, stripped of their facing, reveal the stone bonds that constitute their construction. It consists of a composite bonding technique composed of a brick frame and concrete filling.  
The minaret is actually missing its entire top half; its original appearance is known to us thanks to photographs that were taken at the beginning of the 20th century. It was made up of two superimposed towers, a lower one that was a square-plan tower whilst the other was octagonal. The two towers were crowned by a lantern. The square tower, which still stands today, rises to a height of 9 m; supported on a base of recycled freestone, it is built using a mixed bond. The bricks in each of the four corners form chains of dog-tooth ornamentation cut across by horizontal levels. This framework of bricks is filled in with rubble bonded with lime mortar.

es.name: Mezquita de Rihbat el-Andalus
description:
La mezquita Rihbat el-Andalus es la primera Mezquita Mayor morisca de Testur, ya que el edificio data de 1018/1610. Después de la edificación de una nueva Mezquita Mayor hacia 1024/1615, esta perdió su función como primer santuario de la ciudad, aunque continuaba pronunciándose allí la *jutba* de los viernes. El monumento fue reutilizado hacia mediados del siglo XIII/XIX, época de declive de la ciudad. Después, el monumento fue degradándose considerablemente y cayó en ruinas. Actualmente no queda más que el alminar medio demolido, dos paneles del muro del oratorio y algunos otros restos apenas perceptibles. Los paneles del muro que aún se mantienen en pie, desposeídos de su revestimiento, muestran el aparejo de piedra con que fueron construidos. Se trata de un aparejado mixto, constituido por una armadura de ladrillos y un relleno de masa.  
El alminar actualmente está desprovisto de su mitad superior y sólo conocemos su aspecto primitivo a través de fotografías tomadas a principios del siglo XX. Estaba constituido por dos torres superpuestas, la inferior de trazado cuadrado y la otra de plano octogonal. Ambas torres estaban coronadas por una lucernaria. La torre cuadrada, que aún está en pie, se eleva hasta unos 9 m. Encima de una base construida en piedra tallada de reempleo, ofrece un aparejado mixto. Los ladrillos forman, en los cuatro ángulos, unos engranajes en estrellas cortadas por los hombros horizontales de la bóveda. Esta armadura de ladrillo recibe luego un relleno en sillería, ligado con una argamasa de cal.

fr.name: Mosquée de Rihbat el-Andalous
description:
La mosquée de Rihbat el-Andalous est la première Grande Mosquée morisque de Testour puisque l’édifice date de 1018/1610. Après l’édification d’une nouvelle Grande Mosquée vers 1024/1615, celle-ci a perdu sa place de premier sanctuaire de la ville, mais elle a continué à abriter une *khoutba* du vendredi. Le monument a été désaffecté vers le milieu du XIIIe/XIXe siècle, époque de déclin pour la ville. Depuis, le monument s’est considérablement dégradé, tombant presque entièrement en ruine. Il n’en reste actuellement qu’un minaret à moitié démoli, deux pans de murs de l’oratoire et quelques vestiges à peine apparents. Les pans de murs, encore debout, dépouillés de leur revêtement, laissent apparaître l’appareil avec lequel ils ont été construits. Il s’agit d’un appareil mixte constitué d’une armature de briques et d’un remplissage de béton.  
Le minaret est dépourvu actuellement de toute sa moitié supérieure; son aspect primitif nous est connu grâce à des photographies prises au début du siècle. Il était constitué de deux tours superposées, l’une inférieure de plan carré, l’autre de plan octogonal. Les deux tours étaient couronnées d’un lanternon. La tour carrée, encore debout, s’élève à 9 m; au-dessus d’une base construite en pierre de taille de réemploi, elle offre un appareil mixte. Les briques forment aux quatre angles des chaînages à redans coupés par des arases horizontales. Cette armature de brique reçoit un remplissage en moellons relié par un mortier de chaux.

en.name: *Weapons Market Street*
short_description: A rare photo of the weapons market street that goes back more than 700 years and is located in the Darb al-Ahmar area, to the North of Cairo. It was originally called “Al-`Izzi Market”, after a relative to Prince `Izz al-Din Bahdar, one of the Bahri Mamluks who was said to live there. With the passing of time, people started calling it “Suq al-Silah" street because of its many workshops and factories that made a variety of different weapons, including spears, swords and shields. The street provided weapons to the Citadel during the Mamluk era in Egypt.
keywords: Weapons Market; Cairo Markets; Old Cairo

en.name: *La Reine de Saba: 14 costume sketches*
short_description: Charles Gounod turned to the librettists Jules Barbier and Michel Carré for advice when he was writing his great opera, and so they recommended him the legend of Hiram, the great tale narrated by Gérard de Nervale in his *Voyage en Orient*. The opera was put on in Paris in 1862. As this costume from the court of Suleiman shows, the models and costumes responded above all to the Orientalist stereotypes in vogue at the time.
keywords: Opera; Orientalism

fr.name: *La reine de Saba : quatorze maquettes de costumes*
short_description: Charles Gounod, cherchant à écrire un grand opéra, s'adresse aux librettistes Jules Barbier et Michel Carré qui lui proposent la légende d'Hiram, telle que Gérard de Nerval l'a racontée dans son *Voyage en Orient*. L'opéra est représenté à Paris en 1862. Maquettes et costumes répondent donc à l'imaginaire orientaliste alors en vogue, comme on peut le constater avec ce costume de la cour de Soliman.
keywords: Opéra; orientalisme

en.name: Church of St. Mary of Mercy: paintings by Gaspare della Vecchia
names: Church of St. Mary of Mercy
description: Gaspare della Vecchia painted the cycle of eight scenes from the Life of Christ in the Church of St. Mary of Mercy in Buje – a little town in Istria – in 1711. In the style of the Venetian school, *Wedding at Cana* summarises the characteristic composition; developed diagonally receding into the depth of the picture, inhabited by figures in motion. The stereotypical postures and the typology of the characters show the influence of Gaspare's father, Pietro della Vecchia (1603–1678).
keywords: Painting, Baroque, Venice, Buje, Gaspare della Vecchia
tags: Painting, Baroque, Venice, Buje, Gaspare della Vecchia

en.name: Icon *The Holy Seven Slav Teachers*
short_description: This icon represents icon-painting in Macedonia in the 19th century. This painted variant of the motif of the seven Slav teachers was enriched by Dimitar Dicho Zograf with the romantic awareness of the Macedonian Revival. The style of the most popular and most productive Macedonian painter in the 19th century follows the experience of the painters from that period. It was commissioned by the Robev family for the church of St. Nicholas Gerakomia in Ohrid. It was painted on wood with oil. It represents the Slav missionaries Ss. Cyril and Methodius and their most prominent disciples Clement, Nahum, Gorazd, Sabbas and Angelariy, in a sole composition entitled as “Sedmochislenitzi” (The Seven Holy Teachers). The saints' names are inscribed in the Old Church Slavonic language.
keywords: Icon; iconography

description: This large wood rectangular trunk with a back-hinged lid is supported on four legs joined by a scalloped apron. The trunk is extensively inlaid with mother-of-pearl on its top, front, sides, and base. On the front, a flower and vase motif and a floral spray flank a central lattice-filled roundel. A highly ornate trefoil and geometric band runs along the edges of the central panel. The interior is unornamented with one compartment at left and two small shelves at right.
