ar.name: تابوت بدر الشرفي.
description:
يعتبر تابوت بدر الشرفي مثالاً رائعاً على نقش الحجر بالزخرفة الكتابية الكثيفة، وتحفة للخط الأتابكي، وهو مستطيل الشكل، مصنوع من الحجر، يعلو حجارة الزوايا أشكال معمارية مقببة. يظهر على اللوحة المركزية رثاء للمتوفى محاطة بإطار زخرفي شبه منحرف، الجوانب الأفقية مستقيمة في حين أن الجوانب الشاقولية المائلة مدببة ومنحنية، وهي مقسمة بالتساوي عبر الوسط لتتسع لسطرين من الكتابة: "بدر بن عبد الله الشرفي توفي في ذو القعدة مئة أربعة عشرة و خمسمائة"، وتتضمن كتابة أصغر العبارة التالية: "رحمه الله".  
تظهر المميزات الجمالية لهذا التابوت على سبيل المثال في المسافات المتزنة والفراغات المريحة بين الأحرف العربية، كما يبدو الإيقاع الشاقولي للأحرف العربية أنيقاً على طول الجزء الأسفل من أشرطة الكتابة، على أرضية ناعمة من أوراق الأقثية الملتفة الرقيقة التي تمتد عبر الجزء العلوي من الأشرطة. التباين الناعم بين الكتابة ذات الزوايا مع النماذج النباتية الملتفة يحترم الإبداع والحساسية الخاصة بالكتابة الكوفية الأتابكية.  
على الرغم من أن الرثاء يعطي الاسم والتاريخ الدقيقين، إلا أنه لا يوجد أي مصدر تاريخي يذكر اسم بدر الشرفي، ويبدو أنه كان أحد أفراد عائلة من النخبة العسكرية خلال حكم الأتابك طغتكين لدمشق لصالح السلطان السلجوقي دقاق الذي حكم في الفترة 497-507/ 04-1113.  
يقع قبر بدر الدين الشرفي في أقدم مقبرة في دمشق، وهي مقبرة باب الصغير الواقعة في الزاوية الجنوبية الغربية من المدينة القديمة. وقد تم نقل القبر بسرية في وقت ما خلال القرن الماضي، لكن الدراسات حفظت رسماً لشاهد عيان للتابوت في مكانه الأصلي. المقبرة نفسها هامة من الناحية الرمزية لأنها المكان الذي سقط فيه الصحابة عام 13/ 634 عند فتح دمشق، وعندما دمر العباسيون كل آثار الأمويين خصومهم، لم يتبق أي أثر لهذه الدلائل المبكرة، كما كان الموقع هاماً للفاطميين الذين بجلوا أفراد عائلة الرسول ومقابرهم، ولاسيما المنحدرين من ابن أخيه الإمام علي. تم توسيع المقبرة وتجديدها خلال حكم الأتابكة، وتم بناء الكثير من القبور التي تحمل أسماء الصحابة والخلفاء الأمويين الذين توفوا منذ أكثر من خمسمائة عام على الطراز السلجوقي الأتابكي، مما يدل على أهمية الموقع. حافظت المقبرة على أهميتها كمكان للحج للسنة والشيعة حتى يومنا هذا، وهي تضم قبور أفراد عائلة الرسول وسلالتهم، ومن أهمها ضريح فاطمة السبطي.

تميَّز المقام بالنقوش المتداخلة بالخط الكوفي الحاد الزوايا، وكذلك الأرابيسك ذي الخطوط المنحنية. يقرأ السطرين المكتوبين بالخط الكوفي اسم الشخص المتوفي، وهو بدر الشرفي، وكذلك سنة الوفاة 514 هـ/ 1121 م. هوية هذا الشخص غير معروفة، ولكن نوعية وتصميم المقام تدلّ على أنه كان من ذوي المناصب العليا، وعلى الأغلب أن يكون ذو منصب عسكري مهم من الاتابكة. بُني المقام في مقبرة باب الصغير، والتي تعتبر من أهم المقابر في دمشق، ولكن وفي ظلّ ظروف غامضة، تمَّ إزالة المقام منذ آخر توثيق تم تأريخه عام 1977.
keywords: خط؛ خط كوفي؛ زخرفة كتابية؛ فن جنائزي.
partner: Ministry of Culture, Directorate General of Museums and Antiquities

en.name: Cenotaph of Badr al-Sharafi.
description:
The Cenotaph of Badr al-Sharafi is a fine example of epigraphic stone carving virtuosity and a masterpiece of Atabeg calligraphy.  
The stone cenotaph is rectangular; its cornerstones surmounted by an architectonic domed composition. The central plaque displays an elegant epitaph framed by a trapezoidal cartouche; the horizontal sides are straight while the slanting vertical sides are cusped and curvilinear. It is equally divided across the middle to accommodate two lines of epigraphy: “Badr son of 'Abd Allah al-Sharafi, died in Dhu'l Qa'da, the year fourteen and five hundred”, a smaller superscript concludes: “God have mercy on him”.  
The aesthetic qualities of this cenotaph warrant appreciation and are seen in, for example, the balanced breadth and comfortable spacing of the Arabic lettering. The rhythmic verticality of the Arabic letters are elegantly inscribed along the lower portion of the epigraphic bands and placed over a delicate background of thin and scrolling acanthus leaves that run across the upper portion of the bands. This subtle contrast of angular, non-superfluous calligraphy with spiralling vegetal motifs, is tribute to the creativity and sensitivity of Atabeg *kufic* epigraphy.  
Even though the epitaph gives an exact name and date, there are no records of anyone by the name of Badr al-Sharafi in the available contemporary histories. He was probably a member of the military elite at the time of Atabeg Tughtigin, Governor of Damascus for the Seljuq Sultan Duqaq (r. AH 497–507 / AD 1104–13).  
Badr al-Sharafi's tomb was located in the oldest cemetery in Damascus: the cemetery of Bab al-Saghir, in the southwestern corner of the old city. The tomb was mysteriously removed some time over the previous century, but academic sources fortunately preserved an eye-witness drawing while the cenotaph was still *in situ*. The cemetery itself is symbolically important, known to have been the sight where the conquering *Sahaba* (companions of the Prophet) fell in AH 13 / AD 634 while taking over Damascus. As the 'Abbasids destroyed any traces of their Umayyad predecessors and antagonists, none of this early material evidence survived. The site was important for the Fatimid dynasty who venerated the family of the Prophet and their burial sites, particularly those descended from his nephew, the Imam Ali. Under the Atabeg Turks, the cemetery was grandly renovated and expanded. Many tombs executed in the Seljuq Atabeg style, which anachronistically carried the names of the *Sahaba* and the Umayyad caliphs that had died nearly half a millennium before, were constructed at this time signifying the historical importance of the site.  
The cemetery continues to be a popular site of pilgrimage to this day for both Sunni and Shi'i visitors. It houses the tombs of members and descendants of the Prophet's family, most notably the Mausoleum of Fatima Al-Sibti.

The delicate interlacing of angular *kufic* script with curvilinear arabesques is a very attractive feature of this cenotaph. The two lines of inscription indicate the name of the deceased, Badr al-Sharafi, and the year of his death, AH 514 / AD 1121. Although the identity of this person is unknown, the refined quality of the cenotaph indicates he was probably of high rank, perhaps a member of the Atabeg military elite. The cenotaph was originally located in the Bab al-Saghir cemetery, the most important burial grounds of Damascus, but it has been mysteriously removed since it was last documented in 1977.
keywords: Inscription; funerary art; epigraphy; kufic script
partner: Ministry of Culture, Directorate General of Museums and Antiquities

es.name: Cenotafio de Badr al-Sharafi.
description:
El cenotafio de Badr al-Sharafi constituye un magnífico ejemplo del virtuosismo que puede alcanzar la talla epigráfica en piedra y una obra maestra de la caligrafía atabeg.  
Se trata de un cenotafio rectangular de piedra, con los ángulos coronados por una composición arquitectónica abovedada. La placa central presenta un elegante epitafio enmarcado en un cartucho trapezoidal; el borde superior e inferior son rectos, mientras que los laterales están inclinados y son curvilíneos. Está dividida horizontalmente en dos líneas epigráficas. La mayor reza: “Badr, hijo de Abd Allah al-Sharafi, murió en *du’l-qa’dah* del año catorce y quinientos”; la superior, menor, dice: “Que Dios se apiade de él”.  
La calidad estética de este cenotafio resulta evidente, y se aprecia, por ejemplo, en el ancho equilibrado y el cómodo espaciado de las letras, la verticalidad rítmica de estas –elegantemente emplazadas en la parte inferior de las bandas epigráficas– y el delicado fondo de hojas de acanto enrolladas que se extiende por la parte superior de las bandas. Este sutil contraste entre la caligrafía angular nada superflua y los motivos vegetales en espiral prueba los méritos de la creatividad y la sensibilidad de la epigrafía cúfica atabeg.  
Aunque el epitafio menciona una fecha y un nombre determinados, las fuentes de la época no reflejan la existencia de nadie llamado Badr al-Sharafi. Posiblemente fue un miembro de la élite militar de la época del atabeg Tugtigin, gobernador de Damasco durante el mandato del sultán selyuqí Duqaq (497-507 / 1104-1113).  
La tumba de Badr al-Sharafi estaba en el cementerio de Bab al-Sagir, que es el más antiguo de Damasco y se encuentra en el extremo suroccidental de la ciudad antigua. Desapareció misteriosamente en algún momento del siglo pasado, pero, afortunadamente, fuentes académicas conservan un dibujo que realizó un testigo presencial cuando la tumba estaba aún en su sitio. El cementerio reviste una importancia simbólica, ya que se sabe que fue allí donde cayeron los *Sahaba* (compañeros del Profeta) en 13 / 634 durante la conquista de Damasco. Sin embargo, no se conserva ningún vestigio de las primeras épocas, ya que los abbasíes destruyeron todos los rastros que dejaron los omeyas, sus predecesores y enemigos. El sitio fue importante para la dinastía fatimí, que veneraba a la familia del Profeta –sobre todo a los descendientes de su sobrino, el imam Ali– y sus lugares de enterramiento. Con la llegada de los atabegs turcos, el cementerio fue sometido a una gran renovación y ampliación. En esta época se construyeron muchas tumbas en el estilo selyuqí atabeg, que ponían de relieve la importancia histórica del lugar, ya que constaban de inscripciones anacrónicas con los nombres de los *Sahaba* y los califas omeyas que habían muerto medio milenio antes.  
Hoy en día, el cementerio sigue siendo un popular destino de peregrinación tanto para sunníes como para shiíes. Alberga las tumbas de miembros y descendientes de la familia del Profeta, entre las que destaca el mausoleo de Fátima al-Sibti.

Uno de los rasgos más atractivos del cenotafio es su delicada escritura cúfica angular, finamente entrelazada con arabescos curvilíneos. Las líneas de la inscripción mencionan el nombre del difunto, un tal Badr al-Sharafi, y el año de su muerte, 514 / 1121. Se ignora quién era, pero la refinada calidad del cenotafio indica que se trataba de alguna personalidad, posiblemente un miembro de la élite militar atabeg. El cenotafio estuvo originalmente en el cementerio de Bab al-Sagir, el más importante de Damasco, pero desapareció misteriosamente y la última referencia que existe de él data de 1977.
dates: *Du’l-qa’dah* de 514 de la Hégira / enero-febrero de 1121 d. C.
keywords: inscripción; arte funerario; epigrafía; escritura cúfica.
partner: Ministry of Culture, Directorate General of Museums and Antiquities

fr.name: Cénotaphe de Badr al-Charafi.
description:
Le cénotaphe de Badr al-Charafi est un bel exemple de virtuosité dans le domaine de la sculpture épigraphique, et un chef-d'œuvre de la calligraphie atabeg.  
Structure de forme rectangulaire, ses quatre angles soutiennent une construction architectonique en coupole. La plaque centrale présente une élégante épitaphe dans un cartouche trapézoïdal. Les côtés horizontaux sont rectilignes, les côtés latéraux chanfreinés. Elle contient deux bandeaux de texte d'égale hauteur : "Badr fils d'Abd Allah al-Charafi, mort en Dhoul Qaada, l'an quatorze et cinq cents \[514\]." Et : "Dieu ait pitié de lui."  
La qualité esthétique de cette inscription s'apprécie dans l'espacement équilibré des caractères arabes, la verticalité rythmée des lettres et la finesse du fond délicatement décoré de feuilles d'acanthes en rinceaux qui courent en partie supérieure des bandeaux. Le contraste subtil entre la magistrale calligraphie anguleuse et les motifs végétaux en spirales illustre la créativité et la sensibilité de l'épigraphie coufique atabeg.  
Même si l'inscription fournit une date et un nom précis, le personnage cité est par ailleurs inconnu. Il était probablement membre de l'élite militaire à l'époque de Toughtigin, gouverneur de Damas pour le sultan seldjoukide Duqaq (r. 497-507 H / 1104-1013 J.-C.).  
Cette tombe est située dans le plus ancien cimetière de Damas, celui de Bab al-Saghir, dans la partie sud-ouest de la ville ancienne. Elle a mystérieusement disparu au cours du siècle dernier, mais un dessin précis en avait heureusement été réalisé lorsqu'elle se trouvait encore sur place. Ce cimetière possède une grande importance symbolique car c'est là que seraient tombés les Sahaba (compagnons du Prophète) en 13 H / 634 J.-C. lors de la prise de Damas. Comme les Abbassides détruisirent toute trace de leurs prédécesseurs et adversaires omeyyades, aucune preuve de ces événements n'est parvenue jusqu'à nous. Le site était également important pour la dynastie fatimide, qui vénérait la famille du prophète et ses sites funéraires, en particulier ceux des descendants de son neveu, le prophète Ali. Sous les Atabegs turcs, le cimetière fut rénové et agrandi. De nombreux tombeaux édifiés dans le style atabeg seldjoukide, qui portent anachroniquement les noms des califes Sahaba et omeyyades morts près de mille ans auparavant, ont été édifiés à cette époque.  
Ce cimetière reste un lieu de pèlerinage, aussi bien pour les sunnites que les chiites. Il abrite les tombes de membres et descendants de la famille du Prophète, notamment le mausolée de Fatima al-Sibti.

Les délicats entrelacs d'écriture coufique angulaire et d'arabesques curvilignes font partie des caractéristiques particulièrement séduisantes de ce cénotaphe. Les deux lignes d'inscription fournissent le nom du défunt, Badrt al-Charafi, et l'année de sa mort, 514 (1121 J.-C.). Bien que l'on ne sache rien de lui, le raffinement de son cénotaphe signale sans doute un personnage de haut rang, peut-être membre de l'élite militaire atabeg. Il se trouvait à l'origine dans le cimetière de Bab al-Saghir, le plus important de Damas, mais a été mystérieusement déplacé depuis qu'il a été étudié pour la dernière fois en 1977.
keywords: Inscriptions ; art funéraire ; épigraphies ; écriture coufique
partner: Ministry of Culture, Directorate General of Museums and Antiquities

de.name: Innenraum gegen den Chor
description: Die Wirkung des Innenraums in der Idealansicht von Westen ist durch die mächtigen Wandpfeiler bestimmt, die das Auflager für die reinen Halbkreisbögen doppelter Quer- und einfacher Längsgurte bilden. In ihrer Abfolge entsteht, wie bei Wandpfeilerkirchen üblich, ein kulissenartiger Prospekt, doch ist der Raum hier durch die Reihung von nur drei Einheiten (zwei Langhausjoche und Chor) so kurz, dass er sich fast einem Zentralbau annährt. Der Hochaltar mit dem Gnadenbild, der frei in der Mitte des Chors aufgestellt ist, erscheint somit nicht als fernes Ziel, sondern rückt optisch gleichsam in die Mitte der Raumfolge, zumal in der Würdeform seines Ziboriums das Vierbogengerüst der beiden Langhausjoche nachklingt.

en.name: Interior opposite the choir
description: The effect generated by the interior in the ideal view from the west is determined by the massive pilasters, which form the support for the pristine semi-circular spans of the double transverse and single longitudinal arches. Their arrangement generates, as is usual for pilaster churches, a coulisse-like prospect, however the room is so short due to the sequence of only three elements (two nave bays and choir) that it almost has the appearance of a central-plan building. The high altar with the miraculous picture, which is situated free-standing in the middle of the choir, thus appears, not as a distant goal, but as quasi the centre of the spatial sequence, especially as the grandeur of its ciborium echoes the four-arched structure of the two-nave bays.

en.name: Sprinkler
description: A sprinkler of white opaque glass decorated with a female figure holding a basket in a garden and with flowers. The neck bears coloured bands. A product of Bohemian workshops, probably for the Ottoman market.
keywords: Benaki Museum; glass; sprinkler; enamelled; figural; Bohemian; Ottoman market

en.name: *Comares Courtyard at the Alhambra*
names: *El Patio de Comares, la Alhambra de Granada*
description: The monument of the Alhambra, the last palace of the kingdom of Granada, fascinated travellers to Spain during the nineteenth century. Sorolla saw it for the first time in 1902 and in his successive trips to Granada during 1909, 1910 and 1917 he painted it, away from the Orientalist clichés, focusing on its corners, and especially in its gardens and fountains. In this view of the Patio de Comares, he highlights the reflection of the arches over the pond and a set of mirrors that is repeated in successive rooms of the palace.
keywords: The Alhambra; Painting development

en.name: Balkans, exiled civilians on the move
short_description: The First Balkan War (1912–1913) saw the Ottoman Empire at war with Serbia, Bulgaria and Greece. The violent nature of the conflict caused many populations to be displaced.
keywords: Forced migration; exodus; Balkans

fr.name: Balkans, exil de civils sur les routes
short_description: La première guerre balkanique (1912-1913) oppose la Serbie, la Bulgarie et la Grèce à l'Empire ottoman. La violence des combats entraîne des déplacements très importants de populations.
keywords: Migrations forcées; exodes; Balkans

en.name: *Der Tag wird kommen (The Day will Come)*
description:
This bright, colourful tapestry is made from dyed wool. Four rectangular fields seem to be in front of a white background with a bright red sun. The upper right field shows five male figures with arms stretched towards the sky. They stand naked upon a field of skeletons and flowers symbolizing a graveyard. The living and the dead are separated by formal antagonisms in respect to orientation, flesh, eyes and hands. The shape of the people’s bodies and limbs, however, parallels the bone structure of the dead. The artwork’s title translates to “The Day will Come”, which might point to a resurrection of the dead accompanied by the downfall of earth, symbolized by the tilting flowery fields on the left side of the tapestry.  
In her use of colour, human shape and ornament, Margarita Pellegrin is influenced by the naïve art of the South American natives. During her time in Chile, she was at first assistant and later on lecturer at Chile University in Antofagasta, both were positions that presumably served to intensify Pellegrin’s artistic exchange with local artists. The power that this artwork assigns to life and death, taking place as a magic, yet integral part of nature, might reflect a perspective linked to the close-to-nature lifestyle of the indigenous South American people Pellegrin encountered when she was living in Chile in the 1960s.  
The artist studied at Dresden Hochschule für Bildende Künste, where she met her future husband Hernando Léon. In 1963, she moved to Chile with him. From 1964-69, she worked at Chile University in Antofagasta. After the military coup in 1973, she returned, together with her husband and their three children, to the German Democratic Republic. Since then, she had been living as a freelance artist in Dresden until her death in 2016.
keywords: cotton; wool; design; floral motifs; human figure; Paradise; tree motifs, vegetal motifs
partner: Dresden State Art Collections, Kunstfonds (Art Fund)

en.name: Water jug
description: The body of this terracotta jug is decorated with embossed Arabic inscriptions, and beginning from the end points of the inscriptions, there are raised dot-like ornaments about the size of a chickpea on the surface.

en.name: Dish with moulded decoration
description: The dish ranks among the finest examples of a rare group of pottery that first came to light in the excavations at Samarra and later in those at Susa. The group shares certain characteristics, such as the shallow form without articulation; low-relief decoration moulded with great precision; and the use of a fine glaze which covers the entire surface of the vessel, both inside and outside.

en.name: *The Tunisian post service*
short_description: This oil on canvas painting shows a scene from daily life at the Tunis post and telegraph office, built on the Rue d'Italie (now Rue Charles-de-Gaulle). One of the busiest rooms, the revenue office's great hall is, with its tremendously high ceilings, an impressive example of neo-classical architecture. Featuring elements of carved plaster and a map of Tunisia on a central marble panel, this painting faithfully reproduces the opulence of this historic building.
holder: Musée des Postes, Télégraphes et Télécommunications
keywords: Post and telegraph office; Greco-Roman style

fr.name: *La poste tunisienne*
short_description: Tableau de peinture à l’huile sur toile, il représente une scène de la vie quotidienne à l’Office des postes et télégraphes de Tunis. Edifié à la rue d’Italie, l’actuelle rue Charles-de-Gaulle, la hauteur impressionnante du grand hall de la recette municipale où le public se presse présente une architecture monumentale de style gréco-romain. Plâtre ciselé, panneaux de marbre avec un panneau central reproduisant une carte de la Tunisie, le tableau est fidèle à la somptuosité du monument.

en.name: Qarawiyin Mosque
description:
One of the most ancient and most prestigious mosques of Morocco and of the Islamic West, the Qarawiyin is also the country’s principal university, one of the oldest in the world, frequented ever since the 3rd/9th century by celebrated foreigners like Gerbert d’Aurillac, who became Pope Sylvester II at the end of the 9th century.  
Located in the heart of Fez’s *medina*, in the old Kairouanese quarter from where it derives its name, the mosque was founded in 242/857 by a noblewoman, Fatima al-Fihri. A small oratory of 100 sq.m. at its inception, holding a prayer hall of four naves parallel to the wall of the *qibla* – a design common to *medina*s – it quickly grew over the centuries both in its proportions and in its prestige, and became, from the 8th/14th century onwards, a vast “mosque-cathedral”, able to welcome over 20,000 worshippers to Friday prayers.  
A sanctuary of renown, it became the object of care and concern for monarchs across every Moroccan dynasty. In 344/956, the Settefar Zenet Governor, with financial help from the Emir of Cordoba, endowed it with a minaret whose height was equal to four times the side of its base. It is still visible today in its original state, having become the minaret to which all common plans diagramming future constructions took as a reference.  
Its architectural and decorative style displays the two parallel artistic influences present in Morocco at the time: the Andalusian influence in the treatment of the platform and in the opening of the bays; and the Ifriqiyan influence from Kairouan, revealed through the presence of a dome at its summit, which replaced the traditional skylight.  
In the 6th/12th century the Almoravids extended the prayer hall eastward, and enlarged it by adding lateral naves. They built the courtyard, *sahn*, thus endowing the mosque with the size and structure which is visible today. ‘Ali Ibn Yusuf, an Almoravid prince, embellished it further between 528/1134 and 534/1140, by involving Andalusian architects who added six stalactite, or *muquarnas*, and ribbed domes above the axial nave. The carved and painted stucco coating which they are covered in employ the use of stems and foliage in their decorative motifs, as well as single or double palm leaves and acanthus flowers, onto which inscriptions, written in Andalusian *kufic* characters, are incorporated. These decorations, borrowed mostly from the rich repertoire of andalusian-inspired floral patterns, are introduced to Morocco for the first time and subsequently become classic motifs within Moroccan decorative arts.  
At the close of the 6th/12th century, the Almohads endowed the courtyard with a marble basin, and installed a bronze chandelier which still illuminates the ribbed dome above the axial nave. Considered to be one of the most luxurious models of its kind, it shows the dexterity of the chisellers and copper engravers of the period which is also evident in the bronze surfacing of the mosque’s main doors.  
For their part, the Merinids added, during the 8th/14th century, a small room situated in the minaret, whose function it was to shelter astronomical measuring instruments: astrolabes and clocks, one of which calculated the hours of prayer.  
The Sa‘adians, in the 10th/16th century, oversaw the construction of two symmetrical pavilions in the courtyard, built to shelter the ablution basins. The pavilions recall those of the Court of Lions in the Alhambra of Granada in terms of their design and decoration.  
Numerous renovations were undertaken by the ‘Alawites, who notably built the famous library which adjoins the mosque.

es.name: Mezquita Qarawiyin
description:
La Qarawiyin, una de las mezquitas más antiguas y prestigiosas de Marruecos y del Occidente musulmán, es también la primera universidad del país y una de las más antiguas del mundo. Desde el siglo III/IX ha sido frecuentada por extranjeros célebres como Gerbert d’Aurillac, que fue elegido Papa a fines del siglo IX, adoptando el nombre de Silvestre II.  
Situada en pleno corazón de la *medina* de Fez, en el antiguo barrio de los kairuaníes —de quienes tomó el nombre—, fue fundada en el año 242/857 por una dama noble, Fatima al-Fihri. Al principio era solo un pequeño oratorio de 100 m2, con una sala de oración de cuatro naves paralelas al muro de la *qibla*, conforme a la planta medinesa; pero no tardó en desarrollarse, ganando en proporción y prestigio, para convertirse a partir del siglo VIII/XIV en una gran “mezquita-catedral” capaz de acoger a más de 20.000 fieles en la oración del viernes.  
Este famoso santuario ha sido objeto de atención y cuidados por parte de todos los soberanos de las distintas dinastías de Marruecos. En el año 344/956, el gobernador zenata, con el apoyo financiero del emir de Córdoba, levantó un alminar de una altura igual al cuádruple del lado de la base, todavía visible en la actualidad bajo su aspecto original; este modelo se convertirá en referencia obligada para construcciones posteriores.  
Su estilo arquitectónico y decorativo atestigua la doble influencia artística presente en el Marruecos de la época: andalusí en cuanto al tratamiento de la cubierta y la abertura de los vanos; e ifriqí de Kairuán en la cúpula que corona la techumbre, y que reemplaza al linternón tradicional.  
Los almorávides amplían en el siglo VI/XII la sala de oración por el lado este, añadiendo dos naves laterales. Habilitan un patio o *sahn*, confiriendo así a la mezquita la talla y estructura que presenta en nuestros días. Alí Ibn Yusef, príncipe almorávide, la embellece entre el 528/1134 y el 534/1140, recurriendo para ello a dos arquitectos andalusíes, quienes dotaron a la nave principal de seis cúpulas de mocárabes (estalactitas) con nervaduras. En el enlucido de estuco cincelado y pintado con el que están recubiertas se utilizan como motivos decorativos tallos y hojas (ataurique) junto con palmas simples o dobles, lisas o nervadas, así como palmetas y hojas de acanto, a lo que hay que añadir las inscripciones de tipo cúfico o en cursiva andalusí. Es la primera vez que se utilizan en Marruecos estos ornamentos, adoptados en la mayor parte del rico repertorio floral de inspiración andalusí, y se convertirán en motivos clásicos del arte decorativo marroquí.  
A fines del siglo VI/XII, los almohades dotan al patio de una pila de mármol e instalan una lámpara de bronce, que aún sigue iluminando la cúpula nervada de la nave principal. Esta lámpara, considerada como uno de los modelos más lujosos en su género, es un ejemplo de la destreza de los cinceladores y grabadores en cobre de la época, como puede comprobarse contemplando el revestimiento de bronce de las puertas principales de la mezquita.  
Por su parte, en el siglo VIII/XIV los meriníes añaden una pequeña cámara en el alminar para guardar los instrumentos astronómicos de medida: astrolabios, relojes y una clepsidra para calcular las horas de las oraciones.  
En el siglo X/XVI, los saadíes hicieron construir en el patio dos pabellones simétricos para albergar las pilas para las abluciones, que, por su arquitectura y decoración, recuerdan a los pabellones del Patio de los Leones de la Alhambra de Granada.  
Finalmente, los alauíes han realizado numerosas renovaciones, entre las que cabe destacar la célebre biblioteca contigua a la mezquita.

fr.name: Mosquée Qaraouiyine
description:
Une des plus anciennes et des plus prestigieuses mosquées du Maroc et de l’Occident musulman, la Qaraouiyine est également la première université du pays, et une des plus anciennes au monde, fréquentée dès le IIIe/IXe siècle par des étrangers célèbres tels Gerbert d’Aurillac, promu pape à la fin du IXe siècle sous le nom de Sylvestre II.  
Située en plein coeur de la médina de Fès, dans l’ancien quartier des Kairouanais, dont elle tire son nom, elle fut fondée, en 242/857, par une noble dame, Fatima al-Fihri. Petit oratoire de 100 m2 à ses débuts, avec une salle de prière à 4 nefs parallèles au mur de la *qibla*, conformément au plan médinois, elle ne tarda pas à se développer au fil des siècles pour gagner en proportions et en prestige, et devenir, à partir du VIIIe/XIVe siècle, une vaste “mosquée-cathédrale” en mesure d’accueillir, pour la prière du vendredi, plus de 20 000 fidèles.  
Sanctuaire renommé, elle fit l’objet de sollicitude et de soins des monarques de chaque dynastie du Maroc. En 344/956, le gouverneur zénète, avec le soutien financier de l’émir de Cordoue, la dote d’un minaret d’une hauteur égale à quatre fois le côté de sa base, visible encore aujourd’hui sous son aspect originel, qui deviendra, sur le plan des normes pour les constructions postérieures, le minaret de référence.  
Son style architectural et décoratif témoigne de la double influence artistique présente au Maroc à cette époque: influence andalouse dans le traitement de la plateforme et l’ouverture des baies; influence ifriqiyenne de Kairouan que révèle la présence d’un dôme couvrant le sommet, remplaçant le lanternon traditionnel.  
Les Almoravides, eux, étendent, au VIe/XIIe siècle, la salle de prière sur le côté est, et l’élargissent en ajoutant des nefs latérales. Ils aménagent la cour, *sahn*, conférant ainsi à la mosquée la taille et la structure qu’elle présente de nos jours. Ali Ibn Youssef, prince almoravide, l’embellit entre 528/1134 et 534/1140, en faisant appel à des architectes andalous qui parent la nef axiale de six coupoles à stalactites, *mouqarnas*, et à nervures. Les enduits de stuc, ciselé et peint, dont elles sont recouvertes utilisent comme motifs décoratifs aussi bien la tige et le rinceau que les palmes simples ou doubles, lisses ou nervurées ainsi que la palmette et la feuille d’acanthe, auxquelles s’ajoutent des inscriptions à caractère coufique ou cursifs andalous. Ces décors, empruntés pour la plupart au riche répertoire floral d’inspiration andalouse, sont introduits pour la première fois au Maroc, et deviendront par la suite des motifs classiques de l’art décoratif marocain.  
Les Almohades, à la fin du VIe/XIIe siècle, dotent la cour d’une vasque en marbre, et installent un lustre en bronze qui illumine encore la coupole nervurée de la nef axiale. Considéré comme l’un des plus luxueux modèles du genre, il témoigne de la dextérité des ciseleurs et graveurs sur cuivre de l’époque, dont témoigne, de la même manière, le revêtement en bronze des portes principales de la mosquée. Les Mérinides ajoutent, pour leur part, au VIIIe/XIVe siècle, une petite chambre située dans le minaret pour abriter les instruments astronomiques de mesure: astrolabes, horloges dont une clepsydre pour le calcul des heures de prière.  
Les Saadiens, au Xe/XVIe siècle, font construire dans la cour deux pavillons symétriques abritant les vasques pour les ablutions, qui rappellent par leur architecture et leur décoration les pavillons de la Cour des Lions de l’Alhambra de Grenade. De nombreuses rénovations ont été faites par les Alaouites qui ont, notamment, aménagé la célèbre bibliothèque attenante à la mosquée.

en.name: Tile Panel with a hunting scene
description: This tile panel depicts a hunting scene. Produced during the Safavid period in Isfaha, the tile was made using a *cuerda seca* technique in which designs were outlined by an oily substance mixed with manganese, leaving a dark outline after firing. This prevented the coloured pigments from bleeding into each other. During the Timurid and Safavid periods, this technique was widely used and later introduced to Turkey. This tile panel most likely decorated a hunting palace.
keywords: Tile; Safavid; cuerda seca

en.name: Clogs
description:
*Nanule* – clogs (Tr. *nalın*) are a major category of Ottoman footwear, worn both by men and women. They were carved from a single piece of hardwood, such as walnut, beech, boxwood or ash, held on the foot by a leather strap and usually decorated with mother-of-pearl inlay or metal plaques. The wooden soles of the clogs have two high wedges, as they were designed for use on wet floors in the hamam – a Turkish bath. The height of the clogs also protected the foot from the heat generated by underfloor heating in the bath.  
  
These clogs, from the Museum of Applied Art in Belgrade (a.n. TC-265 (1924), are made of wood. They have flared wedges, the back one expanded at the rear. The toe of the sole is square, and the heel is pointed. The soles and wedges are inlaid with mother-of-pearl and metal wire. The inlay design features mother-of-pearl triangles set within metal wire frames. The leather straps are covered with purple velvet and embroidered with vegetable motifs in couched supported technique, using metal thread and spangles. The clogs had an important place in the shared dress and living culture of the urban population in the Ottoman Balkans, which had diverse confessional and ethnic backgrounds.
keywords: nanule, clogs, hamam, dress, Balkans
materials: Wood, mother-of-pearl, metal wire, leather, silk, metal thread, spangles; inlay, velvet, embroidery

en.name: Tajedit Madrasa
description:
A Wahabite Great Mosque and Madrasa; the name Tajedit, or *Jadid* in Arabic, means “new”. However, this is an ancient monument, the foundation of which, according to oral accounts, dates back to the 3rd/9th century. Indeed, this monument was totally rebuilt, also at a very early date, all whilst preserving a part of the initial construction. The defensive elements it features date back to the 10th/16th century at the very least. What is certain is that the *madrasa* existed in the 9th/15th century because the Shaykh Yunes Ibn Ta’arit Essidghiani, then leader of the Wahabite Council, had taught there.  
Situated in Fatou, to the east of Humt Suq, this *madrasa* is a part of the line of defence that runs parallel to the north-east coast of the island. It is a multifunctional monument although teaching and defence were the main subjects that were taught. It can be seen from afar thanks to the bursting whiteness of its whitewash and its high minaret, which emerges from the ancient forest of olive trees which surrounds it. A rural mosque, it signposts its defensive nature so that it can be noted from a distance; walled in by an enclosure pierced with rectangular loopholes, it opens onto a vast courtyard whitewashed with a thick, oily coat of lime. At the centre of this enclosure, the prayer hall is isolated from the other buildings which look out onto the courtyard, like the *kuttab* which is surmounted by a large dome, the utility rooms, and the ablutions hall. The square-planned mosque rises up majestically at the centre of the courtyard. Its walls widen towards the base, lending it the appearance of a truncated pyramid. The main facade is turned eastward, and a machicolation built of rubble stone, resting on a support made of olive-tree wood, protects the entrance door; a second machicolation surmounts a second door on the northern facade. The square minaret embraces the general look of the mosque by widening out towards the base, its lantern surmounted by a small dome that rests on arcades and small masonry columns. Two buttresses flank the southern facade, reinforcing the pyramidal appearance of the whole. The facades are surmounted by a defensive wall above the roof; traces of old loopholes, which were later blocked up, still remain to remind one of the role this monument must have played in terms of the island’s security.  
The visual harmony of the whole resides in the distribution of space within the area, reserved for the occupation of functions that complement one another. One must finally note, in terms of the interior, the decoration sombrely engraved around the niche of the *mihrab*, representing geometric and floral motifs.

es.name: Medersa Tayedit
description:
Se trata de una Mezquita Mayor y una *medersa* wahabí. El nombre de Tayedit o Yadid en árabe quiere decir “nuevo”; sin embargo, tenemos aquí un monumento antiguo cuya fundación, según los testimonios orales, se remonta al siglo III/IX. De hecho, este monumento fue completamente modificado en una fecha muy antigua y conserva parte de la construcción inicial. Los elementos de defensa con los que está dotado se remontan al menos al siglo X/XVI. Lo que es seguro es que la *medersa* existía ya en el siglo IX/XV, ya que el jeque Yunus ben Taarit Esidguiani, en ese momento jefe del consejo de los wahabíes, impartió clases en ella.  
Situada en Fatu, al este de Humt Suq, esta mezquita forma parte de la línea de defensa paralela a la costa noreste de la isla. Es una mezquita multifuncional, teniendo en cuenta que sus principales funciones son la defensa y la enseñanza. Esta mezquita es visible desde lejos por su llamativa blancura y su alto alminar, que emerge en el antiguo olivar que la rodea. Mezquita de campo, anuncia sus elementos defensivos, que se ven también desde lejos. Es un recinto con un cercado horadado por barbacanas rectangulares, que se abre sobre un amplio patio encalado. En medio de este cercado, la sala de oración está aislada de las otras construcciones que dan al patio, como el *kuttab*, coronado con una gran cúpula, las habitaciones de servicio y la sala de abluciones. La mezquita, de planta cuadrada, se sitúa majestuosamente en medio del patio. Sus muros se van ensanchando hacia la base, dándole un aspecto de pirámide truncada. La fachada principal se abre hacia el este, y un matacán construido con sillería, que reposa sobre un soporte de madera de olivo, protege la puerta de entrada. Un segundo matacán corona una puerta secundaria en la fachada norte. El alminar cuadrado toma el aire general de la mezquita, ensanchándose hacia su base. Posee una lucernaria coronada por una cúpula que reposa sobre arcadas y columnitas de madera. Dos contrafuertes flanquean la fachada sur y refuerzan el aspecto piramidal del conjunto. Las fachadas están coronadas por un muro defensivo encima del tejado. Las huellas de las antiguas barbacanas, abiertas posteriormente, permanecen todavía para recordarnos el papel que ha representado este monumento en la defensa de la isla.  
La armonía del conjunto reside en la distribución de los volúmenes en un espacio delimitado para ser ocupado por las funciones que se complementan. Hay que resaltar, finalmente, que en el interior la decoración es sobria, grabada alrededor del nicho del *mihrab* con motivos geométricos y florales.

fr.name: Médersa Tajedit
description:
Grande mosquée et médersa wahabites; le nom Tajedit, ou *Jadid* en arabe, veut dire nouveau. Cependant nous avons là un monument ancien dont la fondation, selon les témoignages oraux, remonterait au IIIe/IXe siècle. En fait, ce monument fut totalement remanié à une date fort ancienne tout en conservant une partie de la construction initiale. Les éléments de défense dont il est muni remonteraient au moins au Xe/XVIe siècle. Ce dont on est sûr, c’est que la médersa existait au IXe/XVe siècle puisque le cheikh Younès ibn Ta’arit Essidghiani, alors chef du conseil des wahabites, y avait enseigné.  
Située à Fatou, à l’est de Houmt Souk, cette médersa fait partie de la ligne de défense parallèle à la côte nord-est de l’île. C’est le type de monument multifonctionnel bien que l’enseignement et la défense aient été les principales sciences enseignées. Il est signalé au loin par sa blancheur éclatante et son haut minaret qui émerge de la vieille forêt d’oliviers qui l’entoure. Mosquée de campagne, elle affiche de loin ses éléments défensifs; ceinte d’une clôture percée de meurtrières rectangulaires, elle ouvre sur une vaste cour badigeonnée à la chaux grasse. Au milieu de cet enclos, la salle de prière est isolée des autres constructions qui donnent sur la cour, comme le *kouttab* surmonté d’une grande coupole, les chambres de service, et la salle d’ablutions. La mosquée de plan carré se dresse majestueusement au milieu de la cour. Ses murs s’évasent vers la base, lui conférant l’aspect d’une pyramide tronquée. La façade principale ouvre à l’est, un mâchicoulis construit en moellons, reposant sur un support en bois d’oliviers, protège la porte d’entrée; un deuxième mâchicoulis surmonte une porte secondaire sur la façade nord. Le minaret carré épouse l’allure générale de la mosquée en s’évasant vers le bas, son lanternon est surmonté d’une coupolette qui repose sur des arcades et des colonnettes en maçonnerie. Deux contreforts flanquent la façade sud, renforçant l’aspect pyramidal de l’ensemble. Les façades sont surmontées d’un mur défensif au-dessus du toit; les traces des anciennes meurtrières, bouchées ultérieurement, sont encore là pour nous rappeler le rôle qu’a eu à jouer ce monument pour la sécurité de l’île.  
L’harmonie de l’ensemble réside dans la répartition des volumes dans l’espace délimité pour être occupé par des fonctions qui se complètent. Il faut noter enfin, à l’intérieur, la décoration sobrement gravée autour de la niche du *mihrab* représentant des motifs géométriques et floraux.

de.name: Die Glocken von Lissabon und das Sanctus singende Englein
description: Zwei kleine Fresken beziehen sich auf die Heiligsprechung des Antonius im Jahr 1232. Während die ihn anrufenden Englein die himmlische Anteilnahme an dem päpstlichen Akt verbildlichen, nehmen die Glocken auf ein dabei geschehenes Wunder bezug, nämlich daß zeitgleich in Lissabon, der Heimatstadt des Heiligen, alle Kirchenglocken ohne menschliches Zutun geläutet hätten. Die virtuose Untersicht und speziell der Realismus des Glockenstuhles erheben die Bilder in den Rang malerischer Kabinettstücke.
place: Gewölbe der Zwickelräume zwischen Oktogon- und Ovalbau

en.name: The Bells of Lisbon and the Sanctus Singing Angel
description: Two small frescoes refer to the canonisation of St. Anthony in 1232. The angels invoking him represent the heavenly participation in the pontificial act, while the bells refer to a miracle that occurred at the same time: all of the church bells in Lisbon, hometown of the saint, chimed simultaneously without human involvement. The virtuosic view from below and especially the realism of the bell cage give these images the status of pictorial showpieces.
place: Vault of the spandrel spaces between the octagonal and the oval structure
partner: University of Munich, Institute of Art History

ar.name: بورتريهات لجانجير وشاه جهان
description: يظهر هذا الآلبوم رسوم شخصية لأباطرة المغول حيث البروتريه العلوي يبين جانجير (حكم خلال 1605- 27) في جاهاروكا في مشهد وهو يطل من النافذة بينما الأسفل بورتريه أكبر تصور ابنه شاه جهان (حكم خلال 1627- 58) بأبعاد أكبر حيث يوجد سحابة ذهبية أو هالة تحيط برأسه. والأكثر شهرة اليوم هو بناء تاج محل حيث كان شاه جهان أيضا خبيرا في الأحجار الكريمة. وفي  هذا البروتريه فإنه مزين بشكل غني بالعقود ، الأساور والحلي المتدلية من اللآلئ والزمرد والياقوت والجواهر الأخرى. وهو يرتدي عمامة ( توربان) برتقالية مزينة بسلاسل من اللؤلؤ ، الياقوت والزمرد وزينة عمامة من الياقوت الأزرق(الزفير) (ساربيك) من ريش طائر البلشون الأسود. وإن بهارج نطاقه مرصعة بالألماس وقطع الأوبال (حجر كريم ) الكبيرة. وفي وشاحه ثنيات بشكل خنجر (كاتار) وذراعه اليمنى تمسك بسيف وهو يحمل خاتمه الإمبراطوري في يده اليسرى وهذا دليل على سيادته.

en.name: Portraits of Jahangir and Shah Jahan
description: This album painting shows portraits of two Mughal emperors; the upper portrait shows Jahangir (r. 1605–27) in a *jharoka* window-scene, while the lower, larger portrait depicts his son, Shah Jahan (r. 1627–58) in greater dimensions, a golden nimbus or halo encircling his head. Most famous today for commissioning the Taj Mahal, Shah Jahan was also a connoisseur of gemstones. In this portrait, he is richly adorned with necklaces, bracelets, and pendants of pearls, emeralds, rubies, and other jewels. He wears an orange turban decorated with strings of pearls, rubies, and emeralds and a sapphire turban-ornament (*sarpech*) of black aigrette feathers. His gold belt glitters with diamonds and a large opal. In his sash is tucked a dagger or *katar*, and his right arm leans on a sword. He is holding his imperial seal on his left hand, a sign of his sovereignty.
artist: Signed by Balchand and Nadir al-Zaman
keywords: Folio; work-on-paper; works-on-paper; album; portrait; illuminated; figure; human-figure

en.name: Types of Cairo
short_description: The historical photos, belonging to Enrico H. Giglioli's collection, were collected by the Florentine naturalist during his travel around the world in 1865–68 on the Magenta's steam corvette, with the purpose to start diplomatic and commercial relations. The "genre" images seem to be created "ad hoc" to represent human diversity along the different ages. The ethnographic photographs in the Giglioli's collection are part of the historical archive of the Pigorini Museum, and are very important for the history of anthropological science and history of photography. The origins in terms of scientific activity and conservation of Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico "Luigi Pigorini" in Rome, can be traced back to the foundation in 1875 of the "Royal National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography in Rome" within the buildings of the Roman College.
holder: National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography “Luigi Pigorini”
keywords: Woman; photograph; anthropology; ethnology; geography; travel; exploration; scientific expedition; ethnography; museums; model; genre picture; portrait; representation of the other; costume; material culture; collection; Egypt
partner: MIBACT | National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography “Luigi Pigorini”

en.name: Prayer rug
description: Outlined on the contrasting green of the central field, the red prayer niche has a stepped arch fringed with hooks along its inner edges. Inside the niche, a floral composition encircled by 12 tiny ewers recalls the mosque-lamp motif. A recurrent motif of prayer rug designs, ewers are traditionally associated with an *aide-mémoire* meant to remind the believer of the ritual ablution required before prayer. The present rug features a main border reminiscent of the so-called Gothic border of 16th- and 17th-century carpets, and, in the upper corners of the main field, stylised vegetal motifs, which show the Western influence on Turkish art. This rather unusual blending of two stylistic sources is illustrative of the two main “forces” with a strong impact on the decorative vocabulary of 19th-century Ottoman carpets: the Turkish tradition and the influence of European art. The bright colour scheme is quite remarkable and its sharp contrasts almost shocking compared mainly to the fine colouring of the Gördes and Kula carpets that reigned supreme on the European market of Oriental carpets at the turn of the century.
holder: The National Museum of Art of Romania
keywords: prayer rug; Ghiordes
partner: The National Museum of Art of Romania

ar.name: تزويق قرآن كريم.
description:
الورقة اليمنى مأخوذة من قرآن منسوخ على ورق قضيم، وقد كتبت بالخط الكوفي الأسود بحروف ثخينة، وأشير إلى الحروف الصوتية بنقاط حمراء اللون طبقاً لأسلوب النحوي أبي الأسود، واستعملت نقاط إعجام أخرى للحروف كحركات تشكيل، وتمت الإشارة للتقسيم بين الآيات بزخرفة على شكل وردة كبيرة مذهبة وكستنائية اللون، وهي مكونة من ستة تويجات تحيط بدائرة، ومتصلة ببعضها البعض بواسطة ستة من أرباع دوائر ذات لون كستنائي.  
أما الورقة اليسرى فهي مزينة بزخرفة يتكون إطارها من شريط مستطيل، يضم زخرفة غصينة أفعوانية الشكل. تتشابك عدة دوائر ذات محيط مذهب وكستنائي، وتشكل زخرفة هندسية مكونة من ثلاثة صفوف من الجدائل تشكل الزهرة ذات الفصوص الأربعة العنصر الزخرفي الطاغي عليها. في حين، صبغت السطوح المحيطة بها باللون الأخضر. ورسم على الهامش اليساري إكليل مكون من دائرة محاطة بنقاط خضراء ومذهبة، تحوي داخلها سبعة أوراق مبسطة ومذهبة، على خلفية بيضاء اللون، موشاة بنقاط سوداء وخضراء اللون.

أخذت الورقة اليمنى من قرءان منسوخ على ورق قضيم؛ وكتبت بالخط الكوفي الأسود. تمت الإشارة إلى تقسيم الآيات بواسطة وريدة مذهبة وكستنائية؛ وأثثت الورقة اليسرى بتزويق يتكون إطاره من شريط مستطيل يحوي غصينة أفعوانية الشكل.
place: (هنا المصدر) من المرجح أن يكون القيروان لأنها كانت خلال تلك الفترة مركزاً كبيرا لإنتاج الكتب.
keywords: فن الخط؛ الزخرفة النباتية؛ الزخرفة الهندسية.

en.name: Illumination of a Qur’an.
description:
Taken from a Qur'an copied on parchment, the right-hand page is written in thick, black *kufic* characters. The vowels are marked with red dots, in the style of Abi al-Aswad. Other diacritical dots are used as orthographic signs. The division between the verses is indicated by a large gold and brown rosette consisting of six petals surrounding a circle, linked by six brown quarter-circles.  
The left-hand page has an illumination framed by a rectangular ribbon enclosing snake-like ornamental foliage. Several interlinked circles on the gold and brown outer edges form three rows of interwoven geometric decoration whose main motif is a four-lobed fleuron.  
The surrounding area is coloured green. A crown motif projecting towards the left-hand margin is made up of a circle surrounded with green and gold dots and containing stylised gilded leaves.  
The white background is covered with green and black dots.

Taken from a Qur'an copied on vellum, the right-hand page is written in black *kufic* script. The division of verses is marked by a large gold and brown rosette. The left-hand page contains an illumination framed by a rectangular band containing serpentine foliage.
place: Very likely from Kairouan, a great centre for book production at that time.
keywords: Calligraphy; floral decoration; geometric decoration; religious manuscript

es.name: Iluminación de Corán.
description:
Dos páginas de un Corán copiado sobre vitela. La página derecha está escrita en gruesa letra cúfica negra. Las vocales se señalan con puntos rojos, conforme al estilo de Abi al-Aswad. Otros puntos diacríticos se emplean como signos ortográficos. Marca la división entre aleyas una gran roseta dorada y marrón, formada por seis pétalos dispuestos alrededor de un círculo, unidos por seis cuartos de círculo de color marrón.  
La página izquierda está decorada con una iluminación cuyo marco está formado por una franja rectangular que contiene un follaje ornamental serpentiforme. Varios círculos con contornos dorados y marrones se entrelazan para elaborar un diseño geométrico, integrado por tres filas de trenzados cuyo ornamento predominante es un florón de cuatro lóbulos. El espacio circundante está pintado de verde. La corona proyectada hacia el margen izquierdo está integrada por un círculo rodeado de puntos verdes y dorados, con siete hojas estilizadas y doradas en su interior. El fondo blanco está salpicado de puntos negros y verdes.

Hojas extraídas de un Corán copiado sobre vitela. La página derecha está escrita en letra cúfica negra. Una gran roseta, dorada y marrón, marca la división entre versículos. fr.name: Enluminure d’un coran.
description: Tiré d'un coran copié sur du vélin, le feuillet de droite est écrit en coufique noir, les caractères sont gras. Les voyelles sont indiquées par des points rouges, conformément au style d'Abi al-Aswad. D'autres points diacritiques sont utilisés comme signes orthographiques. La division en versets est signalée par une grande rosette, dorée et marron, qui consiste en six pétales, entourant un cercle, reliés par six quarts de cercle de couleur marron. Le feuillet gauche est meublé par une enluminure dont le cadre est constitué d'une bande rectangulaire renfermant un rinceau serpentiforme. Plusieurs cercles aux pourtours dorés et marrons s'entrecroisent et élaborent un décor géométrique constitué de trois rangées de tresses dont le motif prédominant est un fleuron à quatre lobes. Les surfaces environnantes sont colorées en vert. Une couronne projetée dans la marge gauche est constituée d'un cercle entouré de points verts et dorés, dans lequel sont inscrits sept feuillets stylisés et dorés. Le fond blanc est parsemé de points noirs et verts.

place: Sans doute, Kairouan qui était, à l’époque, un grand centre de production livresque.

en.name: Iconostasis in the Church of the Holy Saviour
short_description: This iconostasis was created by one of the greatest Macedonian masters of woodcarving, Petre Filipovski Garka, who formed his own group of artisans and developed his outstanding style of wood-carving, which was widely recognizable in the Balkans in the early 19th century. This exquisite piece of wood-carving was made from walnut in the technique of high relief. The iconostasis depicts scenes from the Old and the New Testament in which biblical figures are rendered wearing traditional costumes worn in Macedonia. The detail shows the self-portraits of Petre Filipovski and his associate artisans.

en.name: Small bucket
short_description: M.A.I. was established in 1872 in Rome as a collection of manufacts (glasses, majolica, sculptures, materials, photographs, metals, casts and other) from antiquity to 19th century, and as a training school for specialising artisans, as part of the process of revaluation of the so-called "minor arts". Venetian glass has a long history, inherited from the Roman, Byzantine and Islamic tradition in the Middle Ages. The small bucket in glass cobalt-blue is decorated with crystal animal-shaped applications and gold leaves recalling ancient eastern motifs. The object was made according to the 18th century taste and recalls 15th century models of aspersoriums, or holy water basins, from Venice dating from the 16th and 17th centuries. These objects were depicted in paintings by Veronese and Carpaccio.
holder: Museo Artistico Industriale, National Gallery of Ancient Art in Palazzo Barberini

en.name: 'The Funeral of Isfandiyar'
description: From a dispersed copy of the Ilkhanid manuscript referred to as the Great Mongol Shahnama, this folio depicts the funeral procession of the Persian hero Isfandiyar. The bier is accompanied by a group of mourners, some wailing and pulling at their hair, which is worn loose as a sign of mourning. The painting technique, with its strong linear quality and thin washes of color, recalls contemporary Chinese brush painting.
keywords: Water; Shahnama; Funeral.

Maghrib (Maghreb) is the name traditionally used to refer to the western regions of the Islamic world, which once consisted not only of North Africa but also Islamic Spain. The script is copied in gold ink, outlined in black, on vellum.

en.name: Walls and ceiling of the Damascus Room
description: The Damascus Room consists of eighteenth-century *‘ajami* wood panelling (four walls and a ceiling), which would have originally decorated a reception room (typically known as a *qa‘a*) of an affluent courtyard home in Syria. It is a quintessential example of late-Ottoman Syrian architectural decoration reconstituted to meet the needs of a twentieth-century environment and collector.

en.name: Bahiya Palace
short_description: Covering an area of eight hectares, the palace consists of 150 rooms lavishly decorated with *mashrabiyya*, marble sculptures, paintings on beech and cedar, stuccowork and *zellige*. Built in two phases in the second half of the 19th century, the estate is comprised of structures built piecemeal, including outbuildings and ancillary structures: a Turkish bath, mosque and stables, and other annexed houses that are connected to each other, many of which are remarkable both in their structure and their ornamentation. Although the buildings are arranged disparately throughout the estate they are organised around several patios and green Islamic-style gardens (*al-agdal*), planted with orange, banana and cypress trees, as well as hibiscus and jasmine, and irrigated by *qanat*.
history: The site of the palace lies southeast of the Marrakesh *Medina*, close to the present royal palace. It was built in two phases by a father and son who served as grand viziers to two ‘Alawid sultans. The first part of the palace, known as Dar Si Musa ‒ the largest and most luxurious in Morocco at the time ‒ was built between 1866 and 1867 by Si Musa, grand vizier to Sultan Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman (reigned 1859-73). Between 1894 and 1900, the second phase of construction started under Si Musa’s son, Si Ahmad ibn Musa, grand vizier to two sultans Mulay al-Hasan I (1873-94) and Mulay ‘Abd al-‘Aziz (1894-1908), to designs by the architect Muhammad ibn Makki al-Misfiwi. During his reign, Ahmad ibn Musa enlarged the southern part of his father’s palace and subsequently developed a number of glamorously designed connecting houses. He lived on the grounds with four wives, a harem of 24 official concubines and their many children. Having built the palace for his favourite wife, Ahmad ibn Musa named it *Bahiya*, meaning “beautiful, brilliant”.
keywords: Islamic art; Islamic architecture; Islamic architecture in Morocco; Moroccan architects; traditional city; Islamic city; palace; royal palace; plan; urban planning; stucco; garden; patio; Islamic garden; zellij; ceramic; geometrical motifs; gardens and architecture

ar.name: ثوب الأرامل
description:
ثوب أسود للنساء الأرامل فقط، من منطقة بئر السبع، مطرز بكثافة على القبة بأشكال تشبه القلايد. الغرز والأشكال المطرزة على هذا الثوب، على عكس باقي الأثواب، يأتي مع القليل من الطيور أو الأزهار. الردهة مطرزة من الجوانب بأشكال منوعة، وفي وسطها قطعة برتقالية من الهرمزي مطرزة بقطبة اللف ببعض أشكال الزهور. الأكمام مطرزة بشكل مختلف، أما على البنايق والردفة الأمامية والخلفية، هناك تطريز كثيف أزرق اللون بعرق السرو والريش وحجابات أعلى البنايق. ومن الجدير بالذكر، أن هناك بعض التفاصيل المثيرة للاهتمام حول هذا الثوب، نجدها في أسفل الثوب (الداير)، حيث تطريز أزرق كثيف، خالٍ من التطريز في المنتصف، و يحمل ذلك معنى اجتماعيًا عميقًا. تدل هذه الجزئية على أن صاحبة الثوب أرملة وغير متزوجة، ولا تنوي الزواج مرة أخرى. من ناحية أخرى، في حالة قيام المرأة بملء الفراغ في الوسط من الأسفل بالتطريز، فهذا إعلان عن نيتها للزواج مرة أخرى.  
تاريخ الحصول على القطعة: 1983 م
dates: النصف الأول من القرن التاسع عشر
keywords: تقليدي، منسوجات فلسطينية، ثوب

en.name: Widow’s Dress from Bir al-Sabe
description: A dress for widowed women only, from Bir al-Sabe. This dress displays heavy embroidery work on the chest panel, similar to a *qalayed* (necklace) motif. The embroidery of this dress is less festive and detailed and adorned with few birds or flower motifs. The neck and shoulders are embroidered on each side and display orange *hirmizi* needlework with few flower shapes. The sleeves show varied embroidery designs, while the *banayeq* (side panels) and the front and back panels show heavy embroidery work in blue with cypress tree and feather motifs, along with talismans on the top of the side panels. This dress has a very unusual and interesting feature; at the bottom of the dress (*dyara*) there is thick blue embroidery, but the dress is devoid of embroidery in the middle. This design feature holds deep social meaning, denoting that the owner of the dress is a widowed, unmarried woman who does not intend to marry again. On the other hand, if the woman fills the gap in the middle with embroidery, this added embellishment is a declaration of her intention to marry again.
keywords: Traditional costume; Palestinian textile; Dress; Clothing

en.name: Nossa Senhora da Luz (Parish Church)
description:
The Parish Church in Ponta do Sol has been documented since 1486, when Rodrigo Anes had the church built. It was dedicated to St Mary and had a tomb in the chancel where he wished to be buried, although since then a lot of work has been carried out on the building, beginning in the early 16th century.  
Built on a simple plan with only one rectangular nave and apse, there are two Late Gothic side chapels by the crossing, acting as a false transept. The one on the left has ribbed vaulting, but the chapel on the right has only an entrance arch. The same taste and style are obvious in the delicate lines of the arch of the present Chapel of the Holy Sacrament, with delicate wood carving and a fine representation of phytomorphic elements. The late 16th-century Mudejar-tracery ceiling of the chancel is of particular interest.

en.name: Tomb of Queen Maria I
description: The Neo-Classical tomb of queen Maria I – made of white, black and pink marble over a plinth – is decorated with two urns and an inscription identifying the queen. The sarcophagus is supported by two lions. At the top is a medallion, containing an effigy of Queen Maria I, presented by Fame and a *putto.*
partner: Institute for the Administration of Architectural and Archaeological Heritage -  IGESPAR

pt.name: Túmulo de D. Maria I

Na fachada frontal, encontra-se uma inscrição que identifica a rainha, suportada por dois leões. O topo é decorado com um medalhão com a efígie da rainha D. Maria, ladeado por esculturas da *Fama* e *Putto*.

description: إن اللغة العربية الجنوبية القديمة التي هي مثل اللغة العربية الحديثة تنتمي لمجموعة اللغات السامية كانت تكتب بأبجديتها الخاصة و\النقوش التي سلمت مثل أنظمة الري ، العقود والنصوص القانونية ونقوش الإهداء والقبور بقيت مصادر مهمة لدراسة اللغة وثقافة اليمن القديم. وفي النصف الأول من القرن السابع اعتنق اليمن الإسلام ومعه الأبجدية العربية . وقد حلت اللغة العربية الشمالية مكان اللغة العربية الجنوبية القديمة

en.name: Ancient South Arabian inscription
description: The ancient South Arabian language, which like modern Arabic belongs to the Semitic language group, was written in its own alphabet. The preserved inscriptions, such as irrigation regulations, contracts, legal texts, dedicatory and grave inscriptions, remain important sources for the study of the language and culture of ancient Yemen. In the first half of the 7th century, Yemen adopted Islam and with it the Arabic alphabet. Northern Arabic supersedes the ancient South Arabian language.

en.name: Project for a steamship for the Sultan of Morocco, by the Fratelli Orlando shipyards (Livorno, Italy)
short_description:
Project drawn to a scale 1:100.  
In 1899, the Fratelli Orlando shipyards (Livorno, Italy) made a project of a screw steamer for the Sultan of Morocco. The steamer was to have two decks, two steam engines of 900 HP and harbour twelve passengers. The project, however, was never realised.  
The Fratelli Orlando shipyards built the cruiser Bascir for the Moroccan Navy and a yacht for the Khédivé of Egypt.

en.name: Hungarian Silk Rug
description: The designer of this rug was the painter and designer Pál Horti (1865-1907), one of the Hungarian pioneers in modern applied arts and a distinctive representative of the Art Nouveau style at the turn of the 20th century.                                                                                                                                                                                                               The central field is decorated with a peacock, blue-green rosette inset against a terracotta base. It is connected to the inner stripe of the border with four curved tendrils that end in leaves. The inner border is ornamented with cherry-red against a green base. The outer, wider border shows Art Nouveau wavy ornaments in cherry red, blue and yellow against a grey base. The wave turns terracotta at the corners.  The carpet was exhibited at the Turin Exhibition of 1902.
keywords: Art Nouveau; European rug; Hungarian rug; Silk; Turin Exhibition 1902

ar.name: سيف ( سيف مستقيم ذو حافتين)
description: حتى وقت قريب كان يندر توقيع الحرفي، أو الشاعر، أو الكاتب العُماني على عمله؛ فقد استمد هذا التقليد في عدم كشف الهوية من الفكر الإسلامي الإباضي؛ الذي يحث على إخلاص العمل لمرضاة الله سبحانه، وتعالى؛ وليس حبا للذات، وما زالت عادة التواضع أمام الله قائمة إلى يومنا هذا؛ إذ يتم التوقيع على الأعمال لأغراض عملية، وتوضيحية بحتة فقط. وعادة ما تكون تلك التواقيع متواضعة من حيث الحجم، والمكان، وأسلوب التنفيذ، وليس غريبا أن يوقع الحرفي على عمله مستعينا باسم بلدته، أو السوق التي يعمل فيها، بدلا من توقيعه الشخصي.

en.name: *Saif* (Straight, double-edged sword)
description: Until recently it was a rare occurrence for Omani artisans, poets, authors and others to sign their work. This custom of anonymity reflects the central belief of Ibadhi Muslims that work is done for the glory of God, not for the glory of self. Today, this custom of humility before God persists, with work being signed for reasons of practicality, not self-aggrandisement. Signatures are typically modest in terms of scale, placement and style of execution. This blade is a rare example, stamped on one side indicating it as "The work of Ali bin Rah'meen". It is common now for artisans to sign their work with the name of the town or *souq* (local market) where their workshop is located in lieu of a personal signature.
keywords: Saif; Sword

en.name: *Adoring Angel*
description:
Georg Raphael Donner was one of the most prominent and influential Central European sculptors of the first half of the 18th century. He developed his individual Neo-Classical style at a distance from the Baroque tradition, relying on models from antiquity and 16th-century Italian sculpture. His first monumental works were made for Pozsony (Bratislava) Cathedral, commissioned by Prince Primate Imre Esterházy.  
First of all he worked on the decoration for the Chapel of St. John the Almsgiver, executing the archbishop's sepulchral statue (1729–32). Later, he created the sculptural group of St. Martin and the beggar, as well as two adoring angels for the new high altar in the cathedral (1733–1735). This significant work is characterised by the perfect harmony between the sculpture and architecture; the idea and the form. The crowned canopy of the altar was originally carried by enormous free-standing fluted columns. The central figural group featured St. Martin seated on the back of a rearing horse. He shares his flowing cloak with the beggar lying on the ground. St. Martin is wearing a Hungarian noblemen's outfit and has the facial features of the archbishop. The beggar of heroic stature is looking at the saint with Christ's face, but the saint does not recognise him immediately. An external viewer of the altarpiece cannot recognise Christ's face either, because it is seen in semi-profile. Two huge kneeling angels join the scene on either side, their adoration directed towards the disguised Redeemer. Despite minor differences in movement, hand gesture and in the arrangement of drapery, the adoring angels are practically symmetrical; they are dignified celestial creatures, although their finely modelled, strong bodies are very real. Their pose expresses intimate and perfect veneration.  
The beauty of the modelling is enhanced by the subtle grey hue and silken lustre of lead, which also lends an earnest, reserved and elegant appearance to the statues. With these statues, Donner reached an initial peak of his oeuvre. The altar was dismantled in the 1860s when the cathedral was rebuilt in the Neo-Gothic style. The main group of the equestrian statue today is in the side aisle of Bratislava Cathedral, and the two adoring angels are part of the permanent collection at the Hungarian National Gallery.

The most important patron of the Viennese sculptor was Primate Imre Esterházy in Pozsony (Bratislava). The high altar of Pozsony (Bratislava) Cathedral was one of Donner's most significant works, but after it was demolished in the 19th century, the group of St. Martin and the beggar can be seen in the nave today, while the two huge angels were taken to Budapest in the 19th century.
keywords: Funerary  monument; metalwork; Italian influence; Christian themes; Pozsony; Bratislava; funerary architecture

en.name: Kilim, *Zorić’s pattern*
description: Pirot kilims were presented in many exhibitions abroad among which was the World Fair (*Exposition Universelle*) in Paris in 1900. For this occasion, engineer Svetozar Zorić, a professor at the Belgrade Higher School (future University of Belgrade), designed a pattern which was named after him *Zorić’s pattern* (*Zorićeva šara*). Different Pirot kilim patterns designed for 1900 Paris World Fair were exhibited in *Ilija M. Kolarac Endowment* in Belgrade in 1899. The exhibited patterns expressed the search for the national style inherent to arts of that period. This kilim, decorated with *Zorić’s pattern*, belongs to *šestak* (a kilim of six square ells) type, which was used as a cover for bed or wall. The colours used are: red, green, yellow, white and black.
keywords: Pirot; Şarköy; kilim; wool; weave

en.name: Oratories
description: Oratory of Our Lady of the Rosary constructed from wood and canvas. There are others dedicated to Our Lady of Mount Carmel, St. Matthew, and St. John the Baptist. With the exception of the Oratory of St. John the Baptist, the outside wings are adorned with paintings.

pt.name: Oratórios
description: Existem, hoje em dia, quatro oratórios: Nossa Senhora do Rosário, Nossa Senhora do Carmo, S. Mateus e S. João Baptista. Apresentam retábulos pintados sobre madeira ou tela e os respectivos volantes, uma vez abertos, formam, com as pinturas centrais, trípticos ou polípticos, normalmente relacionados com o tema da pintura central. Os volantes apresentam também, na face exterior, pinturas da mesma época, à excepção do oratório de S. João Baptista.

en.name: Medwakh Pipe
short_description: This small pipe has a long tradition among the local sailors and seafarers in the Gulf region, who traditionally favoured Medwakh tobacco, a particular local blend mixed with herbs, spices and aromatic bark. It was produced locally and came in three strengths, from cold (barid) to warm (dafi) and hot (har). Unlike other tobaccos, dokha, as it is known as, is not harvested and cured, its vegetal ingredients simply dried in the sun. As the dokha mixtures were very potent, they were only ever smoked in very small pipes like the one illustrated here.
holder: Sharjah Heritage Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
dates: Hegira first half of the 14th century / AD first half of the 20th century
keywords: medwakh; dokha

de.name: Äußeres
description: Am Außenbau deuten nur die geschweiften (am Langhaus glockenförmigen) Fenster auf einen Bau des Spätbarock hin. Alles übrige ist schlicht und unauffällig gegliedert, die ehemaligen gotischen Strebepfeiler wurden auf Bänder reduziert. Die Westseite mit Vorzeichen ist nicht als Schauwand gestaltet, der Giebel gar zum Wetterschutz mit den Schindeln des Daches verkleidet. Der gotische Turm mit Spitzhelm ist am Schaft unverputzt geblieben.

en.name: Exterior
description: Only the curved windows, of a bell-shape on the nave, indicate a building of the Late Baroque period. Everything else is of unimposing design and the former Gothic buttresses have been reduced to bands. The west side has not been designed as an ornamental façade and the gable has even been finished in shingles. The shaft of the Gothic tower with pointed helm roof has remained unrendered.

ar.name: صحن ذو أذنين.
description: صحن على شكل " زبدية ذات أذنين" ذو بريق معدني، ملون بلونين: عسلي وأحمر على أرضية عاجية اللون. تمت زخرفته من الداخل بنطاق مكتوب بأحرف لاتينية مسحت بفعل الزمن، ولم يبق منها إلا عبارة: "في البدء كان الكلمة" (جوفاني101) ومجموعة من النخلات المتتالية التي تشكل نطاقاً ذا بريق معدني. نجد في القعر شكل وسام مع شعار لدلفين، أما في الخارج، حيث الزخرفة التي أزالها التقادم الزمني، فإننا نستطيع رؤية بقايا رسم لورقة نبات.
هذا القدح نتاج للفن الإسباني المغربي؛ ومن المحتمل أن يكون قد أنتج في فالانسيا (إسبانيا)؛ وصنع من فخار مصبوغ مبرنق ومزخرف بنقيشة كتابية بأحرف لاتينية، وبأشكال آدمية وحيوانية.
holder: متحف الحضارات  | متحف الفن الشرقي جوزيبي توتشي
keywords: بريق معدني؛ صحن ذو أذنين؛ فن المدجنين.
