de.name: Kath. Filialkirche Heilig Kreuz, ehem. Jesuitenkirche
description: Der Herkunft ihres Architekten entsprechend wurde die Heilig-Kreuz-Kirche nach dem Muster der seit 1617 bestehenden Kirche der Jesuitenuniversität (sog. Studienkirche) im schwäbischen Dillingen an der Donau als Wandpfeilersaal erbaut, der in einen eingezogenen, tiefen und apsidial schließenden Chor mündet; einzig Detailformen wie die ornamentalisierten Fenster und Portale sowie der Rokoko-Stuck verraten die circa 150 Jahre spätere Entstehungszeit. Ebenfalls dafür kennzeichnend und vom Vorbild abweichend überziehen das Langhaus- und Chorgewölbe großflächige Deckenfresken, die das Patrozinium illustrieren. Mitgeprägt wird das Raumbild durch die stilistisch einheitlichen, nach szenografischen Gesichtspunkten arrangierten Altäre.

Die hoch über der Altstadt gelegene Jesuitenkirche prägt mit ihrer in unverputztem Tuffmauerwerk errichteten Zweiturmfassade das historische Antlitz der einstigen kurbayerischen Grenzstadt. Gemäß der Bautradition der süddeutschen Jesuiten als Wandpfeilerkirche konstruiert, ist sie ein besonders später Vertreter ihrer Gattung und weist daher eine im Rokokostil gehaltene prächtige Ausstattung auf. Raumbeherrschende vielfigurige Deckenfresken des Asam-Schülers Christoph Thomas Scheffler erzählen in dramatischen Kompositionen die Kreuzeslegende.
artist: Pater Ignatius Rhomberg SJ, Rektor des Landsberger Jesuitenkollegs
history: 1575 wurde in Landsberg das nach München zweite Jesuitenkolleg Kurbayerns gegründet, das auch ein Noviziat miteinschloss. Als letzteres um 1750 erweiterungs- und renovierungsbedürftig war, nahm man dies zum Anlaß, auch die Kollegkirche zu erneuern. Unter der Leitung des Dillinger Jesuitenbaumeisters Joseph Ignaz Merani wurde dazu ab 1752 ein großangelegter Neubau errichtet, wobei ihm offensichtlich der berühmte, in Landsberg ansässige Rokoko-Baumeister Dominikus Zimmermann bei der Gestaltung der Portale und Fenster zur Hand ging. Schon 1756 ist der zwei Jahre zuvor vollendete Kirchenbau auch weitgehend ausgestattet. Die Deckenfresken sind das letzte Werk des bei Cosmas Damian Asam geschulten Augsburger Malers Christoph Thomas Scheffler und gelten als seine bedeutendsten Werke.
keywords: Jesuitenkirche; Wandpfeilerkirche; Deckenmalerei; Hochaltar; Hl. Johann Nepomuk

en.name: Catholic Subsidiary Church of the Holy Cross, former Jesuit Church
names: Catholic Subsidiary Church of the Holy Cross, former Jesuit church
description: According to the origin of its architect, the Church of the Holy Cross was built after a specific model: the church of the Jesuit University (so-called Study Church), existing since 1617 in the Swabian town of Dillingen on the Danube. Comparable to that archetype, a hall of wall pillars leads to a recessed, deep and apsidal chancel. Only some unique details such as the ornamentalised windows and doorways as well as the Rococo-stucco betray the period of origin which is about 150 years later. Equally characteristic of this period and deviating from the archetype, extensive ceiling frescoes which illustrate the patrocinium cover the nave and chancel vaults. The appearance of the interior space  is characterised by the altars which are stylistically uniform and arranged according to scenographic perspectives.

Situated high above the old town, the Jesuit Church with its two-towered façade constructed in un-plastered tuff masonry characterises the historical visage of the former old Bavarian border town. Constructed according to the building tradition of southern German Jesuits as a wall pillar church, it is an especially late representation of its building type and therefore exhibits features in the magnificent Rococo style. Multi-figured ceiling frescoes, painted by Christoph Thomas Scheffler, student of Cosmas Damian Asam, dominate the interior space and tell the legend of the cross in dramatic compositions.
artist: Father Ignatius Rhomberg SJ, Rector of the Landsberg Jesuit College
history: In 1575, the second Jesuit College after Munich was founded in the Electorate of Bavaria and also included a noviciate. When the latter was in need of extension and renovation around 1750, this was taken as an occasion to also replace the collegiate church. As of 1752, under the direction of the Jesuit architect Joseph Ignaz Merani of Dillingen, a large-scale new building was erected for this purpose. Merani was obviously given a hand with the doorways and windows by the famous Rococo architect based in Landsberg, Dominikus Zimmermann. By 1756, the church building completed two years before was already largely furnished. The ceiling frescoes were the last work of Augsburg’s painter Christoph Thomas Scheffler, trained by Cosmas Damian Asam, and are considered as his most significant creations.
partner: University of Munich, Institute of Art History

en.name: Beyezid II Complex
description:
Even after the Capital was moved to Istanbul, Edirne maintained its importance for a long time; the Bayezid II Complex, dating from the late 15th century, together with the Selimiye Mosque, a masterly work of Ottoman architecture completed in 1575, are the structures that emphasise the importance given to this city.  
Sultan Bayezid II personally attended the ceremonies for the laying of foundations for his complex on 25 May 1484. During the ceremonies animals were sacrificed and their meat was distributed to the poor. The complex was completed in a short time; only four years, and then opened for service with great ceremony in 1488.  
There are different opinions regarding the identity of the architect who built the complex. According to some researchers, the name of the architect is Hayreddin, while some others believe that it is Yakub Şah Ibn Sultan Şah.  
The Complex of Bayezid II in Edirne, built after another complex of the same Sultan in Amasya, is a large group of buildings spread across an area of 22,000 m2, and consisting of a mosque, *madrasa*, *darüşşifa*, *tabhane*, *hammam*, bridge, *imaret* and storerooms.  
The entrance to the common courtyard, which is surrounded by walls, is through the gates on the north, by the road; to the left of the main gate is the Sinan Ağa Fountain. The mosque is located to the south of the common courtyard; the *darüsşşifa* and the *madrasa* are to the west of the common courtyard, whereas to its east is the *imaret*, constructed as two blocks and consisting of a bakery with two ovens, a candle factory, refectory, a larder, and stables; the section containing the ovens and stoves is quite large. In addition to guests and the personnel of the complex, food was also distributed to the poor in the vicinity. Special meals were prepared during Ramadan, religious feasts, and on Fridays; upon the recommendation by a doctor, special food was also prepared for the sick in a separate kitchen.  
To the southwest of the complex, outside the courtyard walls, lies the bridge over Tunca River, This was in order to make the mosque more accessible to those living nearby and thus enlarge the size of the mosque’s congregation. The *hammam*, built on the same bank of the Tunca River as the rest of the complex near the bridge, does not exist today; according to historical sources, it was a double *hammam* comprising separate sections for women and men.  
  
**Bayezid II Mosque**  
Three entrances lead from the common courtyard to the mosque courtyard: one is on the north, and the other two are on the sides. The courtyard is covered with marble plates and surrounded by domed porticoes on all four sides; at the centre of the rectangular courtyard is a marble fountain. In the seven-bayed portico in the front, the dome covering the central bay in front of the portal, is built higher to emphasise the entrance axis. There are also two outdoor *mihrab*s in the portico.  
At the corners of the *tabhane*s adjoining the east and west of the prayer hall are elegant minarets 38 m. in height with a single *şerefe* and fluted bodies of 3.25 m. in diameter. Both *tabhane*s consist of nine bays, each of which is covered by a dome, with four iwans opening onto a central court and rooms in the corners. There is no direct connection between the *tabhane*s and the mosque: the windows in the walls between the *tabhane*s and the mosque are today blocked up.  
From the courtyard a portal with an elegant and elaborate canopy filled with *muqarnas* opens into the prayer hall, which covers an area of about 500 m2 and is covered with a dome of 20.55 m. in diameter rising upon a polygonal drum. The *mihrab* and the *minbar* are made of marble and the royal loge is noteworthy especially for the forest of reused small columns, on which it rests. The wooden door wings and the cupboard doors and window shutters are elaborately decorated.  
  
**Madrasa**  
According to most researchers who refer to the complex, the *madrasa* was a medical training institution. Some studies indicate that students who completed their education in the *madrasa* went on to study medicine in the adjoining hospital while continuing to reside in the *madrasa*. However, no clarifying evidence regarding this matter is known from historical sources or the known *waqf* charters of the complex.  
The Bayezid II Madrasa is a single-storey rectangular structure with an open courtyard. The entrance at the centre of the east front opens into the courtyard surrounded by domed porticoes on all four sides; there are traces of a fountain that was once located in the centre of this courtyard. The 18 student cells, each covered by a dome and each with a fireplace, were placed at the north, south, and west wings. The *dershane* in the middle of the western side, opposite the entrance, is a rectangular chamber protruding out and covered by a large dome, and on its east wall a stone staircase leads to an interesting balcony, which would probably have been used as a library.  
  
**Daruşşifa**  
To the west of the mosque and southeast of the *madrasa* lies the *darüşşifa* consisting of two courtyards and the main structure, all lined up along the north-south axis. The western side of the first rectangular courtyard is lined with domed cells behind a vaulted portico. On the northern part of the eastern side are domed chambers that had various functions and on the southern side two large double domed chambers flank the *iwan* giving access to the second courtyard.  
The second courtyard, which is entered through an *iwan* in the centre of the southern side of the first courtyard, is smaller and has two domed *iwan*s on the sides, each flanked with two domed cells. The cells in the first courtyard and the eastern cells in the second courtyard are today used as exhibition halls by the Museum of Health. The most attractive structure of the *darüşşifa* is the hexagonal main building: the central hexagonal hall is surrounded by an *iwan* in the centre of each side and a square room with a fireplace on each corner. The *iwan*s and chambers are each covered by an individual dome and the chambers are entered through the *iwan*s. The hexagonal main hall also has a rather large dome rising on a cornice of *muqarnas*. The central lantern of the dome and the windows on the far walls of the *iwan*s illuminate the main hall. A pool with a fountain is located in the centre of the main hall and the *iwan* opposite the entrance *iwan* is deeper than the rest of the structure and protrudes out. Today the structure is an exhibition hall where scenes of Ottoman daily life are excellently presented with mannequins.  
There is some information in historical sources about the function of the various sections of the *darüşşifa*. For example, it is reported that the sections in the first courtyard were used as doctors’ rooms, a pantry, a kitchen, isolation rooms for the mentally ill, a laundry and so on, while medicine was prepared and stored in the rooms that opened onto the two *iwan*s opposite each other in the second courtyard. Again, based on historical records, it is known that on certain occasions musicians performed in the large *iwan* of the hexagonal main structure. According to legend, the sound of sprinkling water had a soothing effect on the mentally ill, and was helpful in their treatment.

es.name: Complejo de Bayezid II
description:
Incluso después de que la capital se trasladara a Estambul, Edirne siguió siendo una ciudad importante por largo tiempo. El complejo de Bayezid II, que data de finales del siglo XV, y la mezquita Selimiye, una obra maestra de la arquitectura otomana terminada en 1575, son los edificios que mejor dan idea de la importancia que tuvo esta ciudad.  
El sultán Bayezid II asistió personalmente a la ceremonia en que se puso la primera piedra de su complejo, el 25 de mayo de 1484. Durante la celebración se sacrificaron animales y su carne se distribuyó a los pobres. La construcción duró poco tiempo, solo cuatro años, y en 1488 se inauguró con una gran ceremonia.  
Hay varias hipótesis acerca de quién fue el arquitecto de este complejo. Para algunos estudiosos, su nombre es Hayreddin; otros creen que es Ya‘qub Şah Ibn Sultan Şah.  
El complejo de Bayezid II de Edirne, construido después que otro complejo del mismo sultán en Amasya, está formado por un gran grupo de edificios distribuidos por un área de 22.000 m2: mezquita, *madrasa*, *darüşşifa*, *tabhane*, *hammam*, puente, *imaret* y almacenes. La entrada al patio común, rodeado de muros, se hace por las puertas del lado norte, junto a la carretera; a la izquierda de la puerta principal está la fuente de Sinan Ağa.  
La mezquita se encuentra en el lado sur del patio; al oeste de ella están el *darüşşifa* y la *madrasa*; al este, el *imaret*, construido en dos bloques y formado por una tahona con dos hornos, una fábrica de velas, un refectorio, una despensa y establos; la zona de las cocinas es muy grande. Además de los huéspedes y los trabajadores del complejo, también se distribuía comida a los pobres de las cercanías. Durante el Ramadán, en las festividades religiosas y los viernes se preparaban platos extraordinarios; para los enfermos, y siguiendo las indicaciones del médico, se hacían comidas especiales en una cocina aparte.  
Al suroeste del complejo, fuera ya de los muros del patio, se encuentra el puente sobre el río Tunca, que facilitaba el acceso a la mezquita a los habitantes de los alrededores, quienes engrosaban así la congregación. En la misma orilla del Tunca que el resto del complejo se construyó un *hammam*, ahora desaparecido; según las fuentes históricas, era doble, con una sección para los hombres y otra para las mujeres.  
A principios de 2001, el *imaret* estaba cerrado y en pésimo estado, y la mezquita, también cerrada, se encontraba en restauración, pero el *darüşşifa* y la *madrasa* están en buenas condiciones y los usa la Universidad de Trakya como Museo de la Medicina y ambulatorio, respectivamente.  
  
**Mezquita**  
Tres entradas llevan desde el patio común hasta el de la mezquita: una en el lado norte y las otras dos en los laterales. El patio, rectangular, está recubierto de planchas de mármol y rodeado totalmente de pórticos con cúpulas; en el centro hay una fuente. En el pórtico frontal de siete crujías, la cúpula del arco central es más alta para subrayar el eje de entrada. En el pórtico hay también dos *mihrab*s.  
En las esquinas de los *tabhane*s adyacentes a la sala de oración por el este y el oeste se encuentran los alminares de 38 m de altura, un solo *şerefe* y cuerpos acanalados de 3,25 m de diámetro. Los *tabhane*s tienen nueve crujías, todas cubiertas por cúpulas, con cuatro *iwan*s que dan a un patio central y habitaciones en los rincones. No hay comunicación directa entre los *tabhane*s y la mezquita, porque las ventanas entre ellos están ahora tapiadas.  
En el patio, un portal de elegante techo lleno de *muqarnas* introduce en la sala de oración, de 500 m2 de superficie y cubierta con una cúpula de 20,55 m de diámetro que se alza sobre un tambor poligonal. El *mihrab* y el *mimbar* son de mármol, y la galería real destaca por el bosque de pequeñas columnas reutilizadas sobre las que descansa. Las hojas de la puerta y los postigos de armarios y ventanas están finamente decorados.  
  
**Madrasa**  
En opinión de la mayoría de los investigadores que se han ocupado del complejo, esta *madrasa* era una escuela de formación médica. Algunos señalan que los estudiantes que completaban su preparación en la *madrasa* seguían viviendo en ella y continuaban estudiando medicina en el hospital contiguo. No obstante, en las fuentes históricas o actas del *waqf* del complejo no hay datos que lo aclaren.  
La *madrasa* de Bayezid II es de planta rectangular, con un solo piso y un patio abierto. La entrada, en medio de la fachada oriental, da al patio con pórticos con cúpulas en sus cuatro lados y en cuyo centro quedan restos de una fuente. En las alas norte, sur y oeste estaban los cuartos de los estudiantes, todos con cúpula y un hogar. El *dershane*, situado en medio del lado occidental, frente a la entrada, es una estancia rectangular, saliente y cubierta por una gran cúpula. De su pared oriental sale una escalera de piedra, que lleva a una galería que quizá sirviera de biblioteca.  
  
**Darüşşifa**  
Al oeste de la mezquita y al sureste de la *madrasa* se encuentra el *darüşşifa*, formado por dos patios y una estructura principal, todos alineados en un eje de norte a sur. En el lado occidental del primer patio, de forma rectangular, hay celdas con cúpula detrás de un pórtico abovedado. En la parte norte del lado oriental hay habitaciones con cúpula destinadas a varias funciones. Finalmente, en el lado sur, dos grandes estancias con doble cúpula flanquean el *iwan* que comunica con el segundo patio. Este segundo patio es más pequeño y tiene dos *iwan*s a los lados, cada uno flanqueado por dos celdas con cúpula. Las celdas del primer patio y las del lado oriental del segundo sirven hoy de salas de exposición del Museo de la Salud. Lo más interesante del *darüşşifa* es el edificio principal: la sala central hexagonal está flanqueada por un *iwan* en el centro de cada lado y una habitación cuadrada con hogar en cada ángulo. Los *iwan*s y las habitaciones están cubiertos por una cúpula individual, y se accede a las habitaciones a través de los *iwan*s. Cubre la sala hexagonal una cúpula bastante grande que se alza sobre una cornisa de *muqarna*s. La linterna de la cúpula y las ventanas situadas en las paredes de los *iwan*s iluminan la sala principal, en cuyo centro hay una pila con fuente. El *iwan* del lado opuesto a la entrada es más profundo y sobresale en el exterior. Hoy, este edificio es una sala de exposiciones donde están excelentemente representadas con maniquíes escenas de la vida diaria del tiempo de los otomanos.  
En fuentes históricas encontramos alguna información sobre las funciones de varias secciones del *darüşşifa*. Por ejemplo, se dice que las estancias del primer patio eran habitaciones de los médicos, despensa, cocina, celdas de aislamiento para los enfermos mentales, lavandería, etcétera, mientras que los medicamentos se preparaban y guardaban en las habitaciones que daban a los dos *iwan*s, uno frente al otro, del segundo patio. Por los registros históricos se sabe también que en el gran *iwan* del edificio hexagonal a veces se daban conciertos. Cuenta la leyenda que el murmullo de la fuente tenía efectos tranquilizadores sobre los pacientes con alguna perturbación mental y servía de ayuda en su tratamiento.

cs.name: Salla Terrena
description: Sál u průjezdu do zahrady je zaklenut neckovou klenbou s výsečemi. Její plochu zdobí podobně jako v patrech zámku štuková výzdoba se zrcadly vyplněnými malovanými výjevy z Ovidiových Proměn, postavami bohyň a Múz s kryptoportréty stavebníků. Konaly se zde hudební produkce, které se staly i vzorem pro zřízení slavného divadla v Jaroměřicích.
artist: Badassare Fontana? (1661 Chiasso – 1733 Chiasso), H. Cavalli

en.name: *Sala terrena*
description: The hall by the passageway to the garden features a segmented vault. It is decorated, like the chateau floors, with stuccowork containing “mirrors” filled with painted scenes from Ovid's *Metamorphoses*, figures of gods and muses.

cs.name: Morový sloup
description: Sloup s Pannou Marií – přemožitelkou zla ve vrcholu – byl postaven jako dík, že ve městě skončila morová epidemie. Patří mezi první, později rozšířené sloupy na Moravě.

en.name: Plague Column
description: The column, crowned by the Virgin Mary vanquisher of evil, was erected in gratitude to the end of the plague epidemic. It was among the first columns of its kind in Moravia.

en.name: *Saint Michael Archangel with Four Saints*
names: *Saint Michael Archangel with the Saints John the Baptist, Benedict, Francis and Jerome*
description: This painting once on the high altar of the church of San Michele, St. Michael is described by the Bolognese art historian Malvasia as “of peculiar invention and of such a pictorial good taste”. The five saints, rarely associated, are crowded in the narrow space without being in emotional contact with each other: Benedict, Francis and Jerome are absorbed in their meditations, only the Baptist seems to notice the presence of the archangel. He points to the scale that will be used on the day of the Last Judgement to weigh merits and sins. The painting can be dated around the half of the second decade of the seventeenth-century based on the pictorial language maturity clearly visible in the monumental scale of the figures and the skilled brilliant use of colour.
The five saints, rarely associated, are crowded in the narrow space without seeming to be in emotional contact with each other.
holder: Museo Diocesano di Arte Sacra di San Giovanni in Persiceto
keywords: St. Michael; St. John the Baptist; St. Benedict; St. Francis; St. Jerome; Altarpiece; Religious/liturgical painting; Alessandro Tiarini; Counter reformation; Christian themes

it.name: San Michele arcangelo fra quattro santi
names: San Michele arcangelo fra i santi Giovanni il Battista, Benedetto, Francesco e Girolamo
description: Quest'opera, ricordata sull'altare maggiore della chiesa di San Michele, veniva definita già dalle fonti dell'epoca *bizzarra d' invenzione e di tanto buon gusto pittorico* (Malvasia). Nell'insolita iconografia i cinque santi si stipano entro lo spazio a disposizione senza entrare in reale contatto emotivo l'uno con l'altro: mentre Benedetto, Francesco e Girolamo sono intenti nelle proprie meditazioni, solo il Battista sembra accorgersi della presenza dell'arcangelo Michele, di cui indica al riguardante la bilancia con la quale, il giorno del Giudizio Universale, saranno valutati i meriti e le colpe di ciascuno. Il dipinto è collocabile intorno alla metà del secondo decennio in base all'analisi stilistica che mostra una raggiunta maturità del linguaggio pittorico, che si esprime attraverso la monumentalità delle figure e la sapiente, quasi smaltata, stesura del colore.
I cinque santi, raramente accostati sono ammassati nello spazio ristretto senza un reale contatto emotivo tra loro.
holder: Museo diocesano di Arte Sacra di San Giovanni in Persiceto
keywords: S. Michele; S. Giovanni Battista; S. Benedetto; S. Francesco; S. Gerolamo; Pala d'altare; pittura religiosa; Alessandro Tiarini; Controriforma; tematiche cristiane

ar.name: صحن.
description:
صحن خزفي مخلوط بمركَّب من الزجاج وأكسيد القصدير، ومطلي بطبقة ذات بريق معدني، ويعتبر نموذجاً لهذا النمط من الأواني الخزفية التي زُخرفت بطريقة نقش معالم الرسم الأساسي على سطح الصحن غير المعرَّض للنار. يبرز النطاق المنقوش (وهي تقنية مأخوذة عن صناعة الأشغال المعدنية) بالأزرق الفريد البراق للأيِّل وقرونه والوردة ثمانية البتلات وبعض أوراق النبتة. أما الزخرفة ذات البريق المعدني واللون الذهبي الأسمر فقد أضيفت في فترة لاحقة إلى الخلفية بعد تعريضها للنار.  
كانت مانيس إحدى البلدات الرئيسية لصناعة الخزف في فلينسيا؛ وقد لعبت دوراً ريادياً في إنتاج الأواني ذات البريق المعدني لتصديرها إلى أوروبا، وخصوصاً إلى فرنسا وإيطاليا. وكانت أواني الخزف المانيسية تخزَّن من أجل تصديرها عن طريق ميناء غروا في فلينسيا، حيث العديد من الخزافين المانيسيين لديهم ورشات ومستودعات للخزف. وقد كان الخزافون خليطاً من المسيحيين والمغاربة (المسلمين)، ولم يكن يُسمح لهؤلاء الأخيرين بمزاولة حرفتهم خارج البلدة، مما يدل على الدور الهام لمهاراتهم الخاصة في اقتصاد مانيس. ومع حلول منتصف القرن السادس عشر (956 هـ) أصبحت مانيس المحتكر الرئيسي لإنتاج الأواني ذات البريق المعدني في فلينسيا.

هذا الصحن المطلي بالبريق المعدني، والمصقول بالقصدير، صُنع في بلدة مانيسس في فالنسيا. كانت البلدة تحتكر صناعة هذا النمط من الخزفيات، التي كان ينفِّذها خزَّافون مسلمون، من بقايا السكان المغاربة السابقين. ومثل هذه الصحون كانت مطلوبة، ورائجة جداً، في كلٍّ من فرنسا وإيطاليا.
dates: أواخر القرن التاسع- العاشر / أواخر الخامس عشر- السادس عشر.
keywords: تجارة؛ زخرفة تصويرية.
materials: خزف منقوش بزخارف نافرة، مع خليط من مركَّب الزجاج وأكسيد القصدير، ومطلي بطبقة ذات بريق معدني.
tags: خزف منقوش بزخارف نافرة، مع خليط من مركَّب الزجاج وأكسيد القصدير، ومطلي بطبقة ذات بريق معدني.

en.name: Dish.
description:
A lustre-painted and tin-glazed dish that is representative of this type of earthenware which was decorated by incising the outlines of the main design onto the surface of the unfired dish. The incised areas (a technique borrowed from the metalworking industry) stand out in the unusual luminescent blue of the stag, its antlers, the eight-petal flower, and the accents on some of the foliage. The brownish-gold lustre decoration of the background was added at a later stage after further firings.  
  
Manises was one of the main pottery-making towns in Valencia. It played a leading role in the manufacture of lustre-wares for export to Europe, principally to France and Italy. Manises' pottery left for export from the Valencian port of Groa where many Manises potters owned pottery warehouses and shops. These potters were a mixture of Christians and Moors (Muslims), the latter of which were not permitted to take their skills to work outside the town, testifying to the value of their special skills to the economy of Manises. By the mid-16th century (AH 956), Manises had a major monopoly on the production of lustre-wares in Valencia.

This lustre-painted and tin-glazed dish was made in the town of Manises in Valencia. It monopolised the manufacture of this type of ceramics, which were made by Muslim potters who were remnants of its old Moorish population. Such dishes were very much sought after in both France and Italy.
dates: Hegira late 9th–early 10th century / AD late 15th–early 16th century.
keywords: Commerce; figurative decoration; animal decoration
materials: Earthenware with incised relief decoration, lustre-painted and tin-glazed.
tags: Earthenware with incised relief decoration, lustre-painted and tin-glazed.

es.name: Plato.
description:
Plato de reflejo metálico y vidriado estannífero representativo de este tipo de cerámica que se decoraba grabando el contorno del motivo principal sobre la superficie sin cocer. Las líneas incisas (técnica tomada de la metalistería) destacan, en un inhabitual azul luminoso, la figura del ciervo y su cornamenta, la flor de ocho pétalos y parte del follaje. El reflejo dorado del fondo se añadió después mediante varias cocciones.  
Manises fue una de las principales localidades productoras de alfarería en Valencia, y desempeñó un papel relevante en la fabricación de objetos de cerámica de reflejo metálico que se exportaban a Europa, principalmente a Francia e Italia, desde el puerto valenciano de Groa, donde muchos alfareros tenían almacenes y tiendas. Entre estos alfareros había cristianos y “moros” (musulmanes); estos últimos no estaban autorizados a ejercer su oficio fuera de la ciudad, lo que es indicativo del valor de sus actividades profesionales para la economía de Manises. A mediados del siglo XVI, Manises tenía un franco monopolio de la producción de cerámica de reflejo metálico en Valencia.

Plato de reflejo metálico y vidriado estannífero procedente de Manises, localidad que monopolizó la manufactura de este tipo de cerámica fabricada por los artesanos que quedaban de la antigua población musulmana. Estos platos eran muy solicitados en Francia e Italia.
dates: Finales del siglo IX–principios del X de la Hégira / XV-XVI d. C.
keywords: comercio; decoración figurativa.
materials: Cerámica; decoración incisa, reflejo metálico y vidriado estannífero.
tags: decoración incisa, reflejo metálico y vidriado estannífero.

fr.name: Plat.
description:
Plat à décor lustré sous glaçure à l'étain (émail stannifère) représentatif d'un type de poterie décorée par l'incision avant cuisson des contours du motif principal de la surface du plat. Les zones incisées (technique empruntée au travail du métal) ressortent dans la curieuse couleur bleue luminescente du cerf, de ses bois, de la fleur à huit pétales et des rehauts de quelques feuilles. Le décor au lustre couleur or brunâtre du fond a été ajouté à une étape ultérieure, après plusieurs cuissons.  
Manisès, l'un des principaux centres de poterie de la région de Valence, joua un rôle majeur dans la fabrication de pièces lustrées destinées à l'exportation vers l'Europe, principalement la France et l'Italie, et expédiées du port de Groa où de nombreux potiers manisiens possédaient des entrepôts et des boutiques. Ces artisans étaient aussi bien maures que chrétiens, les premiers n'étant pas autorisés à travailler hors de la ville, ce qui témoignait d'une certaine façon de la reconnaissance de leur talent. Vers le milieu du XVIe siècle (956 H), Manisès jouait un rôle prépondérant dans la production de poterie lustrée de la région de Valence.

Ce plat peint au lustre sous émail stannifère a été fabriqué dans la ville de Manisès près de Valence. Cette ville eut le monopole de la production de ce type de céramiques, apanage de potiers musulmans qui étaient les derniers descendants de son ancienne population maure. De tels récipients étaient très recherchés à la fois en France et en Italie.
dates: Fin IXe-début Xe siècle de l’Hégire (fin XVe-début XVIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: commerce ; décoration figurative
materials: Faïence à décor en relief incisé, peint au lustre sous émail stannifère.
tags: Faïence à décor en relief incisé, peint au lustre sous émail stannifère.

en.name: *Austrian troops occupy Venice in 1797*
short_description: Napoleon ended the existence of the 1000-year-old Venetian Republic in May 1797. French troops proceeded to occupy Venice for six months from May 1797 to January 1798, then ceded the city to Austria. Austrian troops occupied Venice starting 18 January 1798 until the Peace of Pressburg in 1805.

en.name: Plate
short_description: Kütahya was the second most important ceramic production centre after İznik due to the rich clay deposits in the area. This plate has flat rim, is slightly deep in body and has a circular bottom. It was made of white clay and coated in white on which there are patterns in cobalt blue, yellow, turquoise, purple and red covered with transparent glaze. In the middle of the plate there is an Ottoman coat-of-arms while both sides of the plate are decorated with curtains. Above the coat-of-arms, “Long Live My Sultan” is written in Turkish in Arabic letters forming a crescent and there is a *tuğra* (monogram) of Abdülhamid II (1876-1909) in the middle of the sun covering both the *tuğra* and the crescent.
holder: Vehbi Koç Foundation Sadberk Hanim Museum
keywords: Kütahya ceramics; plate; tughra
partner: Vehbi Koç Foundation Sadberk Hanim Museum

en.name: *Ambassador Mohammed ibn 'Abd al-Malik, Pasha of Tangier, visits Vienna on February 14, 1783*
short_description: This picture shows Moroccan Ambassador Mohammed ibn 'Abd al-Malik, Pasha of Tangier, at his first visit to Vienna on 14 Feb 1783. This visit of the Moroccan delegation in Vienna started the more than 200-years-long peaceful relationship between Morocco and Austria.
keywords: Morocco; Vienna

en.name: High Altar of St. Blaise
description: A combination of white and polychrome marble make up the altar, conceived as custodial with the statue of the saint. The domed antependium has two angels unveiling a curtain in front of a medallion, while a high niche contains a silver statue of St. Blaise –richly decorated with volutes, acanthus leaves,  figures and heads of angels – rising from the mensa. Two kneeling angels with outspread wings in an emotion-laden attitude of prayer and adoration, flank the central composition. This altar, typical of the Baroque aspiration towards dynamism and opulent colour, is typologically consistent with the group of altars created under the influence of Baltazar Longhena, and his altar in the Church of S. Lorenzo Giustiniani in Venice.

ar.name: رداء لرجل أو لطفل
description:
إن الجزء العلوي الخارجي من الثوب (القبا) مصنوع من الحرير الأرجواني متغير اللون، في حين أن الكفَات مبطنة من الداخل بنسيج من الصوف الفارسي ذو النمط المخطط.  
نظرًا لأن الكفًات عادةً ما يتم قلبها من الداخل إلى الخارج، فإن هذا يخلق تباينًا لطيفًا في الألوان. تم استخدام القماش الأوروبي المطبوع لصنع البطانة، كما كان الحال غالبًا خلال أواخر القرن التاسع عشر .  
  
القبا هو لباس خارجي تقليدي لم يتغير شكله إلا قليلًا على مر القرون. جزءه العلوي ضيق ، بينما الجزء السفلي فيه واسع وفي بعض الأحيان به شقوق جانبية.  
  
حصل التاجر السويسري إميل ألبيجر على هذا الرداء في إيران بين عامي 1870 و1896. وكان ألبيجر آنذاك مديرًا لشركة زيغلر وشركاه التجارية ومقرها مانشستر والتي كانت تمتلك مصنعًا للسجاد في سلطان آباد.
materials: حرير متغير اللون، تطريز، بطانة: قماش صوف (*ترمه*)، قطن مطبوع (صناعة أوروبية)
tags: حرير متغير اللون، تطريز، بطانة: قماش صوف (ترمه)، قطن مطبوع (صناعة أوروبية)

en.name: Robe for a man or a child
description:
The outside of the upper garment (*gaba*) is made of a purple silk changeant, whilst its cuffs are lined on the inside with a Persian wool fabric with a characteristic striped pattern. Since the cuffs are usually turned inside out, this creates a pleasant colour contrast. European printed fabric was used to make the lining, as was often the case during the latter 19th century.  
  
The *gaba* is a traditional outer garment whose shape has changed little over the centuries. The upper part is close-fitting, while the lower part is flared and sometimes has side slits.  
  
This robe was acquired by the Swiss merchant Emil Alpiger in Iran between 1870 and 1896. Alpiger was then director of the Manchester-based trading company Ziegler & Co. which owned a carpet factory in Sultanabad.
materials: Silk changeant, embroidery, lining: wool fabric (*termeh*), printed cotton (European manufacture)

ar.name: سبع لوحات من العصور القديمة ومناظر في اليونان ومصر من مخططات معمولة لهذه المنطقة تاريخها 1749 من قبل ريتشارد دالتون.
description: بين عامي 1746 و 1754 قام لورد شارلمون ، جيمس كاولفيلد وهو حامل أول لقب إيرل لشارلمون بجولة كبيرة في أوربا. وبينما كان في صقلية في عام 1749 فقد صادف ريتشارد دالتون وهو رسام وحفار الذي طلب منه أن يصحبه ورفاقه الرحالة تجاه اليونان ومصر من أجل تامين صور لمقالاته. وقد سافر دالتون مع شارلمون حتى عام 1750 وخلالها عمل العديد من الرسوم للمشاهد الطبيعية و العادات والأحداث وكان معروفا كأول إنجليزي يعمل رسوم في هذه المناطق. وبعض هذه الرسوم نشرت في كتاب (الآثار القديمة ومشاهد في اليونان ومصر) الذي نشر تحديدا عام 1791 وتضمن رسوما محفورة لمواقع مهمة خارج إيطاليا. ويبدو من الواضح أن دالتون أيضا قد كان لديه اهتمام كبير في شعائر الحج السنوية ورسم ثمانية أجزاء مختلفة من الشعائر( يقال بأنه عمل ذلك بينما كان متخفيا في بيت قريب) وكل جزء ذو وصف شامل وقد صار دالتون قيم مكتبة الملك جورج الثالث.

en.name: Seven plates from *Antiquities and views in Greece and Egypt, with the manners and customs of the inhabitants, from drawings made on the spot*, A.D. 1749 by Richard Dalton
description: Between 1746 and 1754, Lord Charlemont, James Caulfield, 1st Earl of Charlemont embarked on a Grand Tour of Europe. Whilst in Sicily in 1749, Charlemont encountered Richard Dalton, a draftsman and engraver, whom he asked to accompany him and his travelling companions onwards to Greece and Egypt in order to provide illustrations for his essays. Dalton travelled with Charlemont until 1750 during which time he made many drawings of landscapes, customs and events and was known as the first Englishman to make drawings in these regions. Some of these drawings were published in ‘*Antiquities and views in Greece and Egypt*’, which was published definitively in 1791 and included engraved sketches of important sites beyond Italy. Notably Dalton also seems to have taken great interest in the annual Hajj procession, and sketched eight different parts of the ceremonies (it is said while concealed in a nearby house), each labelled with an extensive caption. Dalton went on to become librarian to King George III.

description: إن الصور التوضيحية الثلاثة عشر في هذه النسخة الرائعة من الخمسة (الأشعار الخمسة) لأمير خسرو دهلوي غالبا تنسب لأعظم الفنانين الفارسيين ، بهزاد. ولكن بالرغم من كونها ملتزمة  جدا بالطراز البهزادي فإنها جميعا غير موقعة. والمخطوطة أيضا مذهبة بشكل واسع ومجلدة بتجليد ساحر مطلي بالذهب ومقولبة بالضغط وذات تجليد مخرم. وقد نسخ النص من قبل محمد ، ابن أزهر وهو أحد الخطاطين العظام في البلاط التيموري.

en.name: *Khamsa* of Amir Khusraw
description: The thirteen illustrations in this fine copy of the *Khamsa* (‘Five Poems’) of Amir Khusraw Dihlavi are often attributed to the greatest of Persian artists, Bihzad. However, although they are very ‘Bihzadian’ in style, none are signed. The manuscript is also extensively illuminated and is bound in an exquisite gilt, pressure-moulded and filigree binding. The text was copied by Muhammad, son of Azhar, one of the greatest calligraphers of the Timurid court.
keywords: illustration; miniature painting; calligraphy; script; Majnun; court; women; sufism

en.name: Historic Centre
description:
"The oldest part of the settlement of Guarda was on a small platform that was marked by an almost circular enclosure at the end of the Middle Ages. The streets were not organised rationally, but took into account the nature of the terrain and the gates, of which there were probably five, that communicated with the outside, in the Mediaeval period. The streets are narrow and winding with some Manueline and some even earlier houses, such as those in Rua Direita and Rua dos Clérigos.  
The Castle was situated on a dominating point inside the *enceinte*, but the clearest line of circulation was Rua Direita, which joined the Porta da Covilhã and the Porta dos Curros, the most distant gateways.  
The Cathedral, also serving as the Parish Church, was another important focal point, being situated in the same square as the *Câmara* (Town Hall), a Manueline edifice. Two more parochial churches were linked to this parish and were a natural pole of attraction for the community. There was also an important Jewish community that lived here until the Manueline period. As decreed by D. Pedro I, the Jewish residential quarter had gates, which remained in place even after their official conversion in 1498.  
Outside the gates, houses stretched beyond the walls and the most highly developed district in the Manueline era was the suburb around the Porta dos Ferreiros, in the Parishes of São Pedro and São Nicolau and close to the Franciscan Monastery.  
It was here, too, that the annual fair was held. Lasting for two weeks, this extremely important event had been created by royal dispensation in 1255."

ar.name: إبريق.
description:
إبريق على شكل إجاصة، مزوَّد بقبضة ومصب مزخرفين بأشكال نباتية وأفاريز منقوشة. الجزء الواقع تحت العنق يشغله إفريز مكتوب بالخط النسخي؛ وتحته مباشرة ثمة إفريز آخر مكوَّن من أشكال نباتية. وهناك نقوش إضافية بالخط النسخي موجودة على عنق الإبريق ومصبِّه. تصاميم الزهر والنقوش التي تزيِّن الإبريق مزخرفة برقائق الفضة. الكتابة المنقوشة على الإطار العلوي والمصب، والمزدانة برقائق النحاس الأحمر، تدعو لصاحب الإناء بالمجد والجاه والنجاح والعمر المديد.  
  
يحظى هذا الإبريق بأهمية كبيرة نظراً لكونه نموذجاً تأريخياً للأشغال الفنية لبلاد الرافدين فضلاً عن أن نقوشه تذكر اسمي حرفيين موصلليين.

كانت الموصل مركزاً مهماً لصنع الأدوات المعدنية، في أثناء الفترة الزنكية. وكان لهذا المركز تأثير عظيم في تقنيات وأساليب الصناعات المعدنية الأرتوقية في الأناضول. يُفيد النقش بأن الإبريق صنعه مُعلِّم يدعى "إياس الموصلّي". وهو يحمل ميزات عصره.

en.name: Ewer (*ibrik*).
description: A ewer (*ibrik*) with a pear-shaped body, a handle and a spout decorated with plant motifs and inscription friezes. The shoulder of the ewer is filled with a frieze written in *naskhi* script. A second frieze, formed of plant motifs, appears directly below. Further inscriptions in *naskhi* script are found on the neck and spout. The floral motifs and inscriptions adorning the ewer are embellished with silver leaf, while the frame of the inscription on the shoulder is embellished with red-copper leaf. The inscriptions on the shoulder and spout wish glory, fame, success and long life to the owner of the vessel. This ewer is of great importance both as a dated example of Mesopotamian work and because its inscriptions provide the names of two Mosul craftsmen.

Mosul was an important centre of Islamic metalwork during the Zangid period. This centre had a great influence on the technique and style of Artuqid metalwork in Anatolia. The inscription states that it was made by a master called 'Iyas of Mosul. It has the characteristics of its period.
holder: Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts.
keywords: Brass; calligraphy; ewer (ibrik); floral decoration; inscription; naskhi; Zangids; vegetal decoration
materials: Cast and engraved brass inlaid with red-copper and silver.

es.name: Aguamanil.
description: Aguamanil *(ibrik)* en forma de pera con asa y pitorro, decorado con motivos vegetales y bandas de inscripciones. La parte superior del cuerpo presenta una banda con caracteres *nasji*. Justo debajo de ésta hay una segunda con motivos vegetales. El cuello y el pitorro están también adornados con escritura *nasji*. Los motivos florales e inscripciones que adornan el aguamanil están a su vez embellecidos con una lámina de plata; sin embargo, el marco que rodea la inscripción de la parte superior del cuerpo está ornado con una lámina de cobre rojo. Las inscripciones del cuerpo y el pitorro desean gloria, fama, éxito y una larga vida al dueño del recipiente. Este aguamanil reviste gran importancia porque es un ejemplo datado de obra mesopotámica y porque en sus inscripciones figuran los nombres de dos artesanos de Mosul.

Mosul fue un importante centro de metalistería islámica durante el periodo zangí y tuvo una gran influencia en la técnica y el estilo de esta artesanía entre los artuqíes en Anatolia. La inscripción señala que el aguamanil fue hecho por el maestro Iyas de Mosul. Presenta las características propias del periodo.
holder: Museo de Arte Turco e Islámico.
keywords: bronce; caligrafía; aguamanil (ibrik); decoración floral; inscripción; nasji; zangíes; decoración vegetal

fr.name: Aiguière (*ibrik*).
description: Aiguière à corps piriforme, dotée d'une poignée et d'un bec. Le décor consiste en motifs végétaux et frises épigraphiées. L'épaule est recouverte d'une première frise en écriture *naskhi*, au-dessus d'une seconde formée de motifs de plantes. D'autres inscriptions *naskhi* figurent sur le col et sur le bec. Les motifs floraux et les inscriptions sont rehaussés à la feuille d'or tandis que le cartouche de l'inscription de l'épaule est incrusté à la feuille de cuivre rouge. Les inscriptions souhaitent gloire, réputation, réussite et longue vie au propriétaire de l'objet. Cette aiguière est d'une grande importance parce qu'elle est un exemple daté de travail mésopotamien et que ses inscriptions fournissent l'identité de deux artisans de Mossoul.

Mossoul était un important centre de l’art du métal durant la période zenguide. Ce centre eut une grande influence sur la technique et le style du travail du métal artukide en Anatolie. Les inscriptions établissent que cette aiguière a été réalisée par un maître appelé “Iyas de Mossoul”. Ses caractéristiques sont celles de l’époque.
holder: Musée des arts turcs et islamiques.
keywords: décoration florale ; laiton, calligraphie ; aiguière ; inscription ; naskhi ; zenguides ; décor végétal
materials: Fonte de cuivre gravée et incrustée de cuivre et d’argent.

tr.name: İbrik.
description: İbrik armut biçimli gövdeli, kulplu ve emziklidir. İbriğin süslemesi, bitki motifleri ve kitabe frizlerinden oluşmaktadır. İbriğin omuz kısmını nesihle yazılmış bir kitabe frizi dolanmaktadır. Bu kitabenin hemen altında bitki motiflerinden oluşan ikinci bir friz yer almaktadır. Eserin boynunda ve emzik kısmında da yine nesihle yazılmış kitabeler bulunmaktadır. İbriği süsleyen kitabeler ve bitki motifleri gümüş varaklarla omuzdaki kitabenin çerçevesi ise kırmızı-bakır varaklarla bezelidir. İbriğin omzunda ve emziğinin üzerinde yer alan kitabeler, eserin sahibine şan, şöhret, başarı ve ebedi hayat dileyen, bereket kitabeleridir. Bu nedenle ibrik, gerek Mezopotamya' ya ait tarihli bir örnek olması, gerek boyun kitabesinde iki Musullu ustanın adının birlikte anılmış olması bakımından büyük önem taşımaktadır.

Zengiler döneminde Musul ve civarı, İslam maden sanatının önemli merkezlerindendi. Bu merkezin, teknik ve üslup bakımından Anadolu'da Artuklu maden sanatına büyük etkisi olmuştur. Kitabesine göre Musullu usta İyas tarafından yapılan bu ibrik, döneminin karakteristik özelliklerini taşımaktadır.
keywords: Bitkisel bezeme; pirinç; hat; ibrik

de.name: Fassade
description: Die Doppelturmfassade von St. Jakob ist eine hochbarocke Umbildung des durch den Salzburger Doms geprägten Schemas. Charakteristisch sind hierfür die vortretenden Türme, mit denen der zweigeschossige Mittelteil im Verbund steht. Gegenüber Salzburg sind die Übergänge durch konkave Wandstücke jedoch fließender gestaltet und die hochovalen Fenster des oberen Geschosses setzen eigene, die Fassadenmitte und die Türme verbindende motivische Akzente. description: The double-tower façade of St. Jacob is a Late Baroque interpretation of a basic plan based on the Salzburg Dome. The projecting towers – which form a unit with the two-storey middle section – are characteristic. In contrast to Salzburg the transitions are more fluent, employing concave wall sections. The vertical oval windows of the upper storeys establish a number of thematic accents. The towers’ upper storeys are also more powerfully built than in Salzburg.
artist: Johann Jakob Herkomer (1648–1717); Johann Georg Fischer (1673–1747)

en.name: Coat of Arms of the Erdödy Counts
description:
The coat of arms has an elongated triangular composition. In the middle is a a horse-head-shaped shield quartered with a heart in the centre: (1) on gold, a black, displayed, crowned eagle; (2) and (3) a blue bar with two six-pointed gold stars one beside the other; (4) on gold, a crenellated castle with a window and a door, in the heart of the shield: on red a stag rearing to the right from a halved gold wheel. Crest: above the shield, a gold crown from which grows gold acanthus leaves and an angel. Bearers of the arms: on each side is an angel with gold wings and one foot stepping sideways. The “background” is richly decorated with acanthus leaves, which in this case take over the function of the mantle.  
The Croatian aristocratic family of Hungarian origin, known as the Bakochs, came from the village of Erdöd. From the 16th to the 19th centuries, the Erdödy family played a leading role in Croatian history, acquiring many estates, bestowing five Croatian *bans* (viceroys) and one bishop, and playing an influential part in Croatian political life. They were particularly famous for fighting against the Ottomans.  
Among their many estates, Klanjec castle – built in 1603 and locally known as Novi Dvori Klanječki – is worthy of special mention.  
The Erdödy coat of arms was produced in the sculpture workshop of the Ljubljana, later the Zagreb master sculptor and woodcarver, Ivan Komersteiner, whose arrival in Croatia marked the final advent of Baroque art.  
In the south apse of Zagreb cathedral there is a similar memorial arms by Ivan Komersteiner produced in 1693 for *Ban* Nikola Erdödy who liberated much of Croatia from the Turks.  
Nikola Erdödy built a chapel in the west wing of Klanjec castle dedicated to St Francis Xavier, which he decorated with wall paintings. It is possible that the family arms shown here is from the castle, or perhaps even that it was on an altar commissioned by the Erdödys, who were known to be great donors.  
The Erdödy arms, probably the work of an unknown sculptor from Ivan Komersteiner's workshops, has retained the basic characteristics of Ivan's style, seen particularly in the use of luscious and fleshy acanthus leaves and angel figures as ornamentation.

Coat of arms of the Erdödy Counts, it comprises a shaped triangular composition around a crowned, quartered shield in gold-blue, with a red heart at the centre, and the family’s symbols. Two guardian angels support it, while there is a third, smaller, angel above the crown. Behind the shield and above the crown are gold acanthus leaves.  
The Erdödys were Croatian aristocrats of Hungarian origin, a family of high nobility that were influential in Croatian political life. The coat of arms is probably the work of the unknown sculptor from the Ivan Komersteiner's workshop. Komersteiner was one of the most important sculptors of continental Croatia at the end of the 17th century.

en.name: Sant’Andrea della Valle, Glory of the Virgin fresco
description:
The fresco, which is spread over a surface of 622 m2, represents the Assumption of the Virgin in the glory of Paradise. At the centre, in the lower register above the altar, the Virgin is ascending. Thanks to her red robe and blue mantle she strikes out from the swirling mass of clouds where saints, prophets, apostles, patriarchs and biblical heroines come together. Two putti are about to crown her with a wreath of roses. Proceeding upwards in the second circle, a celestial concert of angel musicians is depicted, while at the base of the lantern seven little angels support garlands and festoons of flowers and fruit.  
Christ, in a white robe, descends from the top of the lantern to welcome his mother to Heaven.  
A precise and orderly hierarchy is therefore established from top to bottom in which the light that radiates from the figure of Christ plays a structural, as well as symbolic role: golden and dazzling at the top, it dematerializes the angelic figures closest to the lantern, while it becomes more ‘concrete’ towards the bottom, especially in the clouds at the base, producing light-toned colours on the garments of the characters based on very refined accords of pink, yellow, gray, orange, green and purple.  
Among the saints in the lower circle, St. Andrew, with the cross of his martyrdom, can be seen holding the hand of the Theatine Andrea Avellino (canonized just a year before the beginning of the works) as he welcomes him to Paradise, while St. Peter is doing the same with Saint Cajetan.  
The inspiring models for Lanfranco are the domes that Correggio had frescoed in Parma Cathedral and in the San Giovanni Evangelista Church, in the same city. However, Lanfranco also refers to Rubens (who was in Rome at the beginning of the century), especially in the drapery, to Bernini in the gestures in movement of the figures, to the ancient models in the positions of some figures.  
The dome sparked great amazement in Rome, constituting the beginning of a new, fertile season in the decoration of vaults and domes: Baroque illusionism.

The dome, with its vortex of figures (strongly influenced by the art of Corregio in Parma) can be considered the birth of the tendency for the search of illusionist effects of the art of Seicento’s Rome.
history:
The construction of the church of the Clerics Regular (also known as Theatines), an order founded in 1524 by Gian Pietro Carafa (the future Pope Paul IV), began in 1591 on commission of Cardinal Alfonso Gesualdo, protector of the Congregation. After his death, he was succeeded by Sixtus V’s nephew, Cardinal Alessandro Peretti Montalto who, starting from 1608, entrusted the completion of the building to Carlo Maderno, while the initial project had been designed by the Theatine Francesco Grimaldi and Giacomo Della Porta.  
This majestic dome, second in size in Rome only to that of St. Peter’s in the Vatican, was completed in 1623.  
Cardinal Ludovisi, nephew of the newly elected Gregory XV, had pushed for the tribune and dome to be painted by his favourite artist, Domenichino, but Cardinal Montalto opted for a compromise by entrusting the dome to Giovanni Lanfranco (who had already proved his value in the magnificent illusionistic fresco of the Council of the gods in the Casino Borghese) while the pendentives and the vault of the apse were still commissioned to Domenichino. The two artists were both Emilian and pupils of Annibale Carracci. To the dizzying whirlwind of Lanfranco’s figures, Domenichino responded with his classic compositions marked by monumentality and calmness.

it.name: Sant’Andrea della Valle, *Assunzione della Vergine* nella cupola
description:
L'affresco, che si dispiega su 622 metri quadrati di superficie, rappresenta l'*Assunzione della Vergine* nella gloria del Paradiso. Essa sorge in posizione centrale, nel registro inferiore, in asse con l'altare, staccandosi visivamente dalla massa vorticosa di nuvole frammiste a figure di santi, profeti, apostoli, patriarchi ed eroine bibliche grazie alla sua veste rossa e al manto blu dai timbri accesi. Due putti si accingono ad incoronarla con un serto di rose.   
Procedendo verso l'alto, nel secondo girone è raffigurato un concerto celeste di angeli musicanti mentre alla base del lanternino sette angioletti sostengono ghirlande e festoni di fiori e frutta.  
Cristo, in veste bianca, si precipita dall'alto del lanternino per accogliere la propria madre in Paradiso.  
Si stabilisce pertanto una precisa ed ordinata gerarchia dall'alto verso il basso in cui la luce che si irradia dalla figura del Cristo gioca un ruolo strutturale, oltreché simbolico: dorata e abbagliante in alto, essa smaterializza le figure angeliche più prossime al lanternino, mentre si fa più sostanziale verso il basso, specie nelle nuvole alla base, seppur producendo sulle vesti dei personaggi colori dai toni chiari basati su accordi raffinatissimi di rosa, gialli, grigi, arancioni, verdi, viola.  
Tra i santi del girone più basso si distinguono sant'Andrea, con la croce del suo martirio, che introduce in Paradiso, tenendolo per mano, il teatino Andrea Avellino (canonizzato appena un anno prima dell'inizio dei lavori) e san Gaetano da Thiene presentato da san Pietro.  
Il modello ispiratore per Lanfranco è il Correggio delle cupole parmensi del Duomo e di San Giovanni Evangelista ma sono anche molti i riferimenti a Rubens (a Roma agli inizi del secolo), specie nei panneggi, a Bernini nella gestualità in movimento delle figure, all'Antico nelle posizioni assunte da alcuni personaggi.  
La cupola suscitò enorme stupore a Roma costituendo l'inizio di una nuova, fertile stagione nella decorazione di volte e cupole, quella dell'illusionismo barocco.

Con il suo vortice di gironi angelici, fortemente influenzato dalla pittura di Correggio, Giovanni Lanfranco creò la prima cupola barocca di Roma, esempio insuperato di illusionismo in cui la luce proveniente dalla sommità investe le figure smaterializzandole nell’etere paradisiaco.
history:
La costruzione della chiesa dei Chierici Regolari (Teatini), ordine fondato nel 1524 da Gian Pietro Carafa (futuro papa Paolo IV), ebbe inizio nel 1591 su commissione del cardinale Alfonso Gesualdo, protettore della congregazione. Alla sua morte gli subentrò il nipote di Sisto V, cardinale Alessandro Peretti Montalto che, a partire dal 1608, affidò il completamento della fabbrica a Carlo Maderno in luogo degli autori del progetto iniziale, il teatino Francesco Grimaldi e Giacomo Della Porta.  
La grandiosa cupola, seconda a Roma per dimensioni solo a quella di San Pietro in Vaticano, venne portata a compimento nel 1623. Il cardinale Ludovisi, *nepote* del neoletto Gregorio XV, fece pressioni per far sì che tribuna e cupola fossero dipinte dal suo artista prediletto, Domenichino, ma il cardinal Montalto optò per un compromesso affidando la cupola a Giovanni Lanfranco (che aveva già dato prova del suo valore nel magnifico affresco illusionistico del *Concilio degli dei* nel Casino Borghese) mentre i pennacchi e la volta dell'abside a Domenichino. I due artisti erano entrambi emiliani ed allievi di Annibale Carracci. Al vertiginoso vortice di figure di Lanfranco, Domenichino avrebbe opposto le sue composizioni improntate da una classica monumentalità e pacatezza.
keywords: Illusionismo; *trompe-l’oeil*

ar.name: برك سليمان.
description:
تتكون برك سليمان من ثلاث برك متجاورة، رُتبّت بحيث تصب البركة الأولى في الثانية، والثانية في الثالثة التي تتفرع منها قناتان. ويبلغ طول البركة الأولى 116م، ويبلغ أقصى عرض لها حوالي 72 م، ويتراوح عمقها ما بين 6 م و12 م، وتبلغ سعتها حوالي 85,000 متر مكعب. ويبلغ طول البركة الوسطى 129 م وعرضها 76 م، ويصل عمقها إلى حوالي 12 م، وتبلغ سعتها حوالي 90,000 متر مكعب. أما البركة الثالثة السفلية (المملوكية) فهي أكبر البرك الثلاث وأكثرها سعة، إذ يبلغ طولها 177 م وأقصى عرض لها 86 م، ويبلغ عمقها حوالي 15 م، وتصل سعتها إلى حوالي 113,000 متر مكعب. وبذلك تتجاوز سعة البرك الثلاث ربع مليون متر مكعب.  
زوّدت هذه البرك مدينة القدس - التي كانت تعاني دوماً من نقص المياه - بالمياه اللازمة للشرب وللاستخدام المنزلي وللوضوء. وكان يتم جمع مياه الأمطار المتساقطة في منطقة البرك، وأيضاً توجيه مياه الينابيع المنتشرة في المنطقة إلى البرك عبر نظام مائي معقد امتد طوله أكثر من 70 كم. وانسابت مياه البرك إلى القدس نظراً لارتفاع منطقة البرك، واستغلال المنحدرات والأودية. وسارت القناة بخط متعرج، فامتدت ضعف المسافة الجغرافية المباشرة بين مدينة القدس والبرك، ووصل طولها إلى 22 كم.  
وقد ألزمت السلطات العثمانية زعماء القرى التي تمر بها القناة بحماية هذا النظام المائي الحيوي من الاعتداءات. وأقام السلطان عثمان الثاني (حكم في الفترة 1027 – 1032 / 1618 – 1622) عام 1027/ 1618 قلعة حصينة على بعد بضعة أمتار إلى الشمال من البركة الأولى.

وتسمى أيضاً "برك سليمان"، نسبة إلى السلطان العثماني الذي قاد مشروعاً ضخماً لترميمها وتطويرها. وهي مُجمَّع مائي ضخم، يقع إلى الجنوب من بيت لحم، يتشكَّل من ثلاث برك ضخمة، لتجميع المياه. ترتبط البرك بنظام معقَّد من القنوات التي تقوم بتزويدها بالمياه المُجمَّعة من الينابيع التي تبعد عشرات الكيلومترات، وكذلك من القنوات التي تقوم بحمل المياه من البرك لتوصلها إلى القدس. بدأ هذا النظام منذ الفترة الرومانية، وجرى ترميمه وتحسينه على مرّ العصور، وأُضيفت إليه البركة الثالثة في العصر المملوكي. واعتبر مدى فاعلية وصلاح نظام تزويد القدس بالمياه مقياساً لنجاعة السلطة الحاكمة.
dates: يعود بناء البركتين الأولى والثانية إلى النصف الثاني من القرن الأول قبل الميلاد، والبركة الثالثة السفلية إلى ما بين العامين 865 - 872 / 1461- 1467.
dynasty: تعود البركتان الأولى والثانية إلى العصر الروماني، والبركة الثالثة إلى العصر المملوكي.
artist: لا يُعرف مَن رعى البناء في الفترات السابقة للإسلام فيما يخص البركتين الأولى والثانية، وأما البركة الثالثة فقام برعايتها السلطان المملوكي خشقدم (حكم في الفترة 865 - 872 / 1461 - 1467).  وقام السلطان المملوكي الأشرف قايتباي (حكم في الفترة 872 - 901 / 1468- 1496) وبعده السلطان العثماني سليمان القانوني (حكم في الفترة 926 - 974 / 1520- 1566) بترميم وتجديد البرك وقناة المياه المعروفة بقناة السبيل.
تشير وثائق المحكمة الشرعية في القدس إلى تعيين مراد النصراني الأرمني في وظيفة
keywords: بركة؛ برك سليمان؛ قناة؛ قناة السبيل؛ مياه.

en.name: Solomon’s Pools.
description:
The Pools of Solomon comprise three neighbouring pools that were arranged in such a manner that the first pool poured into the second, and the second into the third, and from which canals branched out. The first pool is 116 m long and approximately 72 m wide. Its depth ranges from between 6 m and 12 m, and its capacity was 85,000 cu m. The middle pool is 129 m long and 76 m wide. It is 12 m deep and its capacity was approximately 90,000 cu m. The lower, third pool (Mamluk), is the biggest of the three at 177 m long and 86 m at its widest point. It is around 15 m deep and had the greatest capacity of around 113,000 cu m. Thus the total capacity of all three pools exceeded a quarter of a million cu m.  
Water was channelled from naturally occurring springs in the region to the pools by use of an aqueduct system which was more than 70 km long; the pools also served as reservoirs collecting rainwater. The pools provided the city of Jerusalem – which suffered constantly from drought – with water necessary for drinking, domestic use and for ablutions. Located on high ground, water from the pools flowed to Jerusalem by exploiting the inclined slopes and *wadi*s of the natural landscape. The canal and aqueduct system took a zigzag course running for the equivalent of double the geographical distance between Jerusalem and the pools – about 22 km.  
A mandate was issued by the Ottoman Sultanate for the protection and preservation of the water system which meant that the villages through which the system passed were responsible for its security. In AH 1027 / AD 1618 Sultan ‘Uthman II (Osman II, r. AH 1027–32 / AD 1618–22) constructed a fortified castle several meters to the north of the first pool.

These large water reservoirs located to the south of Bethlehem were named after Ottoman Sultan Sulayman the Magnificent who restored and developed them. Three large pools collected water and were connected to a complicated system of canals that channelled water from springs located tens of kilometres away. Canals transported the water from the pools to Jerusalem. The system was begun in the Roman period and was improved over the ages. A third pool was added in the Mamluk period. The improvement of the system to provide Jerusalem with water was considered a measure of the success of the ruling administration.
dates: The construction of the first and second pools dates to the second half of the 1st century BC. The third, lower pool was built between hegira 865–72 / AD 1461–7.
dynasty: The first and second pools date to the Roman period, the third dates to the Mamluk period.
artist: It is not known who sponsored the construction of the water system in the pre-Islamic period when the first and second pools were built. The third pool was commissioned by the Mamluk sultan, Khushqadam (r. AH 865–72 / AD 1461–7). Restoration and renovation of the pools and the aqueducts known as al-Qanat al-Sabil (the Aqueducts of the Sabil), were undertaken by the Mamluk Sultan al-Ashraf Qaytbay (r. AH 872–901 / AD 1468–96) and after him, Sultan Sulayman the Magnificent (r. AH 926–74 / AD 1520–66).
Documents in the archives of the Shari’a Court in Jerusalem cite the appointment of Murad al-Nasrani the Armenian, in the position of “Architect of the Aqueducts of the Sabil” in AH 970 / AD 1562.
keywords: Pool; canal; aqueduct; water

es.name: Albercas de Salomón
description:
Las albercas de Salomón son tres estanques dispuestos en cascada de los que salen varios canales. La primera mide 116 m de largo y unos 72 m de ancho; su profundidad oscila entre 6 y 12 m y tiene capacidad para 85.000 m³. La alberca central mide 129 m de largo y 76 m de ancho, tiene una profundidad de 12 m y capacidad para 90.000 m³. La tercera, del periodo mameluco, es la mayor, con 177 m de largo y 86 m en el punto más ancho. Tiene unos 15 m de profundidad y capacidad para 113.000 m³. La capacidad total de las tres albercas superaba los 250.000 m³.  
El agua se canalizaba desde los manantiales naturales de la zona mediante un sistema de acueductos de más de 70 km de largo, aunque las albercas también se usaban para recoger el agua de lluvia. La ciudad de Jerusalén sufría sequías constantes, así que estos depósitos suministraban el agua necesaria para consumo personal, doméstico y ritual. Su localización elevada permitía que el agua descendiese hasta la ciudad aprovechando la inclinación natural y los *wadi* del terreno. El sistema de canales y acueductos estaba en zigzag y medía unos 22 km, es decir, el doble de la distancia geográfica entre Jerusalén y las albercas.  
El sultanato otomano emitió una orden de protección y mantenimiento de este sistema de distribución agua, de tal manera que los pueblos por los que discurrían los canales eran responsables de su seguridad. En 1027 / 1618, el sultán Osman II (r. 1027-1032 / 1618-1622) construyó un alcázar unos metros al norte de la primera piscina.

Estos grandes depósitos de agua están al sur de Belén y llevan el nombre del sultán otomano Suleyman el Magnífico, que los restauró y amplió. Las tres albercas recogían agua y estaban conectadas a un complejo sistema de canales que llevaban agua de manantiales situados a decenas de kilómetros de distancia. El agua llegaba a Jerusalén por medio de canales. El sistema se construyó en la era romana y fue mejorándose con el tiempo. La tercera alberca se añadió en la época mameluca. El desarrollo del sistema de suministro de agua a Jerusalén fue una medida gubernamental muy exitosa.
dates: La primera y la segunda albercas se construyeron en la segunda mitad del siglo I a. C. La tercera, en 865-872 de la Hégira / 1461-1467 d. C.
dynasty: Las dos primeras datan de la época romana y la tercera de la época mameluca.
artist: Se desconoce quién patrocinó el sistema de recogida de agua en la época preislámica, cuando se construyeron las dos primeras albercas. La tercera se construyó por encargo del sultán mameluco Jushqadam (r. 865-872 / 1461-1467). El sultán mameluco al-Ashraf Qaytbay (r. 872-901 / 1468-1496) y el otomano Suleyman el Magnífico (r. 926-74/ 1520-66) fueron los responsables de la restauración y renovación de las albercas y del Qanat al-Sabil (acueductos del *sabil*).

En los documentos conservados en los archivos del Tribunal de la Sharia de Jerusalén se cita el nombramiento de Murad al-Nasrani (el Armenio) como “arquitecto de los acueductos del *sabil*” en 970 / 1562.
keywords: Piscina; canal; acueducto; agua.

fr.name: Piscines de Salomon.
description:
Les piscines de Salomon comprennent trois bassins en cascade d'où partent des canaux. Le premier mesure 116 m de long par environ 72 m de large pour une profondeur de 6 à 12 m et une capacité de 85 000 mètres cubes. Le deuxième, de 129 m de long, 76 m de large et 12 m de profondeur, offre une capacité d'environ 90 000 mètres cubes. Le troisième, d'époque mamelouke, est le plus vaste. Il mesure 177 m de long par 86 m dans sa plus grande largeur. Il est profond de 15 m et présente une capacité de 113 000 mètres cubes environ. La capacité totale du système dépasse les 250 000 mètres cubes.  
L'eau venait de sources naturelles grâce à un système d'aqueducs de plus de 70 km de long. Les bassins recueillaient également l'eau de pluie. Ils fournissaient à la ville de Jérusalem, qui souffrait toujours de la sécheresse, une alimentation pour les usages domestiques. De cette position élevée, l'eau s'écoulait vers la ville en exploitant les pentes naturelles et les lits de ruisseaux. Le système de canaux et d'aqueducs en zigzag mesurait environ 22 km, soit le double de la distance en ligne droite entre la ville et les piscines.  
Un édit du sultanat ottoman confia la sécurité de l'approvisionnement aux villages traversés par ce système. En 1027 H / 1618 J.-C., le sultan 'Othman II (Osman II, r. 1027-1032 H / 1618-1622 J.-C.) fit construire un château fortifié à quelques mètres au nord du premier bassin.

Ces grands réservoirs d’eau situés au sud de Bethléem doivent leur nom au sultan ottoman Soliman le Magnifique qui les restaura et les développa. Trois grands bassins récupéraient l’eau et étaient raccordés à un système complexe de canaux qui, à partir de sources situées à dix kilomètres de là, acheminaient l’eau jusqu’à Jérusalem. L’installation, commencée à la période romaine, fut améliorée à travers les âges. Un troisième bassin fut ajouté à la période mamelouke. Le perfectionnement du système pour approvisionner Jérusalem en eau fut considéré comme un témoignage du succès de l’administration dirigeante.
dates: La première et la deuxième piscines datent de la seconde moitié du Ier siècle av. J.-C. La troisième – le bassin inférieur – a été construite entre 865 et 872 de l'Hégire / 1461-1467 J.-C.
artist: Le nom du ou des commanditaires du système de distribution d'eau dans la période préislamique est inconnu. Le troisième bassin a été commandité par le sultan mamelouk Khuchqadam (r. 865-872 H / 1461-1467 J.-C.). Des restaurations et rénovations des bassins et des aqueducs du *sabil* (al-Qanat al-Sabil) ont été entreprises par le sultan mamelouk al-Achraf Qaytbay (r. 872-901 H / 1468-1496 J.-C.) et le sultan Soliman le Magnifique (r. 926-974 H / 1520-1566 J.-C.).
Des documents conservés au tribunal de la charia de Jérusalem mentionnent la nomination d'un dénommé Mourad al-Nasrani l'Arménien, “architecte des aqueducs du *sabil*” en 970 H / 1562 J.-C.
keywords: Piscines; canaux; aqueducs; eau

en.name: Mirror
description:
The mirror, which has a gilded wooden frame and ground-glass edges with flower and plant ornaments, is probably the work of one of the numerous glass workshops on the island of Murano, near Venice. Its form most probably suited the sophisticated taste of the European nobility. There are similar mirrors in many manors and museum collections today.  
Unfortunately, the original owner is unknown.  
Exhibited in the Baroque salon of the permanent collection of Varaždin’s Gothic-Renaissance castle, the mirror, together with other items of the collection, present the visitor with the most representative trends and refined atmosphere of the Baroque period in Varaždin.

The mirror, which has a gilded wooden frame and ground-glass edges with flower and plant ornaments, is probably the work of one of the numerous glass workshops on the island of Murano, near Venice. It is representative of the trends and refined atmosphere of the Baroque period in Varaždin.
keywords: Furnishing; glass; floral decoration; gilding; wood carving

en.name: Istanbul water pipeline map
short_description: During the 19th century, new technologies radically transformed both travel and communications. The Cendere Hamidian Water Pump Station was built by Abdülhamid II in 1902. The station is located at an altitude of 34 metres above sea level. With its function, architectural design and mechanical equipment, the station is a unique reminder of Ottoman architecture. It pumped to Balmumcu and Beşiktaş – with water coming from 20 different pipes in Kağıthane, propelled by steam pump machines.
holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph; History of Water in Ottoman Empire; Water; map
partner: Ministry of Culture and Tourism (General Directorate for Cultural Heritage and Museums)

en.name: Monastery of St. George – Rajchica
short_description: The Monastery in v. Rajchica near Debar is one of the most outstanding 19th-century monasteries in the Republic of Macedonia. The Monastery Church is dedicated to St. George Victorious. It is a model of sacral structure distinctive of the 19th century local construction masters from the Reka Area. The church is a combination of inscribed cross and single-nave structure with three domes. Part of the holy remains of St. George the Victorious – that is, his hand – is kept in the monastery. For many years now the monastery has been serving as a nunnery and nuns have been creating and embroidering robes for church dignitaries in Macedonia and elsewhere.
artist: Local construction masters. Frescoes painted by icon painter Mihail, monk Daniel and their student Dicho Zograph
history: The Church was built in 1835. Upper zones of its frescoes were painted in the span of 1840–1852 by icon-painter Mihail and priest Danail. Lower zones were completed by their disciple, the renowned icon-painter Dicho Zograph from v. Tresonche near Debar, one of the most outstanding Macedonian icon painters.
keywords: iconostasis; frescoes; icons

en.name: Calligraphy
description:
Considered one of the masterpieces of Ottoman classical literature, *Su Kasidesi* (*Water Ode*) is Fuzûlî’s celebrated ode (*kaside*) written in praise of the Prophet Muhammad. The poem employs water (*su*) as its central metaphor, intertwining themes of purity, life, longing and spiritual elevation. Throughout the *kaside*, water appears as an entity filled with devotion—flowing, bowing, crying, evaporating and kneeling—mirroring the poet’s own yearning for the divine.  
  
Fuzûlî’s intricate wordplay transforms water into a symbol of both physical and spiritual life, reflecting the Islamic belief that all creation originates from water. By personifying water as an admirer of the Prophet, the poem situates natural elements within an emotional and devotional universe.  
The musical rhythm of the *aruz* metre, the repetition of sound patterns and the carefully layered imagery create an atmosphere of reverence. The poem’s rhetorical brilliance lies in its fusion of mystical Sufi thought, high literary artistry and deep emotional sincerity.  
  
*Su Kasidesi* continues to be celebrated as one of the finest examples of Ottoman poetic expression, demonstrating Fuzûlî’s mastery in blending spirituality, metaphysics and lyrical beauty.
holder: İstanbul Su Müzesi / Istanbul Water Museum
keywords: Poem; Calligraphy; water; spirituality

en.name: Tunisia at the 1889 Paris World Fair
short_description: The industrial developments of the 19th century also brought about the birth of world fair, which, as well as offering accounts and images of abroad, presented Europeans with the opportunity for virtual, effortless travel.

fr.name: La Tunisie à l’exposition universelle de 1889 à Paris
short_description: Le XIXe siècle industriel inventa les expositions universelles qui, outre la littérature et les images de voyage, offrirent aux Européens le voyage immobile.

ar.name: زبدية.
description: زبدية كبيرة ملونة تحت التزجيج على قاعدة عالية مزينة من الخارج بأزهار وأوراق بدرجات الأزرق والأخضر تتعرج بحرية على السطح. وفي مركز الأزهار الأكبر حجماً هناك نموذج زخرفي على شكل شريط متموج، ويزين القاعدة نماذج زهرية وورقية مشابهة إلا أنها أكثر تنظيماً، وفي الأسفل هناك شريط رفيع من الإطارات الزخرفية التي يحتوي كل منها على أربع وريقات. يدل الحجم المميز لهذه الزبدية، والمهارة التي تم تنفيذ الزخارف بها أنها قد أنتجت للطبقات العليا في البلاط العثماني رغم عدم وجود ما يؤكد ذلك.

وعاء كبير، ذو قاعدة مرتفعة، مُزخرف بأوراق شجر كبيرة، وأزهار، باللونين الأزرق والأخضر. يدلُّ حجم ونوعية هذا الوعاء، على أنه قد صُنع خصيصاً لشخص عثماني رفيع المرتبة، واستُخدم لغسل القدمين، أثناء الوضوء.
keywords: زخرفة زهرية؛ ماء.

en.name: Bowl.
description: A large bowl on a high foot, decorated with underglaze painting. On the exterior, flowers and leaves in shades of blue and sage-green meander with relative freedom about the surface. The largest flowers feature a distinct cloud-band motif at their centre. Similar flower and leaf motifs, more regularly organised, adorn the foot, at whose base is a thin band of repeating cartouches containing four leaves each. The extraordinary size of this bowl, as well as the skill with which it is decorated, suggests production for the highest levels of the Ottoman hierarchy, although direct evidence for this is lacking.

A very large footed bowl on a high foot, decorated with large leaves and flowers in blue and sage-green. The size and quality of this bowl suggests that it was made for a high-ranking Ottoman official, possibly for washing the feet during ablutions.
keywords: floral decoration; water; inlay

es.name: Cuenco
description: Cuenco de gran tamaño, con pie alto y decoración pintada bajo vidriado. En la superficie exterior serpentean, dibujadas con trazos relativamente libres, flores y hojas en tonos azules y verde salvia. Las flores de mayor tamaño presentan en el centro un distintivo motivo de nubes. El pie está decorado con parecidos motivos de hojas y flores, y en su parte inferior corre una estrecha banda de cartuchos con cuatro hojas cada uno. Aunque no existen pruebas directas, la destreza con que está decorado este cuenco y su gran tamaño sugieren que se hizo para alguien perteneciente a la más alta jerarquía otomana.

Enorme cuenco con pie alto y decoración de grandes hojas y flores en verde salvia y azul. El tamaño y la calidad de esta pieza sugieren que se hizo para un alto cargo otomano, que posiblemente lo utilizaría para lavarse los pies en las abluciones.
keywords: decoración floral; agua

fr.name: Coupe.
description: Grande coupe sur piédouche à décor peint sous glaçure. Côté extérieur, des fleurs et des feuilles de diverses nuances de bleu et de vert-sauge se répartissent sur toute la surface dans une certaine liberté. La corolle des fleurs les plus importantes comporte un motif de ruban de nuages clairement visible. Des fleurs et des feuillages similaires, mais disposés plus régulièrement, décorent le pied à la base duquel court un mince bandeau de cartouches répétés contenant chacun quatre feuilles. Les dimensions extraordinaires de cette coupe, ainsi que le savoir-faire dont témoigne son décor, suggèrent qu'elle a été produite pour un représentant des plus hauts niveaux de la hiérarchie ottomane, bien que l'on n'en détienne pas la preuve.

Grande coupe sur haut piédouche, ornée de grandes feuilles et fleurs en bleu et vert sauge. La taille et la qualité de cette coupe suggèrent qu'elle a été fabriquée pour un dignitaire ottoman de haut rang, peut-être pour le lavement de pieds au cours des ablutions.
keywords: Décoration florale ; eau

en.name: *The Encyclopaedia of Islam*, edited by M. Th. Houtsma (and others)
short_description: The first of four volumes of the *Encyclopaedia of Islam*, a dictionary of the georgraphy, ethnography and biography of the Muhammadan peoples by Th. Houtsma and others. It was published by Brill in Leiden and Lyuzac in London. It contains the ex libris of Antonis Benakis.

ar.name: ضلع خشبي مذهب.
description: القطعة هي واحدة من مجموعة من القطع الخشبية المطلية بالجص والمزخرفة بالحفر بزخارف نباتية وهندسية وكتابية مطلية بماء الذهب وبالألوان الأزرق والأحمر والأخضر والأبيض على خلفيات من ألوان مختلفة خاصة من اللون الأسود. والقطع جزء من زخارف القبة الداخلية للمسجد الأقصى التي استبدلت الأجزاء التالفة منها عام 1938 بعد أن تعرضت للتلف التدريجي بفعل الرطوبة وتسرب المياه. وترجع أهمية هذه القطع إلى كونها الشاهد الوحيد تقريباً على ترميم قبة المسجد الأقصى في العصر الفاطمي زمن الخليفة الظاهر بأمر الله (حكم في الفترة 411 - 427 / 1021 - 1036). ويذكر أن الأجزاء الأخرى المشابهة قد ضاعت نتيجة الحريق المتعمد الذي نشب في المسجد عام 1969 والذي أدى إلى تدمير غالبية أجزاء القبة الخشبية بالإضافة إلى أجزاء أخرى من المسجد الأقصى. كانت القباب تتكون في العادة من قبة داخلية وأخرى خارجية. وتتكون القبة الداخلية من هيكل خشبي يصفّح من الداخل بألواح خشبية مدوّرة. وتثبت ألياف النخيل على الألواح الخشبية باستعمال مسامير خشبية، ثم تغطى الألياف بطبقة جصيّة بسمك عدة سنتمترات. وبعدها يتم حفر الجص باستعمال أدوات الحفر والنحت على الجص لتشكيل الزخارف المطلوبة التي تلوّن بألوان مختلفة. أما القبة الخارجية فتتكون من هيكل خشبي يصفح من الخارج بصفائح معدنية تصنع على الأغلب من الرصاص كما هو الحال في قبة المسجد الأقصى اليوم، وتصنع أحياناً من النحاس كما هو الحال في قبة الصخرة اليوم. ولا تختلف قبة المسجد الأقصى عن قبة الصخرة من حيث تقنيات الصنع.

ضلع خشبي من القبة الداخلية للمسجد الأقصى، مُزيَّن بزخارف نباتية وهندسية وكتابية، مطلية بماء الذهب، وملوَّن على خلفية ملونة. هذا الضلع الشاهد الوحيد تقريباً على ترميم قبة المسجد الأقصى في العصر الفاطمي، زمن الخليفة الظاهر، في حين ضاعت الشواهد الأخرى نتيجة الحريق المُتعمَّد الذي نشب في المسجد عام 1969م.
dates: على الأغلب أن القطعة تعود إلى فترة الترميم الفاطمي للمسجد الأقصى، وذلك حوالي عام 424 / 1033.
